item.title: East Bay Date-night Neighborhoods
item.description: Solano Avenue packs more than 200 mostly independent shops and restaurants into one walkable mile, no reservation and no moving the car. Most people cross
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Date-night Neighborhoods

Solano Avenue packs more than 200 mostly independent shops and restaurants into one walkable mile, no reservation and no moving the car. Most people cross the bridge for date night and miss eight corridors exactly like it. Eight East Bay date-night corridors.

Rockridge / College Avenue — College Ave commercial district, Rockridge, Oakland CA 94618. A long walkable run of wine bars, dinner spots, and dessert, all without moving the car. @rockridgeoakland.

Solano Avenue — Solano Ave commercial district, Albany and Berkeley CA. One mile and over 200 mostly independent shops and restaurants, lower-key than Rockridge and easy to wander without a reservation. @onsolanoavenue.

Lakeshore / Grand Avenue — Lakeshore Ave district near Lake Merritt, Oakland CA. Walk the lake before dinner and after, with the downtown skyline lit across the water at night. @lakeshoreaveoak.

Park Boulevard / Glenview — Park Blvd commercial corridor, Glenview, Oakland CA 94602. The quiet one, a small-town main street of around 22 locally owned spots two miles east of Lake Merritt.

Piedmont Avenue — Piedmont Ave commercial district, Oakland CA 94611. An old-school date strip whose merchants association goes back to 1939, with dinner and dessert stacked into a few walkable blocks. @piedmontavenue_oakland.

Downtown Walnut Creek — Downtown commercial district, Walnut Creek CA. The 680 answer when you would rather skip the drive into Oakland, with theaters, hundreds of restaurants and shops, and a full evening on this side of the bridge. @walnutcreekdowntown.

Downtown Lafayette — Mt. Diablo Blvd corridor, Lafayette CA. Smaller than Walnut Creek, with a Restaurant Row of nearly 40 eateries and a more local, lower-key feel. @lafayettechamber_ca.

Downtown Pleasanton — Main Street district, Pleasanton CA. Tree-lined old-town Main Street with historic buildings, fine dining, and easy parking, no bridge traffic to get there. @pleasantondt.

Eight East Bay date-night corridors: Rockridge, Solano, Lakeshore, Park Boulevard, Piedmont, Walnut Creek, Lafayette, Pleasanton. Which is your go-to when you want to park once and walk the whole night?

item.title: East Bay Road Trips / Weekend Escapes
item.description: Highway 1 through Big Sur reopened in January 2026, open again for the summer after a long stretch of closures. Good reason to refresh the weekend escape l
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Road Trips / Weekend Escapes

Highway 1 through Big Sur reopened in January 2026, open again for the summer after a long stretch of closures. Good reason to refresh the weekend escape list most East Bay people run on autopilot. Every trip here leaves room to go Friday night and be back for work Monday. Seven of them, closest first.

Healdsburg and Sonoma, Sonoma County — Wine country at gentler prices than Napa, with a walkable plaza in each town. About an hour to ninety minutes north. Best for a slow couple's weekend.

Carmel and Monterey, Monterey County — The aquarium on Cannery Row, 17-Mile Drive, and Carmel-by-the-Sea's storybook downtown in one trip. About two hours south.

Pinnacles National Park, San Benito County — California's newest national park, named in 2013. Condors overhead, talus caves you can walk through when they are open, and far thinner crowds than Yosemite. About two hours south.

Big Sur, Central Coast — Highway 1 reopened in January 2026 after slide repairs, so Bixby Bridge, McWay Falls, and the Henry Miller Library are back on the route. A one-way signal at Rocky Creek Bridge runs through the summer, so expect a short wait. About three hours south.

Mendocino, Mendocino County — A Victorian village on the headlands, three hours north via 101 and 128, not the six-hour coast crawl on Highway 1. Bluff trails, redwoods inland, and a downtown that has barely changed in decades.

Lake Tahoe, Sierra Nevada — North Shore for quiet coves and trails, South Shore for the busier scene and casinos over the Nevada line. Both fit a weekend. About three and a half to four hours east.

Yosemite Valley, Mariposa County — No timed-entry reservation for summer 2026, but valley parking fills by mid-morning on busy days, so go early. Camp in spring, lodge in winter, day-trip if you must. About four hours southeast.

The full list, closest first: Healdsburg and Sonoma, Carmel and Monterey, Pinnacles, Big Sur, Mendocino, Lake Tahoe, Yosemite Valley. Which one has been sitting on your someday list the longest?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Sunset Views + Lookouts
item.description: On a clear winter day, the view from Mount Diablo's summit spans over 8,500 square miles, parts of 40 California counties in a single look. Most people dri
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sunset Views + Lookouts

On a clear winter day, the view from Mount Diablo's summit spans over 8,500 square miles, parts of 40 California counties in a single look. Most people drive the same East Bay ridge roads every week and never once pull over. These are the lookouts worth stopping the car for. Eight of them.

Grizzly Peak Blvd overlooks — Pull-outs along Grizzly Peak Blvd, Berkeley. The San Francisco skyline that ruins postcards: golden at sunset, eerie when the fog pours over the ridge, razor sharp on a clear winter morning. Open 24 hours, free, park along the road.

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. A flat, windswept hilltop loop out on the bay: the Golden Gate, the Bay Bridge, and the city skyline in one slow sweep. Kite fliers own the afternoons. Open 6am to 10pm.

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. Paved, level, stroller friendly along Nimitz Way. The surprise is the view east toward Briones and the reservoirs; most people only ever turn west toward the Bay. @ebrpd

Mount Diablo summit — Summit Rd, Mt Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. At 3,849 feet, the highest peak in the East Bay. On the clearest days the view reaches the Sierra crest, and Lassen Peak, 181 miles north, lifts over the curve of the earth. Summit center open daily 10 to 4.

Sibley Volcanic Regional Preserve — 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. Round Top is a 10-million-year-old volcano turned on its side; you walk the ridge with the Bay to the west, Mount Diablo to the east, and the geology right under your boots. Open 5am to 10pm.

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. At 1,905 feet, the highest point in Tilden and the Berkeley hills. The reward for the climb up Wildcat Canyon Road, and empty most weekday evenings.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3450 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. Redwood groves up top, and ridge openings that drop your eye down to the city, out across the Bay, and all the way to the Golden Gate. Less famous than Grizzly, just as good. Open dawn to dusk.

Albany Bulb — West end of Buchanan St, Albany. An old landfill peninsula that became an unofficial sculpture park, dog run, and shoreline lookout, jutting straight out toward the Golden Gate. Free, open, and unlike anywhere else on the bay.

Eight East Bay lookouts: Grizzly Peak, Cesar Chavez Park, Inspiration Point, Mount Diablo summit, Sibley, Vollmer Peak, Joaquin Miller, Albany Bulb. Which one do you send people to when they want the view without the crowd?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Sunrise Hikes
item.description: Everyone sets the alarm for Mission Peak. The quieter East Bay climbs hand you the same Bay-wide payoff with a fraction of the crowd, and one is a flat wal
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sunrise Hikes

Everyone sets the alarm for Mission Peak. The quieter East Bay climbs hand you the same Bay-wide payoff with a fraction of the crowd, and one is a flat walk that opens at 5am. Worth the early wake-up, from Diablo's 3,849-foot summit on down. Seven sunrise hikes.

Mission Peak — Stanford Avenue staging area, Fremont. About three miles up and over two thousand feet of climb, with the whole South Bay spread out below at first light. The lot holds 43 cars and opens at 6:30am, so it fills fast.

Mount Diablo summit — Mount Diablo State Park, near Walnut Creek. At 3,849 feet it is the highest point in the East Bay. Drive most of the way, then walk the short summit loop for a view that reaches the Sierra on a clear day.

Wildcat Peak — Tilden Nature Area, Berkeley. A shorter, less crowded climb than Mission Peak with the same Bay-wide payoff at sunrise. A circular stone lookout, built by Rotary in the early 1960s, sits at the top.

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. At 1,905 feet it is the highest point in the Berkeley Hills, yet the climb from the nearby lot runs about twenty minutes. The sunrise view most Cal students never find.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan Street, Albany. A flat ten-minute walk to the water, with the Golden Gate Bridge and the San Francisco skyline across the Bay at first light. It opens at 5am, earlier than any peak on this list. The sunrise walk for people who do not want to hike.

Round Top — Sibley Volcanic Regional Preserve, Oakland. A volcanic ridge above the Caldecott Tunnel where sunrise lights the Bay from east to west. The rock under your boots came from a volcano dated at roughly 10 million years old.

Nimitz Way — Inspiration Point, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. A paved ridgetop path, stroller and leashed-dog friendly, with quick access to wide views of the Bay, San Pablo Reservoir, and Mount Diablo. The sunrise route that does not punish you.

Seven East Bay sunrise climbs: Mission Peak, Mount Diablo, Wildcat Peak, Vollmer Peak, Albany Bulb, Round Top at Sibley, and Nimitz Way at Inspiration Point. Which one earns the early alarm for you, the highest summit or the flat walk to the water?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Weekend Escape Towns
item.description: Carmel sits just under two hours from the East Bay and Sausalito barely forty minutes, no airport and no overnight bag. Leave after Friday dinner, be home
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Weekend Escape Towns

Carmel sits just under two hours from the East Bay and Sausalito barely forty minutes, no airport and no overnight bag. Leave after Friday dinner, be home by Sunday coffee. Eleven weekend escape towns within about two hours.

Sausalito, Marin County — A waterfront town of houseboats and bayfront patios, with ferry deck views back across to the city. About 40 minutes out.

Napa Valley, Napa County — Wineries and tasting rooms plus a walkable downtown along the river, close enough to enjoy without staying over. About an hour out.

Santa Cruz, Santa Cruz County — The Beach Boardwalk keeps free admission and runs year round right on the sand. About 90 minutes out.

Bodega Bay, Sonoma County — A working fishing harbor on Highway 1 with fresh Dungeness crab, coastal trails, and the town Hitchcock filmed for The Birds. About 90 minutes out.

Tomales Bay, Marin County — Shoreline oyster farms like Hog Island, plus flat water kayaking and quiet views the whole length of the bay. About 90 minutes out.

Healdsburg, Sonoma County — A town plaza ringed by tasting rooms and restaurants, with the Russian River just a few minutes away. About 90 minutes out.

Monterey, Monterey County — Home of the Monterey Bay Aquarium and Cannery Row, with sea lions barking off Fisherman's Wharf. About two hours out.

Carmel-by-the-Sea, Monterey County — A storybook village of art galleries and hidden courtyards above a white sand beach, just off Highway 1. Just under two hours out.

Pinnacles National Park, San Benito County — Jagged rock spires and cave trails, plus some of the best odds in California of spotting a wild condor overhead. About two hours out.

Guerneville, Sonoma County — A Russian River resort town tucked under the redwoods, with river beaches, summer canoe runs, and Armstrong Redwoods State Reserve next door.

Sebastopol, Sonoma County — Gravenstein apple country turned arts town, with the Barlow market district, antique warehouses, and Mom's Apple Pie on the way in.

Eleven escapes within about two hours: Sausalito, Napa Valley, Santa Cruz, Bodega Bay, Tomales Bay, Healdsburg, Monterey, Carmel, Pinnacles, plus Guerneville and Sebastopol. Which one are you leaving for first?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Date-night Plays
item.description: Chabot opens its historic telescopes to the public free every Friday and Saturday night, 1,500 feet above the Bay. Hardly anyone plans a date around it. Mo
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Date-night Plays

Chabot opens its historic telescopes to the public free every Friday and Saturday night, 1,500 feet above the Bay. Hardly anyone plans a date around it. Most couples just rerun the same dinner reservation. Here are the East Bay date nights actually worth calling the sitter for. Seven of them.

Sunset hike at Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Orinda, CA 94563 (Tilden Regional Park). The paved Nimitz Way stays nearly level while the Golden Gate, both bays, and the reservoirs open up on either side. Bring a thermos and time it for golden hour. @ebrpd

First Friday art walk — Telegraph Ave, 22nd to 27th St, KONO District, Oakland, CA. Galleries stay open and the street fills with music, makers, and food on the first Friday of every month, 5 to 9pm. The city's most underrated standing date. @oakfirstfridays.

Live jazz at Yoshi's — 510 Embarcadero W, Oakland, CA 94607. A serious jazz room and a full Japanese restaurant under one roof at Jack London Square, booking touring acts since 1972. Dinner and the show without moving the car. @yoshis_oak.

Bouldering at Berkeley Ironworks — 800 Potter St, Berkeley, CA 94710. Even if neither of you climbs, an hour on the boulder wall beats another bar. Watching is fun, falling is funnier, and it stays open to 10pm on weeknights. @berkeleyironworks.

Dance night at Ashkenaz — 1317 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702. A worn wooden floor and live world music since 1973, with a beginner dance lesson often built in before the band starts. Zero experience required. @ashkenazberkeley.

Tiki cocktails at Forbidden Island — 1304 Lincoln Ave, Alameda, CA 94501. A dim, fully themed tiki lounge pouring proper rum drinks since 2006, open to midnight. The kind of room that turns a Tuesday into a trip. @forbiddenisland.

Stargazing at Chabot Space and Science Center — 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland, CA 94619. Free telescope viewing on the observatory deck every Friday and Saturday, 7:30 to 10:30pm, weather permitting, through refractors from 1883 and 1916. The night sky does the talking. @chabotspace.

Seven East Bay date nights worth the sitter: Inspiration Point at sunset, Oakland First Fridays, jazz at Yoshi's, bouldering at Ironworks, a dance floor at Ashkenaz, tiki at Forbidden Island, telescopes at Chabot. Which one are you booking first?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Farmers Markets
item.description: The Ecology Center opened Berkeley's farmers market in 1987, and it was the first in the country to ban plastic bags. Most people run the same supermarket
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Farmers Markets

The Ecology Center opened Berkeley's farmers market in 1987, and it was the first in the country to ban plastic bags. Most people run the same supermarket loop all week and never learn which East Bay market the chefs actually shop, or which morning gets you there before the best stalls sell out. Six worth the early alarm.

Berkeley Saturday Farmers Market — Center St at Martin Luther King Jr Way, Berkeley. Saturdays 10 to 3, run by the Ecology Center since 1987, one of the first certified farmers markets in California.

Grand Lake Farmers Market — Grand Ave at Lake Park Ave, Oakland. Saturdays 9 to 2 year-round at Splash Pad Park, the biggest market on the Lake Merritt side.

Temescal Farmers Market — 5300 Claremont Ave, Oakland. Sundays in the DMV lot, a chef-favorite market with a tight, high-quality grower list.

Old Oakland Farmers Market — 9th St at Broadway, Oakland. Fridays downtown since 1989, heavy on produce and prepared food for the lunch crowd.

Jack London Square Farmers Market — Water St at Broadway, Oakland. Sundays on the waterfront, produce plus crafts with the estuary as the backdrop.

Montclair Farmers Market — Mountain Blvd, Oakland. Sundays in Montclair Village, a smaller hills market where the regulars know the growers.

Six worth the early alarm: Berkeley Saturday, Grand Lake, Temescal, Old Oakland, Jack London Square, and Montclair. Which market gets your Saturday?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay BikeTrails
item.description: The Iron Horse Trail runs 32 paved miles from Concord to Pleasanton on an old rail line, most of it without a single traffic crossing. Plenty of East Bay r
item.content:encoded:
East Bay BikeTrails

The Iron Horse Trail runs 32 paved miles from Concord to Pleasanton on an old rail line, most of it without a single traffic crossing. Plenty of East Bay riders still load the bike in the car to go ride somewhere else. Eight trails on this side worth staying for.

Iron Horse Regional Trail — Concord to Pleasanton, about 32 miles, Contra Costa and Alameda. The old Southern Pacific line, now flat, fast, paved, and running through five downtowns. The Amador Valley to Kimball Ave segment is closed through July 31, 2026 for maintenance. @ebrpd

Lafayette-Moraga Regional Trail — Olympic Blvd staging, Lafayette to Valle Vista, Moraga. Eight paved miles through a suburban canyon, oak shade, old train trestles, an easy gradient the whole way. The morning loop cyclists keep on rotation.

Bay Trail, Oakland and Alameda waterfront — The Oakland Estuary on one side, container cranes on the other. A flat, clear path with the best surprise scenery on this list: a working port on your left, open water on your right.

Nimitz Way — Inspiration Point staging, Wildcat Canyon Rd, Orinda, in Tilden Regional Park. A paved ridge route past Wildcat Peak with the Bay on one side and Briones Reservoir on the other. The view-per-mile leader.

Briones Crest loop — Bear Creek staging, Briones Regional Park, Lafayette. Fire roads through open grassland with climbs that earn their descents. The training ride for anyone working up to Mount Diablo.

Cull Canyon to Don Castro — Cull Canyon Rec Area, 18825 Cull Canyon Rd, to Don Castro, Castro Valley. A reservoir-to-reservoir local route on quiet roads, with water views and a lunch stop in between.

Pleasanton Ridge Regional Park — 9895 Foothill Rd, Pleasanton. Singletrack with views of Mount Diablo and the Livermore Valley. The technical option for riders who want to be worked.

Crockett Hills Regional Park — Crockett. Quiet trails most East Bay cyclists never explore, climbing from town to ridgelines over the Carquinez Strait.

Eight East Bay rides: Iron Horse, Lafayette-Moraga, the Oakland-Alameda Bay Trail, Nimitz Way, Briones Crest, Cull Canyon to Don Castro, Pleasanton Ridge, and Crockett Hills. Which one is your standing weekend loop?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Hiking, Kid-friendly Under 3 Miles
item.description: Half a mile from a parking lot in the Oakland hills, the Stream Trail runs straight into towering coastal redwoods. Most East Bay parents cross a bridge to
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Hiking, Kid-friendly Under 3 Miles

Half a mile from a parking lot in the Oakland hills, the Stream Trail runs straight into towering coastal redwoods. Most East Bay parents cross a bridge to Muir Woods for the same kind of trees and a longer line. Eight kid-friendly hikes under three miles.

Lake Anza loop — Lake Anza Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. About 1.4 miles around the swim lake, past blackberry bushes and the little steam-train station. The Saturday-morning win. @ebrpd

Sequoia Bayview Trail — Joaquin Miller Park, 3540 Sanborn Dr, Oakland. A two-mile redwood loop with small streams and wooden bridges the kids like to count. The shaded pick for a hot day.

Indian Joe Creek Trail — Sunol Regional Wilderness, 1895 Geary Rd, Sunol. Two miles along a year-round creek with stepping stones, butterflies, and mossy rocks. The trail is open; Shady Glen is closed.

Stream Trail — Canyon Meadow staging, 7867 Redwood Rd, Oakland, in Redwood Regional Park. About 1.5 flat miles along the canyon floor through towering coastal redwoods, half a mile from the car.

Wildcat Creek Trail to Jewel Lake — Tilden Nature Area, end of Central Park Dr, Berkeley. A 1.7-mile flat boardwalk loop, heavy on birds, easy for strollers and short legs. The all-ages morning.

Round Top Loop — Sibley Volcanic Preserve, 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. Two miles around an extinct volcano, with stone labyrinths to find along the way and a real summit feel.

Bear Creek Trail — Bear Creek staging, 1611 Bear Creek Rd, Briones Regional Park, Lafayette. About 1.8 miles through cattle pasture, spring wildflowers, rolling green hills, and distant Mount Diablo.

Rotary Peace Grove — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. A one-mile interpretive loop through redwoods donated by Rotary clubs from around the world. Short, quiet, easy to fold into a Tilden morning.

Eight under three miles: Lake Anza, Sequoia Bayview, Indian Joe Creek, Stream Trail, Wildcat Creek to Jewel Lake, Round Top, Bear Creek, and Rotary Peace Grove. Which one did your kids actually finish?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Hiking, Worth Crossing the Bay for
item.description: The pole at the summit of Mission Peak is the most photographed spot in Alameda County, and the climb to it built East Bay hiking culture. These are the tr
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Hiking, Worth Crossing the Bay for

The pole at the summit of Mission Peak is the most photographed spot in Alameda County, and the climb to it built East Bay hiking culture. These are the trails worth crossing a bridge for, the ones Marin does not have. Eight of them.

Mission Peak — Stanford Ave staging, 43600 Mission Blvd, Fremont. A roughly five-mile round trip to a 2,517-foot summit, and the pole at the top half of Alameda County has a photo with. @ebrpd

Mount Diablo via Mitchell Canyon — 96 Mitchell Canyon Rd, Clayton, in Mount Diablo State Park. The signature East Bay climb. On the clearest days the summit view reaches the Sierra crest. The seven-county look earns the work.

Sunol Regional Wilderness — 1895 Geary Rd, Sunol. A four-mile loop through grassland to a granite gorge the district itself calls Little Yosemite. The hidden canyon most Bay Area hikers never make the drive for.

Briones Crest Loop — Bear Creek staging, Briones Regional Park, Lafayette. About six miles of rolling green hills over three summits, with cattle, wildflowers, and Mount Diablo in the distance. The all-day workout.

Las Trampas Rocky Ridge — 18012 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. A steep climb to a 2,000-foot ridge with the Bay to the west and the Central Valley to the east. The hard East Bay hike most people overlook.

Black Diamond Mines Regional Preserve — 5175 Somersville Rd, Antioch. Old coal-mining trails through some of the East Bay's strangest terrain, past Rose Hill Cemetery and abandoned mine shafts.

Pleasanton Ridge — Augustin Bernal staging, 8200 Golden Eagle Way, Pleasanton. Miles of ridge trail with olive groves, circling hawks, and the South Bay laid out below. The longest unobstructed views around.

Coyote Hills Regional Park — 8000 Patterson Ranch Rd, Fremont. The marsh-and-grassland combo hikers skip for the bigger names, with Ohlone shellmounds and sunset over the Bay.

Eight worth the drive: Mission Peak, Mount Diablo via Mitchell Canyon, Sunol, Briones Crest, Las Trampas, Black Diamond Mines, Pleasanton Ridge, and Coyote Hills. Which one finally sold you on this side of the Bay?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Kids, Parks with Playgrounds
item.description: Tilden packs a Little Farm, a steam train, and an antique merry-go-round into one park. That's how it eats a whole Saturday without a single screen. It is
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Kids, Parks with Playgrounds

Tilden packs a Little Farm, a steam train, and an antique merry-go-round into one park. That's how it eats a whole Saturday without a single screen. It is not the only East Bay park that pulls that off. Eight with playgrounds worth the morning.

Tilden Regional Park — Berkeley, off Grizzly Peak Blvd and Wildcat Canyon Rd. The Little Farm with goats and sheep, the steam train, and the merry-go-round. Generations of East Bay kids grew up here. Plan four hours. @ebrpd

Lakeside Park at Lake Merritt — Bellevue Ave, Oakland. Playgrounds, a duck pond, the Necklace of Lights, and Children's Fairyland right next door. A whole Saturday inside one ZIP code.

Crown Memorial State Beach — 8th St and Otis Dr, Alameda. A playground right next to the sand, the San Francisco skyline across the water, and a Bird Sanctuary trail at the south end. Bring sunscreen.

Heather Farm Park — 301 N San Carlos Dr, Walnut Creek. Two big playgrounds, a duck pond, and a community garden across 100 acres. The go-to for the 680 corridor.

Civic Park — 1375 Civic Dr, Walnut Creek. A downtown park with a creek, a playground, and the library right next door. The walkable family afternoon.

Quarry Lakes Regional Recreation Area — 2100 Isherwood Way, Fremont. Two lakes, two playgrounds, and a summer swim beach. The closest thing to a lake day with no real drive.

Roberts Regional Recreation Area — 10570 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. A playground set inside an old-growth redwood grove, with picnic tables that fit the whole birthday party.

Hap Magee Ranch Park — Danville. A playground plus farm animals, goats, sheep, and chickens. The hidden one most East Bay parents miss.

Eight for the kids: Tilden, Lakeside at Lake Merritt, Crown Beach, Heather Farm, Civic Park, Quarry Lakes, Roberts, and Hap Magee Ranch. Which one runs your crew down the fastest?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Running Routes
item.description: The paved loop around Lake Merritt is the most-run path in the East Bay, flat and lit the whole 3.1 miles around the water. Locals keep a rotation going so
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Running Routes

The paved loop around Lake Merritt is the most-run path in the East Bay, flat and lit the whole 3.1 miles around the water. Locals keep a rotation going so they never Google where to run again. Ten loops worth adding to yours.

Lafayette Reservoir loop — 3849 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A 2.7-mile paved loop around the water. You pay to park, but the rolling terrain and the views earn it. The 680 corridor's morning anthem.

Lake Merritt loop — Around Lake Merritt, Oakland. The 3.1-mile shoreline path, flat and lit and water-adjacent the whole way. The most-run route in the East Bay for a reason.

Iron Horse Trail — Concord to Pleasanton, Contra Costa and Alameda. Flat, paved, no traffic crossings for miles. That's why East Bay marathoners build their base here. Amador Valley to Kimball Ave closed through July 31, 2026. @ebrpd

Heather Farm Park loop — 301 N San Carlos Dr, Walnut Creek. About 1.5 miles of trails inside 100 acres, hills if you want them and flat if you do not. The training-wheels route.

Tilden Park — Lake Anza area, 2501 Grizzly Peak Blvd, Berkeley. About 3.5 miles with one honest climb, eucalyptus shade, and the lake waiting at the turnaround. Berkeley's signature trail run.

Bay Trail at the Berkeley Marina — Berkeley Marina shoreline. A four-mile out and back along the water, the Bay Bridge in front of you and the kite field at the turnaround. The flat scenic option.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3450 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. About 3.5 miles through the redwood grove, trail running with redwood air. The shaded summer rotation.

Briones Regional Park, Bear Creek loop — Bear Creek staging, Lafayette. About four miles of rolling fire roads through cattle pasture. The hill workout most road runners never try.

San Pablo Bay Trail — Bay Front Park, end of Tennent Ave, Hercules. A flat waterfront stretch with wide-open Bay views and almost no crossings.

Lake Chabot — 17600 Lake Chabot Rd, Castro Valley. Rolling shoreline fire trails around the reservoir, as long a run as you want.

Ten on rotation: Lafayette Reservoir, Lake Merritt, Iron Horse, Heather Farm, Tilden, the Berkeley Marina Bay Trail, Joaquin Miller, Briones, plus the Hercules Bay Trail and Lake Chabot from your comments. Which loop is your default?

item.title: East Bay NatureCenters
item.description: Children's Fairyland opened on the shore of Lake Merritt in 1950, and Walt Disney walked through it for ideas before Disneyland existed. It is one of eight
item.content:encoded:
East Bay NatureCenters

Children's Fairyland opened on the shore of Lake Merritt in 1950, and Walt Disney walked through it for ideas before Disneyland existed. It is one of eight East Bay spots where the kids learn without noticing.

Lawrence Hall of Science — 1 Centennial Dr, Berkeley. A hilltop science museum with a full Bay view from the patio, hands-on exhibits, a planetarium, and the giant Pheena whale to climb on. @thelawrencehallofscience

Children's Fairyland — 699 Bellevue Ave, Oakland. The original storybook park, still running kids through the same little gates it opened with in 1950. @fairylandca

Habitot Children's Museum — 1569 Solano Ave, Berkeley. Built for toddlers and preschoolers: a pretend grocery store, an art studio, a water table. Two hours of gentle wins. @habitotmuseum

Little Farm — Tilden Nature Area, Canon Dr, Berkeley. Goats, sheep, pigs, and chickens. Bring lettuce or celery from home, the only food the animals are allowed to have. @ebrpd

Oakland Zoo — 9777 Golf Links Rd, Oakland. A gondola ride over the African Savanna and a California Trail wing with condors, grizzlies, and mountain lions. The all-day commit. @oaklandzoo

Crab Cove Visitor Center — 1252 McKay Ave, Alameda. An aquarium of Bay species with a low-tide pool program and pier fishing demos. Hours are seasonal, so check before you drive over.

Sulphur Creek Nature Center — 1801 D St, Hayward. A native wildlife rehabilitation center with owls, foxes, raccoons, and snakes. The most underrated kid spot in the East Bay.

Coyote Hills Visitor Center — 8000 Patterson Ranch Rd, Fremont. Ohlone shellmounds, marsh boardwalks, and a small museum right at the trailhead.

Eight where they learn without noticing: Lawrence Hall, Children's Fairyland, Habitot, the Little Farm, Oakland Zoo, Crab Cove, Sulphur Creek, and Coyote Hills. Which one was your kid's favorite?

item.title: East Bay Summer, Outdoor Swim Spots
item.description: The East Bay does not cool off in the ocean, it cools off in lakes. Lake Anza alone has a sandy beach and summer lifeguards tucked inside the Berkeley Hill
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Summer, Outdoor Swim Spots

The East Bay does not cool off in the ocean, it cools off in lakes. Lake Anza alone has a sandy beach and summer lifeguards tucked inside the Berkeley Hills. Eight outdoor swim spots families keep coming back to.

Lake Anza — Off Canon Dr, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. A sandy beach inside a Berkeley Hills lake, lifeguards through summer, a swim test for kids over seven. The Berkeley summer ritual. @ebrpd

Lake Temescal Recreation Area — 6500 Broadway, Oakland. A roadside lake at the foot of Highway 13 with a sandy swim beach, picnic tables, and easy parking. The drive-up summer day.

Don Castro Regional Recreation Area — 22400 Woodroe Ave, Hayward. A reservoir with a fenced swim lagoon, lifeguards, and no boats in the swim area. The family safety pick.

Cull Canyon Regional Recreation Area — 18825 Cull Canyon Rd, Castro Valley. The same EBRPD format, a fenced lagoon and a sand beach, seasonal. The 580 corridor go-to.

Quarry Lakes Regional Recreation Area — 2100 Isherwood Way, Fremont. Two big lakes, a designated swim area, and a fishing pier. The southeast Bay summer escape.

Crown Memorial State Beach — 8th St and Otis Dr, Alameda. Calm Bay water, a long flat beach, and the San Francisco skyline across the water. Best for beach play, not deep swimming.

Clarke Memorial Swim Center — Heather Farm Park, 1750 Heather Dr, Walnut Creek. An Olympic-size lap pool plus a kids' pool with splash features, open year-round. The all-weather option.

Roberts Pool — 10570 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. A renovated, heated outdoor pool set inside a redwood grove, open weekends and holidays June 20 to September 27. Swimming when lifeguards are on.

Eight ways to cool off: Lake Anza, Lake Temescal, Don Castro, Cull Canyon, Quarry Lakes, Crown Beach, the Clarke Center at Heather Farm, and Roberts Pool. Where does your family go?

item.title: East Bay Birding
item.description: Lake Merritt became the first official wildlife refuge in the United States in 1870, and it sits right in the middle of downtown Oakland. Pelicans, cormora
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Birding

Lake Merritt became the first official wildlife refuge in the United States in 1870, and it sits right in the middle of downtown Oakland. Pelicans, cormorants, and egrets, no drive required. Eight East Bay birding spots.

Rotary Nature Center at Lake Merritt — 600 Bellevue Ave, Oakland. The center reopened in 2026 on the shore of that 1870 refuge. Pelicans, cormorants, and egrets in the middle of downtown.

Hayward Regional Shoreline — 3010 W Winton Ave, Hayward. Marsh trails along the Bay edge with great blue herons, snowy egrets, and sandpipers; best at dawn or dusk. @ebrpd

Eastshore State Park — University Ave at Frontage Rd, Berkeley. A long stretch of restored shoreline with migratory shorebirds in fall and spring, terns and gulls year-round.

Jewel Lake — Tilden Nature Area, Canon Dr, Berkeley. A small lake at the bottom of Wildcat Canyon with songbirds, woodpeckers, and the occasional dusk owl.

Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge — 1 Marshlands Rd, Fremont. The largest urban wildlife refuge in the country, salt ponds and boardwalks, the birder's pilgrimage.

Briones Reservoir — Bear Creek Rd, Orinda. A restricted-access EBMUD watershed with a Bay-watching lookout for bald eagles, ospreys, and red-tailed hawks; a trail permit is required.

Coyote Hills Regional Park — 8000 Patterson Ranch Rd, Fremont. A marsh boardwalk plus grasslands with owls in the willows and harriers low over the marsh.

Sibley Volcanic Preserve — 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. A ridge raptor-migration corridor in fall along the Oakland-Orinda border.

Eight East Bay birding spots: the Rotary Nature Center, Hayward Shoreline, Eastshore, Jewel Lake, Don Edwards, Briones Reservoir, Coyote Hills, and Sibley. What is your favorite local sighting?

item.title: East Bay Date-night Walks
item.description: The best East Bay date night costs nothing and needs no reservation: a long walk at golden hour. Lake Merritt lights its Necklace of Lights at dusk, and it
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Date-night Walks

The best East Bay date night costs nothing and needs no reservation: a long walk at golden hour. Lake Merritt lights its Necklace of Lights at dusk, and it is only the opener. Seven East Bay date walks worth the babysitter.

Lake Merritt loop — Around Lake Merritt, Oakland. The three-mile Necklace of Lights lit up at dusk. Walk the long way around past the boathouse. The classic East Bay date opener.

Cesar Chavez Park — Berkeley Marina, west end of University Ave, Berkeley. Bay views west, the bridge straight ahead, the kite field out at the tip. Bring a thermos; the wind makes you walk closer.

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. A paved ridge trail open to every pace. The bench at the end earns whatever you packed. First date or twentieth. @ebrpd

Crown Memorial State Beach — 8th St and Otis Dr, Alameda. A long flat boardwalk with the San Francisco skyline straight ahead and calm Bay water beside you. An easy talking pace.

Middle Harbor Shoreline Park — 2777 Middle Harbor Rd, Oakland. Container cranes on one side, the sunset on the other. Industrial and romantic at once, quiet and hand in hand.

Iron Horse Trail, downtown Walnut Creek — Iron Horse Regional Trail, Walnut Creek. Pop out at any cross street for ice cream, then walk back the way you came. The conversation date.

Jack London Square — Waterfront promenade, Jack London Square, Oakland. Ferries pulling in, the old swing bridge moving overhead, boats along the boardwalk. Easy parking, easy night.

Seven East Bay date walks: Lake Merritt, Cesar Chavez Park, Inspiration Point, Crown Beach, Middle Harbor, the Iron Horse Trail in Walnut Creek, and Jack London Square. Which one is your go-to?

item.title: East Bay Live Music
item.description: The Greek Theatre has been staging shows on the UC Berkeley hillside since 1903, eucalyptus and headliners under the same stars. Twelve East Bay live-music
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Live Music

The Greek Theatre has been staging shows on the UC Berkeley hillside since 1903, eucalyptus and headliners under the same stars. Twelve East Bay live-music rooms worth the Friday night.

The Greek Theatre — 2001 Gayley Rd, Berkeley. An outdoor amphitheater carved into the hillside in 1903. Eucalyptus, open sky, and a bucket-list seat. @greekberkeley

Fox Theater — 1807 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A restored 1928 art-deco palace on Telegraph. Mid-size touring acts and locals you will see headline elsewhere in a few years. @foxoakland

Paramount Theatre — 2025 Broadway, Oakland. An art-deco landmark from 1931, fully restored. Symphony nights, classic film series, arena-quality sound. @oakparamount

Yoshi's — 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland. Two sets a night in the dinner-jazz tradition, the room where Bay Area jazz history keeps adding chapters. @yoshis_oak

Freight and Salvage — 2020 Addison St, Berkeley. A folk and roots listening room running since 1968. No chatter while the artist plays, that is the rule. @thefreightberkeley

Ashkenaz — 1317 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A world-music and dance hall since 1973. Cumbia, klezmer, soul, and a wood floor with forty years of footwork on it. @ashkenazberkeley

The UC Theatre — 2036 University Ave, Berkeley. A restored vaudeville house turned all-ages music hall that has shaped Bay Area audiences for a decade.

The New Parish — 1743 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. An intimate 400-capacity room with a beloved upstairs patio where you can still hear the set. @thenewparish

Retro Junkie — 2112 N Main St, Walnut Creek. Tribute bands, karaoke, and pinball in an 80s-and-90s room, the 680-corridor live-music pick. @retrojunkiebar

Ivy Room — 860 San Pablo Ave, Albany. A 200-capacity independent room hailed as one of the best-sounding in the Bay, punk to jazz to Americana.

924 Gilman — 924 Gilman St, Berkeley. The volunteer-run, all-ages, no-alcohol punk collective that launched Green Day and Operation Ivy, running since 1986. @924gilman

Calvin Simmons Theatre — Henry J Kaiser Center, 10 10th St, Oakland. A 1,500-seat 1915 hall reopened after two decades dark.

Twelve East Bay live-music rooms: the Greek, Fox, Paramount, Yoshi's, Freight, Ashkenaz, the UC Theatre, the New Parish, Retro Junkie, the Ivy Room, 924 Gilman, and the Calvin Simmons, the last five from your comments. Which stage has your favorite show memory?

item.title: East Bay Late-night Drives
item.description: The best late-night East Bay date is a drive with the windows down. Skyline Boulevard alone strings the ridge from Joaquin Miller to Tilden through eucalyp
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Late-night Drives

The best late-night East Bay date is a drive with the windows down. Skyline Boulevard alone strings the ridge from Joaquin Miller to Tilden through eucalyptus tunnels with the city lights below. Seven roads that turn into dates.

Skyline Boulevard — Oakland Hills, from Joaquin Miller Rd to Grizzly Peak, Oakland. The ridge drive that strings the East Bay together, eucalyptus tunnels and city lights to the west. Take it slow.

Grizzly Peak Boulevard — Berkeley and Oakland Hills. An empty road at night with San Francisco lit up across the Bay. Pull off at the Caldecott vista. The classic East Bay night drive.

Niles Canyon Road — Route 84, Niles district of Fremont to Sunol. Creek on one side, granite on the other, two lanes through redwood country. Roll the windows down.

Crow Canyon Road — Castro Valley to San Ramon. Country curves, oak trees, and no traffic after ten. The drive that talks itself out of going home.

Wildcat Canyon Road — Berkeley Hills to San Pablo Dam Rd. A ridge through eucalyptus that drops down into Tilden. Pull off at the Inspiration Point lot for the city-lights view.

Tunnel Road to Highway 24 — Oakland to the Caldecott. The cut through the hills, with the lights of Lafayette and Walnut Creek opening up. The twelve-minute escape.

Lake Merritt at midnight — Around Lake Merritt, Oakland. The Necklace of Lights, no traffic, a slow lap with the windows down.

Seven East Bay night drives: Skyline, Grizzly Peak, Niles Canyon, Crow Canyon, Wildcat Canyon, Tunnel Road, and the Lake Merritt loop. Where do you point the car at midnight?

item.title: East Bay Patios
item.description: The East Bay patio season is short, so locals guard the good ones. Pizzaiolo's back garden turns over fast at seven, and Fentons has done sidewalk sundaes
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Patios

The East Bay patio season is short, so locals guard the good ones. Pizzaiolo's back garden turns over fast at seven, and Fentons has done sidewalk sundaes on Piedmont Ave for generations. Six outdoor patios worth the long lunch.

Mua — 2442 Webster St, Oakland. An industrial bi-level with a covered patio and eclectic art, open from 5pm Tuesday through Sunday. The early-evening seats are the calm ones.

Massimo's — 5200 Mowry Ave, Fremont. Italian since 1976, with a side patio in the warmer months. Most book the dining room; the patio holds the quiet two-tops. @massimosfremont

Pizzaiolo — 5008 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Wood-fired pies and natural wine. Most queue at the bar; the back garden seats are first-come and turn over fast at seven.

Curbside Creamery — 482 49th St, Oakland, in Temescal Alley. A shared courtyard tucked behind Telegraph that most people miss. Pair a scoop with a sandwich from the neighbors. @curbsidecreamery

Fentons Creamery — 4226 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Sidewalk seating with the sundae chaser. Most do not realize Fentons runs a full lunch menu. @fentons_creamery

Suju's Coffee and Tea — 4949 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont. A shaded patio open late, to 11pm daily. The afternoon seat when it is too hot inside.

Six East Bay patios: Mua, Massimo's, Pizzaiolo, Curbside Creamery, Fentons, and Suju's. Where do you settle in for the long lunch?

item.title: East Bay Movie Theaters
item.description: The Grand Lake Theatre still lights its original 1926 neon marquee over Grand Ave every night. Six East Bay movie houses worth the drive, from that marquee
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Movie Theaters

The Grand Lake Theatre still lights its original 1926 neon marquee over Grand Ave every night. Six East Bay movie houses worth the drive, from that marquee to the couches at the New Parkway.

Grand Lake Theatre — 3200 Grand Ave, Oakland. Built in 1926, the original neon marquee preserved. Most come for one show and then book the balcony for the next twenty. @grandlaketheater

Landmark Piedmont Theatre — 4186 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Oakland's oldest continuously operating movie house. The regulars time visits to the smaller-room art-house programming.

AMC NewPark 12 — 400 Newpark Mall, Newark. IMAX with Laser, Dolby Cinema, all recliners. The Fremont-area default for tentpole opening weekends.

Cine Lounge Fremont 7 — 39160 Paseo Padre Pkwy, Fremont. A Bollywood and Hollywood mix with full bar service and loaded recliners most guests do not know to order from. @cineloungefremont

The New Parkway Theater — 474 24th St, Oakland. Couches, beer, and a full kitchen; you order at the counter and they bring it to your seat. @thenewparkway

Rialto Cinemas Elmwood — 2966 College Ave, Berkeley. A three-screen indie house programmed by film nerds. The documentaries most people skip are the highlight. @rialtocinemaselmwood

Six East Bay movie houses: Grand Lake, Landmark Piedmont, AMC NewPark 12, Cine Lounge Fremont 7, the New Parkway, and Rialto Elmwood. Which marquee is your date-night default?

item.title: East Bay Boutique Hotels, a Night Away
item.description: The Claremont has stood on the Berkeley-Oakland line since 1915, all white towers and 22 acres you can spot from the freeway. Five East Bay stays for a nig
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Boutique Hotels, a Night Away

The Claremont has stood on the Berkeley-Oakland line since 1915, all white towers and 22 acres you can spot from the freeway. Five East Bay stays for a night away without going near an airport.

Claremont Resort and Club — 41 Tunnel Rd, Berkeley. The 1915 landmark on the hill, with the pools, the spa, and the Bay view that has anchored East Bay date nights for a century.

Hotel Shattuck Plaza — 2086 Allston Way, Berkeley. A 1910 boutique hotel in the heart of downtown, two blocks from campus, with a Mediterranean restaurant and lobby bar downstairs.

Graduate by Hilton Berkeley — 2600 Durant Ave, Berkeley. Themed around Cal history and walkable to dinner, with a rooftop that opens seasonally to a skyline view toward the Bay.

Kissel Uptown Oakland — 2455 Broadway, Oakland. A restored Beaux Arts landmark reborn as a design forward hotel in Uptown, with Otto's kitchen and a rooftop lounge.

Hilton Garden Inn — 45976 Warm Springs Blvd, Fremont. Modern rooms near Mission San Jose, with the quiet mountain-view side facing the old Mission.

Five East Bay stays: the Claremont, Hotel Shattuck Plaza, Graduate Berkeley, Kissel Uptown Oakland, and the Hilton Garden Inn in Fremont. Which one would you pick for the night?

item.title: East Bay Family Weekend Rituals
item.description: Tilden's quarter-scale steam train has been running kids through the Berkeley hills for decades, and the Little Farm is a five-minute drive from the platfo
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Family Weekend Rituals

Tilden's quarter-scale steam train has been running kids through the Berkeley hills for decades, and the Little Farm is a five-minute drive from the platform. Eight East Bay weekend rituals that hold up over time.

Tilden Steam Train and Little Farm — Steam train at Grizzly Peak Blvd and Lomas Cantadas, Little Farm at Tilden Nature Area, Canon Dr, Berkeley. Goats and a quarter-scale locomotive; the combo is the whole morning. @redwoodvalleyrailway

Children's Fairyland — 699 Bellevue Ave, Oakland. A storybook park since 1950, the one Walt Disney toured for ideas. Newcomers underestimate it. @fairylandca

Quarry Lakes — 2100 Isherwood Way, Fremont. A swim beach, two playgrounds, and fishing. South-East Bay families know it; north-side families should. @ebrpd

Coyote Hills at golden hour — 8000 Patterson Ranch Rd, Fremont. Marsh boardwalks most people do in daylight. Sunset is the play.

Niles Antique Faire — Niles Town Plaza, 37482 Niles Blvd, Fremont. The big one is the last Sunday of August, dawn to mid-afternoon, hundreds of sellers filling the old town.

Mission Peak sunrise — Stanford Ave staging, 43600 Mission Blvd, Fremont. The 5am crowd gets the parking and the light; the 8am crowd gets neither.

Fentons Sunday sundae — 4226 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. A multi-generational tradition since 1894. The line is long on weekends. The line is the experience. @fentons_creamery

Piedmont Park — Highland Ave, Piedmont. A small neighborhood park with big regulars, the low-key one families rotate back to.

Eight rituals: the Tilden train and farm, Fairyland, Quarry Lakes, Coyote Hills at sunset, the Niles faire, a Mission Peak sunrise, a Fentons sundae, and Piedmont Park. What is your family's go-to?

item.title: East Bay Dog Parks
item.description: Point Isabel is the largest off-leash dog park on the West Coast, 23 acres of Richmond shoreline with the San Francisco skyline across the water. Eight Eas
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Dog Parks

Point Isabel is the largest off-leash dog park on the West Coast, 23 acres of Richmond shoreline with the San Francisco skyline across the water. Eight East Bay dog parks worth the drive.

Point Isabel Regional Shoreline — 2701 Isabel St, Richmond. Twenty-three acres of off-leash Bay shoreline, trails, and beach access, with a dog wash on site. @ebrpd

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. A 90-acre off-leash hilltop on the Berkeley Marina, kite hill and Bay Bridge views, shorter lines than Point Isabel.

Hardy Dog Park — 491 Hardy St, Oakland. A small fenced run under the College Ave overpass where the regulars know each other's dogs by name.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3590 Sanborn Dr, Oakland. Off-leash trails inside the redwoods that most newcomers never explore. They are the move.

Hap Magee Ranch Park — 1025 La Gonda Way, Danville. Two fenced runs, small and large dogs separated, worth the drive even from Oakland.

Heather Farm Dog Park — 505 N San Carlos Dr, Walnut Creek. A big, well-kept run with a water station where most of the local dogs are regulars.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. Off-leash on the old landfill peninsula, with public art, Bay views, and a sculpture trail. The dog park with personality.

Lake Chabot — 17600 Lake Chabot Rd, Castro Valley. Miles of dog-friendly fire road along the water.

Eight for the dogs: Point Isabel, Cesar Chavez, Hardy, Joaquin Miller, Hap Magee, Heather Farm, Albany Bulb, and Lake Chabot. Where does yours pull the leash toward?

item.title: Berkeley Walks
item.description: Indian Rock in North Berkeley has stone steps carved right into the outcrop and a 360-degree Bay view that beats any dinner reservation at sunset. Eight Be
item.content:encoded:
Berkeley Walks

Indian Rock in North Berkeley has stone steps carved right into the outcrop and a 360-degree Bay view that beats any dinner reservation at sunset. Eight Berkeley walks worth a Saturday morning.

Indian Rock Park — 950 Indian Rock Ave, Berkeley. A sandstone outcrop with carved steps to the summit, open dawn to late, and the sunset locals guard.

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. Ninety acres on a former landfill, off-leash trails, and the Solar Calendar sculpture at the north end most people miss.

Berkeley Rose Garden — 1200 Euclid Ave, Berkeley. Eight terraces and 1,500 rose bushes built in 1937, with peak bloom from mid-May into June.

Tilden Regional Park — Off Grizzly Peak Blvd and Wildcat Canyon Rd, Berkeley. Two thousand acres, the Lake Anza loop, and a Botanic Garden of California natives most newcomers skip. @ebrpd

Codornices Park — 1201 Euclid Ave, Berkeley. Across from the Rose Garden, with the concrete hillside slide built in 1947. Pack cardboard for speed.

Claremont Canyon Regional Preserve — Stonewall Rd trailhead off Claremont Ave, Berkeley. The Stonewall-Panoramic climb to a Bay-and-bridge ridge view you remember.

Berkeley Fire Trails — Strawberry Canyon, Centennial Dr, Berkeley. A wide graded path along the ridge behind the stadium, with a wildflower stretch in April.

Grizzly Peak overlook — Grizzly Peak Blvd, Berkeley Hills. A pull-off above Tilden with a four-bridge view on clear nights.

Eight Berkeley walks: Indian Rock, Cesar Chavez, the Rose Garden, Tilden, Codornices, Claremont Canyon, the Fire Trails, and Grizzly Peak. Which one is your Saturday reset?

item.title: East Bay Sunset Spots
item.description: From the draw-outs on Grizzly Peak you get the Bay Bridge, San Francisco, and the Golden Gate in a single frame, no hike required. Seven East Bay sunset sp
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sunset Spots

From the draw-outs on Grizzly Peak you get the Bay Bridge, San Francisco, and the Golden Gate in a single frame, no hike required. Seven East Bay sunset spots that earn the drive.

Grizzly Peak Boulevard — Kensington to Skyline Blvd, Berkeley and Oakland Hills. Pull off at any named viewpoint for the full Bay in one frame. The drive is the date.

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. A paved ridge trail, 30 minutes round trip, to the bench locals call the seat of the East Bay. @ebrpd

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The highest summit in the Berkeley Hills, a 360-degree view, and an easy fire-road climb.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3590 Sanborn Dr, Oakland. A eucalyptus path to a sunset bench, the locals' spot when Grizzly Peak is jammed.

Sibley Volcanic Preserve — 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. A volcano you can hike, with Mount Tam turning pink across the Bay at sunset.

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. Kite hill on the Berkeley Marina, a full Bay view and no climb required.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. The Bay's edge with a sculpture trail above, a different sunset every visit.

Seven for golden hour: Grizzly Peak, Inspiration Point, Vollmer Peak, Joaquin Miller, Sibley, Cesar Chavez, and Albany Bulb. Which one do you drive to?

item.title: East Bay Short Workday Walks
item.description: The Lake Merritt half-loop is 1.5 lit and paved miles you can walk on a lunch break and be back before the next meeting. Eight East Bay short walks that fi
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Short Workday Walks

The Lake Merritt half-loop is 1.5 lit and paved miles you can walk on a lunch break and be back before the next meeting. Eight East Bay short walks that fit inside a workday.

Lake Merritt half-loop — Lakeside Park, 666 Bellevue Ave, Oakland. About 1.5 miles around the south side, lit and paved, the Necklace of Lights overhead. The lunchtime escape.

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. A half-mile flat loop on the Berkeley Marina with the Bay Bridge straight ahead. A quick reset.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3590 Sanborn Dr, Oakland. A 1.2-mile loop inside the redwoods. Smell the air, forget the inbox.

Lafayette Reservoir — 3849 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A 1.4-mile paved stretch around the water; pay to park, worth the 30-minute reset.

Heather Farm Park — 301 N San Carlos Dr, Walnut Creek. An 0.8-mile inner loop past the duck pond and garden, back at the car in 20 minutes.

Crown Memorial Beach — 8th St and Otis Dr, Alameda. A half-mile of flat boardwalk with Bay water and the SF skyline. Bring a sandwich. @ebrpd

Lake Anza loop — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. About 1.4 miles around the swim lake, eucalyptus and blackberry and easy steps.

Iron Horse Trail, downtown Walnut Creek — Near the Walnut Creek BART, a one-mile out and back through the corridor.

Eight workday walks: the Lake Merritt half-loop, Cesar Chavez, Joaquin Miller, Lafayette Reservoir, Heather Farm, Crown Beach, Lake Anza, and the Iron Horse Trail. Which is your midday reset?

item.title: East Bay After-dinner Strolls
item.description: The Necklace of Lights strings 3.4 fully lit miles around Lake Merritt, the after-dinner lap most couples never extend past. The best part of the date is t
item.content:encoded:
East Bay After-dinner Strolls

The Necklace of Lights strings 3.4 fully lit miles around Lake Merritt, the after-dinner lap most couples never extend past. The best part of the date is the walk, and eight corridors are built for it. Eight East Bay corridors worth strolling end to end.

Lake Merritt loop — Around Lake Merritt, Oakland. The 3.4-mile Necklace of Lights, fully lit. The classic post-dinner lap.

Piedmont Avenue — Piedmont Ave district, Oakland. Walk the avenue end to end after dinner, windows lit, the pace slow. @piedmontavenue_oakland

College Avenue — Rockridge, Oakland, from the BART station. Twelve blocks of after-dinner browsing, with bookstores open till nine. @rockridgeoakland

Solano Avenue — Albany and Berkeley. A mile of independent shops to wander slowly with whoever you brought. @onsolanoavenue

Park Street — Downtown Alameda. After dinner, walk down to the restored Alameda Theatre marquee. @downtownalameda

Fourth Street — Berkeley, between University and Virginia. Quieter at night, shop windows lit, walkable in 20 minutes. @fourthstreetshops

Grand Avenue — Grand Lake, Oakland. Walk toward the Grand Lake Theatre's neon marquee.

Niles Boulevard — Niles Historic District, Fremont. Antique-shop windows lit along the old main street. @nmsaniles

Eight after-dinner strolls: Lake Merritt, Piedmont, College, Solano, Park Street, Fourth Street, Grand, and Niles. Which avenue do you walk after dinner?

item.title: East Bay Easy Summit Hikes
item.description: Round Top is a volcano summit you can reach in two miles and 600 feet of climb, Bay views and all. Seven East Bay summit hikes for people who think summits
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Easy Summit Hikes

Round Top is a volcano summit you can reach in two miles and 600 feet of climb, Bay views and all. Seven East Bay summit hikes for people who think summits mean suffering.

Round Top — Sibley Volcanic Preserve, 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. Two miles and 600 feet to a volcano summit with Bay views. The accessible peak. @ebrpd

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. A fire road to the highest point in the Berkeley Hills, 1.5 miles at a gentle grade.

Wildcat Peak — Tilden Nature Area, 600 Canon Dr, Berkeley. A short climb to a sweeping panorama; closer than Mount Tam and half the effort.

Mount Wanda — John Muir NHS, Alhambra Ave at Franklin Canyon Rd, Martinez. Named for John Muir's daughter, a one-mile climb through oak grassland.

Inspiration Point to Wildcat ridge — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Orinda. A paved approach to a dirt ridge trail, 1.7 miles each way.

Knobcone Point — Sibley Volcanic Preserve, 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. The quieter cousin to Round Top, the same view with fewer people.

Cragmont Rock Park — 960 Regal Rd, Berkeley. A five-minute walk from the car to a Bay-view boulder.

Seven easy summits: Round Top, Vollmer Peak, Wildcat Peak, Mount Wanda, the Inspiration Point ridge, Knobcone Point, and Cragmont Rock. Which one surprised you with how easy it was?

item.title: East Bay Walk-in Date Nights
item.description: The Chez Panisse cafe upstairs runs the same kitchen as the dining room for half the bill, and it is friendlier to a walk-in. Eight East Bay date nights th
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Walk-in Date Nights

The Chez Panisse cafe upstairs runs the same kitchen as the dining room for half the bill, and it is friendlier to a walk-in. Eight East Bay date nights that need no reservation.

Chez Panisse Cafe — 1517 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The Alice Waters cafe upstairs, the same kitchen as downstairs at half the price. @chezpanisse

Bar Panisse — 1515 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The Chez Panisse bar next door, a late walk-in spot most diners never notice. @barpanisse_

Heinold's First and Last Chance Saloon — 48 Webster St, Oakland. Built in 1883 from a whaling ship, with a floor that still slants from the 1906 quake. @firstandlastchanceoakland

Drake's Dealership — 2325 Broadway, Oakland. A beer garden inside an old Dodge dealership, 30-plus taps and room to walk in. @drakesdealership

The UC Theatre — 2036 University Ave, Berkeley. Dark-night film screenings, five dollars with any prior show stub. @theuctheatre

Fox Theater lobby — 1807 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A restored 1928 Moorish-revival palace; the mezzanine standing room is the move. @foxoakland

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. A decommissioned landfill turned sculpture park, free and open, best at sunset.

Faction Brewing — 2501 Monarch St, Alameda. Bay views with the city skyline lined up off the deck at Alameda Point. @factionbrewing

Eight walk-in date nights: the Chez Panisse cafe, Bar Panisse, Heinold's, Drake's Dealership, the UC Theatre, the Fox lobby, Albany Bulb, and Faction Brewing. What is your no-reservation move?

item.title: East Bay Institutions That Outlasted Everything
item.description: Heinold's First and Last Chance has poured in the same slanted-floor shack by the Oakland estuary since 1883. Eight East Bay institutions that outlasted ev
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Institutions That Outlasted Everything

Heinold's First and Last Chance has poured in the same slanted-floor shack by the Oakland estuary since 1883. Eight East Bay institutions that outlasted everything around them.

Heinold's First and Last Chance Saloon — 48 Webster St, Oakland. Pouring since 1883, the floor still tilted from the 1906 quake. @firstandlastchanceoakland

Fentons Creamery — 4226 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Open since 1894, five generations in, the black and tan sundae theirs. @fentons_creamery

Chez Panisse — 1517 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Alice Waters since 1971, the restaurant that built California cuisine. @chezpanisse

Cheese Board Collective — 1504 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Worker-owned since 1971, one rotating pizza a day and a line that always moves. @cheeseboardcoll

Yoshi's — 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland. A jazz club and Japanese kitchen since 1972, two sets a night. @yoshis_oak

Berkeley Bowl — 2020 Oregon St, Berkeley. An independent grocery since 1977 whose produce aisles became a legend. Wednesday is restock day. @berkeleybowl

Acme Bread — 1601 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. Steve Sullivan since 1983, and the walnut levain sells out by 11am on Saturdays. @acmebreadcompany

Caffe Strada — 2300 College Ave, Berkeley. A campus institution since 1989, with a heated fireplace patio and a white hot chocolate regulars swear by. @caffestradaberkeley

Eight that outlasted everything: Heinold's, Fentons, Chez Panisse, the Cheese Board, Yoshi's, Berkeley Bowl, Acme, and Caffe Strada. Which one would you defend in an argument?

item.title: East Bay Sunrise Hikes
item.description: Mission Peak releases its sunrise-hike permits 24 hours ahead, and almost nobody knows the early window exists. Eight East Bay spots worth setting the alar
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sunrise Hikes

Mission Peak releases its sunrise-hike permits 24 hours ahead, and almost nobody knows the early window exists. Eight East Bay spots worth setting the alarm for, summits and ridges and shoreline before the city wakes.

Mission Peak — Stanford Ave staging, 43600 Mission Blvd, Fremont. Sunrise permits release 24 hours in advance. The 5am climb beats the crowd and the heat. @ebrpd

Mount Diablo summit — Summit Rd, Mount Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. Drive up and park at the visitor center; the Bay opens up by 6:30 most mornings.

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The four-mile paved Nimitz Way, easy at 5am, with the fog peeling off by 7.

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The highest point in the East Bay park system, a five-minute walk from the lot off Grizzly Peak Blvd.

Joaquin Miller ridge — 3450 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. The least-visited sunrise spot here; park at the upper lots and walk five minutes to the view.

Sibley Volcanic Preserve — 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. The Round Top trail, where the bay haze burns off around 7:30 and the volcano ridge opens up.

Berkeley Marina kite hill — Cesar Chavez Park, 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. The wind is dead at sunrise and the Golden Gate gets its best hour of the day.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. The bay-side sunrise walk most people only ever do at sunset.

Eight for the alarm: Mission Peak, Mount Diablo, Inspiration Point, Vollmer Peak, Joaquin Miller, Sibley, the Berkeley Marina kite hill, and Albany Bulb. Which one gets you up early?

item.description: The Cheese Board pizza line looks brutal until 11:30, when the first round comes out and it starts moving fast. Eight East Bay walk-ups where the wait is t
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Walk-ups Worth the Line

The Cheese Board pizza line looks brutal until 11:30, when the first round comes out and it starts moving fast. Eight East Bay walk-ups where the wait is the price of admission.

Cheese Board Pizza — 1512 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Show up at 11:30, not noon; one rotating pizza a day and a line that keeps moving. @cheeseboardcoll

Boichik Bagels — 3170 College Ave, Berkeley. The closest the Bay has come to a real New York bagel, and it sells out before noon. @boichikbagels

Bake Sum — 3249 Grand Ave, Oakland. Mochi muffins and milk bread; get there Saturday at 9am or wait for the next bake. @bakesumpastries

Fentons Creamery — 4226 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Open since 1894, and the black and tan sundae is the order worth the weekend wait. @fentons_creamery

Vik's Chaat — 2390 4th St, Berkeley. Thirty-plus years of chaat; the pani puri is mandatory and the line is half the fun. @vikschaat

Burma Superstar — 4721 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Tea leaf salad and coconut chicken curry, no reservations, open daily till nine. @burmasuperstar

Acme Bread — 1601 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. The walnut levain sells out by 11am on Saturdays, so get there at open. @acmebreadcompany

Pizzaiolo — 5008 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Charlie Hallowell since 2005; Saturday brunch beats the weeknight wait by an hour. @pizzaiolooakland

Eight worth standing in line for: Cheese Board, Boichik, Bake Sum, Fentons, Vik's Chaat, Burma Superstar, Acme, and Pizzaiolo. Which line do you actually wait in?

item.title: East Bay Drive-up Views
item.description: Inspiration Point's Nimitz Way is four paved, wheelchair-accessible miles that most people assume is a rough trail. Eight East Bay views you do not have to
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Drive-up Views

Inspiration Point's Nimitz Way is four paved, wheelchair-accessible miles that most people assume is a rough trail. Eight East Bay views you do not have to hike for, the drive-up moves for when you want nature, not cardio.

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The paved, wheelchair-accessible Nimitz Way, with a bench overlooking Briones Reservoir. @ebrpd

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The highest point in the East Bay park system, a short walk from the lot off Grizzly Peak Blvd.

Mount Diablo summit — Summit Rd, Mount Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. The visitor center sits in the original 1939 stone tower, with drive-up access on weekends.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3450 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. The Cascade waterfall runs after winter rain, February through April.

Berkeley Marina kite hill — Cesar Chavez Park, 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. The wind builds 1pm to 5pm year-round, and the whole Bay is right there.

Crown Memorial Beach — 8th St and Otis Dr, Alameda. A mile and a half of sand, a bird sanctuary at the south end, and telescopes on the boardwalk.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. A decommissioned landfill turned sculpture park; sunset is the move.

Chabot Space and Science Center — 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. Research-level telescopes open to the public Friday through Sunday nights. @chabotspace

Eight without the climb: Inspiration Point, Vollmer Peak, Mount Diablo, Joaquin Miller, the Berkeley Marina, Crown Beach, Albany Bulb, and Chabot. Which one is your long-way-home?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Quiet Date Nights

The Chez Panisse bar hides behind the restaurant and only takes walk-ins after 9pm, so most diners never know it is there. Nine East Bay date nights the locals keep quiet.

Bar Panisse — 1515 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The Chez Panisse bar across the wall, a late walk-in spot after 9pm. @barpanisse_

Faction Brewing — 2501 Monarch St, Alameda. Bay views with the city skyline lined up off the deck at Alameda Point. @factionbrewing

The New Parish — 1743 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. The upstairs bar is open during shows, cheaper than the floor with the same sound piped up. @thenewparish

Ashkenaz — 1317 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A world-music dance hall since 1973, with free dance lessons on Tuesdays before the show. @ashkenazberkeley

Freight and Salvage cafe — 2020 Addison St, Berkeley. The folk-venue cafe opens 90 minutes before the show, cheaper food than the hall. @thefreightberkeley

The UC Theatre — 2036 University Ave, Berkeley. Dark-night film screenings, five dollars with any prior show stub. @theuctheatre

Woodminster Amphitheater — 3300 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. Free summer Sunday concerts in a 1941 WPA-built amphitheater in the redwoods. @woodminstermusicals

Lake Merritt loop — Around Lake Merritt, Oakland. The Necklace of Lights since 1925; a Sunday-morning lap before the farmers-market crowd.

The Alley — 3325 Grand Ave, Oakland. A dim piano bar where the sing-along runs from 9pm to last call. @the_alley_of_oakland

Nine quiet date nights: Bar Panisse, Faction, the New Parish, Ashkenaz, the Freight cafe, the UC Theatre, Woodminster, the Lake Merritt loop, and the Alley. What is your quiet move?

item.content:encoded:

Pizzaiolo changes its pasta menu every week and keeps the pizza locked. That's why the regulars show up on a Tuesday. Seven East Bay weeknight dinners worth leaving the house for.

Pizzaiolo — 5008 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Charlie Hallowell since 2005; the pasta menu changes weekly, the pizza does not. @pizzaiolooakland

Belotti Ristorante e Bottega — 5403 College Ave, Oakland. Rockridge's Michelin-recognized Italian, hand-rolled pasta made in-house. @belottirb

Wood Tavern — 6317 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge neighborhood standard since 2007; sit at the bar and order what the kitchen is excited about. @tavern_oakland

Burma Superstar — 4721 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Tea leaf salad, samusa soup, coconut chicken curry, open daily till nine. @burmasuperstar

Ramen Shop — 5812 College Ave, Oakland. Three Chez Panisse alumni since 2013; the seasonal ramen is the order. @ramenshopoakland

Vik's Chaat — 2390 4th St, Berkeley. Thirty-plus years of chaat; the kati rolls feed two. @vikschaat

item.title: East Bay Day Trips Inside the Area Code
item.description: Charlie Chaplin filmed in the Niles district of Fremont in 1915, and its antique row still runs along Niles Boulevard. Eight East Bay day trips that get yo
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Day Trips Inside the Area Code

Charlie Chaplin filmed in the Niles district of Fremont in 1915, and its antique row still runs along Niles Boulevard. Eight East Bay day trips that get your Saturday back by four, no drive to Tahoe required.

Niles District — Niles Blvd, Fremont. Charlie Chaplin filmed here in 1915, and the antique shops still line the old main street. @nmsaniles

Mount Diablo summit — Summit Rd, Mount Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. On a clear winter day you can see Half Dome; mid-January after a storm is the window.

Coyote Hills — 8000 Patterson Ranch Rd, Fremont. Tidal marsh boardwalks and an Ohlone shellmound dating back two thousand years. @ebrpd

Point Pinole — 5551 Giant Hwy, Richmond. An abandoned dynamite factory turned shoreline park, with a eucalyptus tunnel road and a long fishing pier.

Old Mission San Jose — 43300 Mission Blvd, Fremont. The 1797 mission is still active; the bells ring at 9 on Sunday mornings. @oldmissionsanjose

Niles Canyon Railway — 6 Kilkare Rd, Sunol. Steam-train rides along the original 1869 transcontinental alignment; tickets around thirty dollars. @nilescanyonrailway

Crockett — Crockett, below the Carquinez Bridge. A town of three thousand where the C&H sugar refinery still runs, with a strait overlook worth the drive.

Brentwood U-pick orchards — Brentwood, East Contra Costa. Fifty-plus U-pick farms; cherries in spring, then peaches and stone fruit through summer. Most Bay Area locals have never been east of Walnut Creek.

Eight day trips: Niles, Mount Diablo, Coyote Hills, Point Pinole, Mission San Jose, the Niles Canyon Railway, Crockett, and Brentwood's orchards. Which one gets your Saturday?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Dive Bars

The White Horse in North Oakland has poured since 1933, one of the oldest continuously operating gay bars in the country and never once raided. Eight East Bay dive bars worth the stool time.

Cafe Van Kleef — 1621 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. An eclectic Uptown bar since 2000; the fresh greyhound is the signature and the room is the show. @cafevankleef

Heart and Dagger Saloon — 504 Lake Park Ave, Oakland. A rock-and-roll dive in Grand Lake with pool, pinball, and a lemon-tree patio. Cash only. @heartdaggeroakland

Eli's Mile High Club — 3629 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Oakland. A 1970s blues club turned music venue and kitchen, a real Oakland institution. @elismilehighclub

The White Horse — 6551 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Open since 1933, one of the oldest gay bars in the country, with a jukebox, karaoke, and a disco ball. @whitehorsebar

The Alley — 3325 Grand Ave, Oakland. A historic piano bar where the 9pm sing-along runs until last call. @the_alley_of_oakland

19th Street Station — 1900 Broadway, Oakland. A downtown neighborhood pub by the BART stop, sports memorabilia on the walls and homemade tamales at the bar.

Hotsy Totsy Club — 601 San Pablo Ave, Albany. Albany's oldest bar, since 1939, with free shuffleboard and a jukebox stocked 1952 to 1979. @hotsytotsyclub

Cato's Ale House — 3891 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. A wood-paneled neighborhood ale house since 1992, beer list deep, and no TV. @catosalehouse

Eight for the stool time: Cafe Van Kleef, Heart and Dagger, Eli's Mile High Club, the White Horse, the Alley, 19th Street Station, Hotsy Totsy, and Cato's. Which one would you defend in an argument?

item.description: Oakland's Art Murmur turned First Fridays into a citywide gallery walk, and most of the rooms behind it are artist-run and free. Eight East Bay galleries w
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Art Galleries

Oakland's Art Murmur turned First Fridays into a citywide gallery walk, and most of the rooms behind it are artist-run and free. Eight East Bay galleries worth the First Friday.

Mercury 20 Gallery — 475 25th St, Oakland. Artist-run since 2006, six rotating shows a year across forty artists. Friday and Saturday, 12 to 5. @mercury20gallery

Pro Arts Gallery — 150 Frank H. Ogawa Plaza, Oakland. A nonprofit since 1974 that runs East Bay Open Studios every June, when 400 artists open their workspaces. @proartsoakland

Mills College Art Museum — 5000 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. Free admission Tuesday through Sunday, now part of Mills at Northeastern. @millsartmuseum

BAMPFA — 2155 Center St, Berkeley. The Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive; the film calendar is the secret weapon. @bampfa

Slate Contemporary — 5510 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge gallery with six shows a year, an easy walk-in after a College Ave dinner. @slate_art

The Compound Gallery — 1339 61st St, Emeryville. Eighteen years in, with working artist studios attached to the gallery. @thecompoundgallery

Oakland Museum of California — 1000 Oak St, Oakland. The state museum of California, with Friday Nights and Off the Grid food trucks April through October. @oaklandmuseumca

Worth Ryder Art Gallery — 116 Kroeber Hall, UC Berkeley. Run by the Art Practice department, with student and faculty shows free to the public. @worthryder

Eight for First Friday: Mercury 20, Pro Arts, the Mills museum, BAMPFA, Slate, the Compound, OMCA, and Worth Ryder. Which show stuck with you?

item.title: East Bay Independent Bookstores
item.description: Moe's has stacked four floors of used books on Telegraph since 1959, and the East Bay still has nine more indies holding the line. Ten independent bookstor
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Independent Bookstores

Moe's has stacked four floors of used books on Telegraph since 1959, and the East Bay still has nine more indies holding the line. Ten independent bookstores still standing.

Moe's Books — 2476 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. Four floors since 1959; the top floor is rare and out of print, and most students never get past the second. @moes_books

Pegasus Books — 1855 Solano Ave, Berkeley. Used and new since 1969, with a basement of deep stock most browsers miss. @pegasusbooks

Pegasus Books Downtown — 2349 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The Solano store's downtown sister, smaller but the buy counter turns faster.

Mrs — Dalloway's. 2904 College Ave, Berkeley. An Elmwood indie with a literary garden section, open Monday through Saturday. @mrsdallowaysberkeley

Diesel, A Bookstore — 5433 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge shop of politics, art, and literary fiction with a packed reading series. @dieselabookstore

East Bay Booksellers — 6022 College Ave, Oakland. Reopened in 2024 after a fire, same crew, new Rockridge home. @eastbaybooksellers

Walden Pond Books — 3316 Grand Ave, Oakland. Independent since 1973, with a poetry section curated tighter than any chain. @waldenpondbooks

Builders Booksource — 1817 4th St, Berkeley. Architecture and construction since 1982; the trade shelves are unmatched in the Bay. @buildersbooksource

Marcus Books — 3900 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Oakland. Founded 1960, the oldest Black-owned bookstore in the country. @marcus.books

Orinda Books — 276 Village Sq, Orinda. A quieter community bookstore with weekly author events, out on the 24 corridor. @orindabooks

Ten East Bay indies: Moe's, both Pegasus stores, Mrs. Dalloway's, Diesel, East Bay Booksellers, Walden Pond, Builders, Marcus, and Orinda. Which section do you disappear into?
