item.description: Great Western Power Company built its climbing gym inside a converted downtown Oakland power station, lead walls tall enough to test your nerve. Most East
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Climbing Gyms

Great Western Power Company built its climbing gym inside a converted downtown Oakland power station, lead walls tall enough to test your nerve. Most East Bay climbers still assume the good walls are across a bridge. Six East Bay climbing gyms.

Berkeley Ironworks — 800 Potter St, Berkeley. A Touchstone gym with ropes, bouldering, and a full fitness floor, open from 6am on weekdays.

Great Western Power Company — 520 20th St, Oakland. A Touchstone gym in a converted downtown power building, tall lead walls and a big bouldering cave.

Pacific Pipe — 2140 Mandela Pkwy, Oakland. A Touchstone bouldering gym in West Oakland, open late to 11pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

Bridges Rock Gym — 5635 San Diego St, El Cerrito. A community gym with ropes and boulders, easy parking, and a mellow crowd.

Diablo Rock Gym — 1220 Diamond Way, Concord. An East County Touchstone hub since 2003, slabs, overhangs, and Saturday classes. @diablorockgym

The Peak — 4020 Technology Pl, Fremont. Roped climbing and bouldering across a range of angles, with beginner Saturdays and food on site. @thepeakoffremont

Six without a bridge: Berkeley Ironworks, Great Western Power, Pacific Pipe, Bridges, Diablo Rock, and the Peak. Which one gets your first Saturday?

item.description: NEST on Piedmont Ave folds prenatal, restorative, and pilates into one schedule, and the restorative class is the recovery move most newcomers skip. Five E
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Yoga and Pilates

NEST on Piedmont Ave folds prenatal, restorative, and pilates into one schedule, and the restorative class is the recovery move most newcomers skip. Five East Bay yoga and pilates studios for a Saturday ritual.

NEST Yoga — 3976 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Beginner through advanced, prenatal, restorative, and pilates mixed in. The restorative class is the recovery move. @nestyoga_oakland

Mighty Pilates — 2631 Ashby Ave, Berkeley. 2,400 square feet with twelve Balanced Body reformers under a skylight; the privates are the value. @mightypilates

Bayside Pilates — Off Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Classically trained instructors on genuine Gratz apparatus, where the form work is harder and better.

Reform Your Body Pilates — 1940 University Ave, Berkeley. Apparatus-based work with a six-week intro program built as a rebuild plan.

Funky Door Yoga — 2567 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Bikram and hot pilates, 105 degrees, 90 minutes, no music; week four is when it changes. @funkydooryoga

Five for the Saturday ritual: NEST, Mighty Pilates, Bayside, Reform Your Body, and Funky Door. Which would you try first?

item.title: East Bay Plant Nurseries
item.description: East Bay Nursery has grown California natives on San Pablo Ave since 1942, and the walk-through beats any online order. Eleven East Bay nurseries worth a S
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Plant Nurseries

East Bay Nursery has grown California natives on San Pablo Ave since 1942, and the walk-through beats any online order. Eleven East Bay nurseries worth a Saturday.

East Bay Nursery — 2332 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. Family-owned since 1942; natives, drought-tolerant, veggie starts, fruit trees. @eastbaynursery

Berkeley Horticultural Nursery — 1310 McGee Ave, Berkeley. Operating since 1922, strong on roses, Japanese maples, and edibles; the back greenhouse is the move. @berkeleyhort

The Dry Garden — 6556 Shattuck Ave, Oakland. Drought-tolerant specialists with succulents and grasses you will not find at a chain. @thedrygardennursery

Curious Flora — 740 Market Ave, Richmond. The former Annie's Annuals, mail-order plus retail, deep on rare and unusual perennials.

Planting Justice — 319 105th Ave, Oakland. A nonprofit fruit-tree and food-plant nursery that hires returning citizens, with 200-plus heirloom varieties. @plantingjusticenursery

Broadway Terrace Nursery — 4340 Clarewood Dr, Oakland. A neighborhood nursery where the personal advice on edibles and ornamentals is the difference. @broadwayterracenursery

Regan Nursery — 4268 Decoto Rd, Fremont. More roses than anybody in the Bay Area, plus Japanese maples and shade stock. @reganroses

Native Here Nursery — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. Volunteer-run, 20,000 plants all sourced from Alameda and Contra Costa Counties. @nativeherenursery

The Watershed Nursery — 601 A Canal Blvd, Richmond. An employee-owned native-plant cooperative in Point Richmond since 2001.

Alden Lane Nursery — 981 Alden Ln, Livermore. A full garden center under old valley oaks, family-run since 1955. @aldenlanenursery

Spiral Gardens — 2838 Sacramento St, Berkeley. A community nursery of edibles, herbs, and natives that funds a produce stand and farm.

Eleven nurseries: East Bay, Berkeley Hort, the Dry Garden, Curious Flora, Planting Justice, Broadway Terrace, Regan, Native Here, plus Watershed, Alden Lane, and Spiral Gardens. Which one did you grow up at?

item.title: East Bay Hardware Stores
item.description: Laurel Ace Hardware has told MacArthur shoppers what they actually need since 1921, before anyone spends a dollar at the big box. Most people still make th
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Hardware Stores

Laurel Ace Hardware has told MacArthur shoppers what they actually need since 1921, before anyone spends a dollar at the big box. Most people still make the big-box run first. Ten East Bay hardware stores and lumberyards worth knowing.

Berkeley Ace Hardware — 2020 Milvia St, Berkeley. An old-style store where the staff ask what you are actually trying to fix before they sell you anything, plumbing and electrical up front.

Laurel Ace Hardware — 4024 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A Laurel District anchor since 1921, crowded on Saturday mornings for a reason. @laurel.ace

Truitt and White Lumber — 642 Hearst Ave, Berkeley. A real lumberyard plus full hardware since 1946, the door to walk through when the project needs actual lumber. @truittandwhite

Cole Hardware Rockridge — 5533 College Ave, Oakland. Remodeler-friendly with paint, plumbing, electrical, and keys cut fast, plus a morning regulars rush. @colehardware

Pete's Ace Hardware — 2569 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. Operating since 1926 and marking its centennial this year; ask a question and you get three fixes before you spend a dollar.

Encinal True Value Hardware — 2801 Encinal Ave, Alameda. Family-run since 1965, walkable from the Webster corridor, the place for the one bulb you cannot find online.

Economy Lumber — 750 High St, Oakland. Family-owned since 1957, millwork, custom cuts, and hard-to-find dimensional lumber, with trade pricing on bigger orders. @economylumber

Pagano's Hardware — South Shore Center, Alameda. An Alameda tradition for over 70 years; the right hardware store ten minutes away is worth more than most upgrades. @paganoshdwtownecentre

Ashby Lumber — 824 Ashby Ave, Berkeley. A West Berkeley hardware and building-supply yard since 1968, stocked for framers, remodelers, and fence-and-deck jobs.

Pastime Hardware — 10057 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito. An El Cerrito Ace and a longtime neighborhood pick.

Ten for the punch list: Berkeley Ace, Laurel Ace, Truitt and White, Cole Hardware, Pete's Ace, Encinal True Value, Economy Lumber, Pagano's, plus Ashby Lumber and Pastime. Which counter has saved your weekend project?

item.title: East Bay Dog Parks
item.description: Point Isabel runs 23 acres of off-leash shoreline, by many counts the largest dog park in the country, and it is not even the only great one on this side o
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Dog Parks

Point Isabel runs 23 acres of off-leash shoreline, by many counts the largest dog park in the country, and it is not even the only great one on this side of the Bay. Eight East Bay dog parks where the off-leash crowd actually shows up.

Point Isabel Regional Shoreline — 2701 Isabel St, Richmond. Twenty-three acres of off-leash space with Bay views the whole way, and the Mudpuppy's dog wash right at the entrance. @ebrpd

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. A fully fenced enclosure open 6am to 10pm, the windiest park in the region, where the frisbee crowd lives on Saturdays.

Hardy Dog Park — 491 Hardy St, Oakland. Fenced and off-leash under the freeway, with separate small-dog and large-dog sections and a crowd that knows every dog by name.

Joaquin Miller Dog Park — Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. Two fenced sections in the hills, wooded and cooler in summer than the flatlands. Bring water, the spigot runs dry in the dry months.

Mountain View Cemetery — 5000 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Leashed only, open to walkers on the 1.8-mile paved loop with views back toward the Bay, and a quiet the dogs respond to. @mountainviewcemetery.oakland

Ohlone Dog Park — 1800 Hearst Ave, Berkeley. A fully fenced dog area with separate small-dog and big-dog sides on bark mulch, where Berkeley rescues get their first off-leash run.

Canine Corral at Hap Magee Ranch Park — 1025 La Gonda Way, Danville. An acre and a half in two sections with trail loops that connect, so the dog runs and you hike. Closed Tuesday mornings for maintenance.

Drigon Dog Park — 34666 7th St, Union City. Open Tuesday through Sunday, 6am to 10pm, with water stations and an obstacle course the dogs actually learn to work.

Eight for the off-leash run: Point Isabel, Cesar Chavez, Hardy, Joaquin Miller, Mountain View Cemetery, Ohlone, Hap Magee, and Drigon. Where does your dog run first?

item.title: East Bay Rainy-day Indoor Kids Spots
item.description: Children's Fairyland opened in 1950 and a young Walt Disney walked through it before he built Disneyland. When the rain hits and the kids are climbing the
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Rainy-day Indoor Kids Spots

Children's Fairyland opened in 1950 and a young Walt Disney walked through it before he built Disneyland. When the rain hits and the kids are climbing the walls by ten, these are the rooms that hold them. Six East Bay indoor spots built for small humans on a wet Saturday.

Habitot Children's Museum — 1569 Solano Ave, Berkeley. Hands-on exhibits for ages eight months to seven years; the waterworks station is where you lose track of time. Bring a change of clothes. @habitotmuseum

Children's Fairyland — 699 Bellevue Ave, Oakland. The original 1950 storybook park that inspired Disneyland; buy the magic key and the talking displays talk. @fairylandca

Lawrence Hall of Science — 1 Centennial Dr, Berkeley. Hands-on math and science with Bay views; park early on weekends, the lot fills by 10:30am. @thelawrencehallofscience

Chabot Space and Science Center — 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. A planetarium and telescope nights, with a science floor that saves the visit when the little ones lose the planetarium. @chabotspace

Adventure Playground — 160 University Ave, Berkeley. Free and city-run at the Marina, where kids hammer real nails and build forts out of scrap wood.

Pump It Up — 2995 Whipple Rd, Union City. An inflatable bounce arena with open-jump sessions; the late-morning slot is the move if the kid naps by one.

Six for the wet Saturday: Habitot, Children's Fairyland, Lawrence Hall, Chabot, Adventure Playground, and Pump It Up. Which one buys you the afternoon?

item.description: Earl Anthony's Dublin Bowl carries the name of the PBA legend who once managed it, forty lanes that go wide open on a weekend morning. When the kids are bo
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Bowling and Arcades

Earl Anthony's Dublin Bowl carries the name of the PBA legend who once managed it, forty lanes that go wide open on a weekend morning. When the kids are bored and the parks are used up, this is the three-hour fix. Five East Bay bowling alleys and arcades.

Earl Anthony's Dublin Bowl — 6750 Regional St, Dublin. Forty lanes named for the PBA legend who managed it; league nights are tight, weekend mornings wide open. @earlanthonysdublinbowl

Clayton Valley Bowl — 5300 Clayton Rd, Concord. Open daily to midnight, with cheap morning games and two-dollar late lanes Monday through Thursday.

High Scores Arcade — 1414 Park St, Alameda. Eighty classic cabinets, Galaga to Q*bert, all in original cabs on free play for one entry fee. @highscoresarcade

Pacific Pinball Museum — 1510 Webster St, Alameda. More than 100 playable machines from the 1940s on, all free play with one ticket; Tuesdays run two for one. @pacificpinball

Dave and Buster's — 2075 Diamond Blvd, Concord. Not local and not independent, but when it is raining and the kid wants flashing lights, the Wednesday family night works. @daveandbusters

Five for the boredom fix: Earl Anthony's, Clayton Valley Bowl, High Scores, Pacific Pinball, and Dave and Buster's. Which one wins the rainy Friday?

item.title: East Bay Scenic Drives
item.description: From the top of the Mount Diablo summit road, on a clear winter day, you can see the Sierra Nevada crest more than a hundred miles east. Some of the best E
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Scenic Drives

From the top of the Mount Diablo summit road, on a clear winter day, you can see the Sierra Nevada crest more than a hundred miles east. Some of the best East Bay views cost nothing but gas and a slow hour. Eight East Bay scenic drives locals run when they want the view without the hike.

Skyline Boulevard — Oakland Hills, Joaquin Miller Rd to Grizzly Peak. A ridge road with Bay views on one side and forest on the other; the pullouts are where the photo lives.

Grizzly Peak Boulevard — Berkeley and Oakland Hills. The climb to the ridge with sunset views over the Golden Gate, best in the orange hour from a parked car.

Niles Canyon Road — SR-84, Fremont to Sunol. Two-lane curves through oak woodland and the Alameda Creek watershed, along the old Transcontinental Railroad alignment. Notice the trestles.

Mount Diablo summit road — Mt Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. Eleven miles of switchbacks to the 3,849-foot summit; on a clear winter day the Sierra crest is visible. The drive is the destination.

Pinehurst Road — Canyon, between Moraga and Oakland. A narrow road under redwoods through the tiny Canyon community, tree canopy at golden hour that resets the week.

Wildcat Canyon Road — Berkeley Hills to San Pablo Dam Rd. Rolling open hills and grazing pasture that feel rural until you remember BART is 15 minutes back.

Old Tunnel Road — Berkeley Hills, near the Caldecott corridor. The original road through the hills before the tunnel, hairpins and view openings most commuters skip.

Highway 13 north — Through the Oakland Hills. The freeway becomes a wooded ridge drive past Joaquin Miller and Redwood Park.

Eight for the slow hour: Skyline, Grizzly Peak, Niles Canyon, the Mount Diablo summit, Pinehurst, Wildcat Canyon, Old Tunnel, and Highway 13. Which drive resets your week?

item.description: La Mediterranee has run its College Ave dining room since 1980, family-owned, the pomegranate chicken barely changed in forty years. For the table that wan
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Mediterranean and Greek

La Mediterranee has run its College Ave dining room since 1980, family-owned, the pomegranate chicken barely changed in forty years. For the table that wants olive oil, lemon, and lamb on a Tuesday night. Six East Bay Mediterranean and Greek spots locals keep in the rotation.

Zaytoon — 1133 Solano Ave, Albany. A Mediterranean spot and bar with hard-to-find Middle Eastern dishes, open Tuesday through Sunday; the mezze platter for two is the order. @zaytoon510

La Mediterranee — 2936 College Ave, Berkeley. Family-owned and running since 1980; the pomegranate chicken and the meza combo are why locals reorder. @cafelamed_berkeley

Wally's Cafe — 3900 San Pablo Ave, Emeryville. A no-frills Lebanese kitchen with a free bowl of lentil soup and baklava on every order; the lunch shawarma plate is the deal. @wallyscafe

Taza Mediterranean Grill — 1915 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. Counter service, charcoal-grilled meats, generous portions; the mixed grill is the order to share. @taza__mediterranean

Lavanta Mezze Bar — 599 Dutton Ave, San Leandro. A modern Greek-Mediterranean, mezze-forward menu; the lamb chops and the baklava cheesecake are the two to order. @lavanta_sanleandro

Fournos — 600 Dutton Ave Ste C, San Leandro. A family Greek kitchen with the moussaka and the lamb gyro that draw Tri-Valley regulars.

Six for the rotation: Zaytoon, La Mediterranee, Wally's, Taza, Lavanta, and Fournos. What is your standing Mediterranean order?

item.title: East Bay Public Libraries
item.description: The Berkeley and Oakland libraries both lend power tools, not just books, and most residents go years without finding out. Your card gets you into museums
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Public Libraries

The Berkeley and Oakland libraries both lend power tools, not just books, and most residents go years without finding out. Your card gets you into museums free too. Ten East Bay libraries with more going on than the checkout desk.

Berkeley Public Library — 2090 Kittredge St, Berkeley. The art deco landmark downtown, a reading room that makes you smarter just sitting in it, and a Saturday tool lending library most people never clock. @friendsbpl

Oakland Main Library — 125 14th St, Oakland. The flagship by the lake with the Oakland History Center upstairs, plus a Tool Lending Library and a Seed Library new residents miss for years. @oaklibrary

Lafayette Library and Learning Center — 3491 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. The 2009 stone and glass showpiece, half library and half community campus, and the Friday film series is the local secret.

Hayward Public Library — 888 C St, Hayward. The 21st Century building with a maker space, a recording booth, and a public tech lab, the branch built for right now. @haywardlibrary

Alameda Free Library — 1550 Oak St, Alameda. The island's main branch, a big light filled atrium and a kids floor that earns the bike ride across the estuary.

San Leandro Main Library — 300 Estudillo Ave, San Leandro. A freshly expanded children's wing, regular author talks, and a Friends bookstore in the basement for the bargain dig. @sanleandrolib

Rockridge Branch — 5366 College Ave, Oakland. Walk in study space and a steady author calendar, with a children's section that punches well above a branch its size.

Walnut Creek Library — 1644 N Broadway, Walnut Creek. The modern flagship beside Civic Park, floor to ceiling glass and a hold shelf that turns over fast.

Pleasanton Public Library — 400 Old Bernal Ave, Pleasanton. The summer reading program pulls the whole Tri-Valley in, and the local history room runs deeper than you would guess. @pleasantonlibandrec

Lakeview Branch — 550 El Embarcadero, Oakland. Storytimes for the under fives Tuesday and Saturday mornings, when the toddler crowd claims the rug early.

Ten branches worth the trip: Berkeley, Oakland Main, Lafayette, Hayward, Alameda, San Leandro, Rockridge, Walnut Creek, Pleasanton, and Lakeview. Which library program do you actually use?

item.description: The plot waitlists at East Bay community gardens run 6 to 12 months, and the volunteer days have regulars who have shown up for years. City Slicker Farms t
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Community Gardens

The plot waitlists at East Bay community gardens run 6 to 12 months, and the volunteer days have regulars who have shown up for years. City Slicker Farms turned a West Oakland lot into a whole farm park. Six East Bay community gardens that mean more than they look.

City Slicker Farms — 2847 Peralta St, Oakland. A West Oakland farm park and community garden with a free Saturday farm stand and volunteer days for first-timers. @cityslickerfarms

Spiral Gardens — 2850 Sacramento St, Berkeley. A community garden, nursery, and produce stand with weekly volunteer hours Tuesday and Saturday. @spiralgardensofficial

Karl Linn Community Garden — Peralta Ave at Hopkins St, Berkeley. One of the original neighborhood gardens, with open community workdays the first Sunday of the month.

Peralta Community Garden — 1400 Peralta Ave, Berkeley. A lush plot-share garden next to Karl Linn, built and tended by neighbors.

People's Grocery Garden — 3501 San Pablo Ave, West Oakland. A food-justice garden at the California Hotel greenhouse, with community workdays that welcome first-time volunteers. @peoples_grocery

Edible Schoolyard — MLK Jr Middle School, 1781 Rose St, Berkeley. Alice Waters' one-acre teaching garden, with public tours and volunteer days you sign up for on the calendar.

Six gardens that give back: City Slicker, Spiral Gardens, Karl Linn, Peralta, People's Grocery, and the Edible Schoolyard. What is your local growing space?

item.title: East Bay Sichuan and Hunan
item.description: If your idea of Sichuan food is sweet sauce and no numb, you have been eating the mall version. The peppercorn is supposed to buzz. Five East Bay kitchens
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sichuan and Hunan

If your idea of Sichuan food is sweet sauce and no numb, you have been eating the mall version. The peppercorn is supposed to buzz. Five East Bay kitchens that bring the mala heat properly, Oakland to Pleasant Hill.

Spices 3 — 370 12th St, Oakland. A Szechuan specialist in Oakland Chinatown; the dan dan noodles, mapo tofu, and dry-fried green beans are the table orders. @spicesthreeoakland

Chengdu Style Restaurant — 2600 Bancroft Way, Berkeley. A Sichuan kitchen where the Chengdu cold noodles and the boiled beef in red sauce bring real heat.

China Village — 1335 Solano Ave, Albany. A Michelin-listed Szechuan institution on Solano; the dry-braised dishes and the mala plates are why it stays packed.

Sichuan Fortune House — 41 Woodsworth Ln, Pleasant Hill. A longtime Contra Costa Sichuan favorite; the mapo tofu and the cumin lamb are the standing orders.

Easterly Hunan Cuisine — 2323 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The sister heat, Hunan-style, with smoked-pork dishes and a dry pot the Sichuan crowd appreciates.

Five for the peppercorn: Spices 3, Chengdu Style, China Village, Sichuan Fortune House, and Easterly for the Hunan side. What is your standing mala order?

item.title: East Bay Tide Pools Worth the Drive
item.description: The East Bay's own tide pools sit right at Crown Beach in Alameda, and the deeper ones are a short drive over the hill to the San Mateo coast. Time it to a
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Tide Pools Worth the Drive

The East Bay's own tide pools sit right at Crown Beach in Alameda, and the deeper ones are a short drive over the hill to the San Mateo coast. Time it to a minus tide and the kids forget the iPad exists. Eight tide-pool spots, from the Alameda shoreline out to the coast.

Crown Memorial State Beach — 8th St and Otis Dr, Alameda. The East Bay's most accessible tide pools, beginner-friendly with parking right at the sand. Best at minus tides.

Crab Cove Visitor Center — 1252 McKay Ave, Alameda. Next to Crown Beach, with staff-led tide-pool walks on low-tide weekends.

Point Pinole Regional Shoreline — 5551 Giant Hwy, Richmond. A long shoreline with rocky pockets and far fewer crowds than the Alameda spots. Bring water shoes. @ebrpd

Pillar Point — 1 Johnson Pier, Half Moon Bay. Worth the 45-minute drive; the pools are deeper and the variety bigger. Minus-tide weekends are the move.

Fitzgerald Marine Reserve — 200 Nevada Ave, Moss Beach. Among the most famous tide pools in the region, with ranger-led walks on weekends.

Bean Hollow State Beach — 11000 Cabrillo Hwy, Pescadero. Smaller and less crowded, with rock formations that make it the photo stop.

Pescadero State Beach — Cabrillo Hwy, Pescadero. Tide pools south of the main beach; pair it with Pescadero Marsh for a half-day.

Ano Nuevo State Park — 1 New Years Creek Rd, Pescadero. Tide pools plus elephant seals in season; the guided walks December through March are the trip to plan around.

Eight for the minus tide: Crown Beach, Crab Cove, Point Pinole, Pillar Point, Fitzgerald, Bean Hollow, Pescadero, and Ano Nuevo. Pack water shoes and a tide app. What did your kid find last time?

item.title: East Bay Mural Walks
item.description: The Richmond Greenway hides three miles of murals, a fresh one about every quarter mile, where the bike route doubles as the art route. The best East Bay a
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Mural Walks

The Richmond Greenway hides three miles of murals, a fresh one about every quarter mile, where the bike route doubles as the art route. The best East Bay art is not behind a gallery door. Eight East Bay mural walks where the walls do the curating.

Downtown Oakland murals — Broadway and Telegraph, Downtown Oakland. Dozens of pieces across the Art Murmur core; the First Friday walk is the way to see them.

Lake Merritt — Around Lake Merritt, Oakland. Murals and public art along the three-mile pedestrian loop, refreshed as new artists are commissioned.

Mandela Parkway — Mandela Pkwy, West Oakland. The West Oakland corridor of community murals, walkable from West Oakland BART.

Fruitvale — International Blvd, Fruitvale District, Oakland. Decades of Latino and Chicano muralism along the International corridor, some of it dating back generations.

Telegraph and People's Park — Telegraph Ave to Dwight Way, Berkeley. A concentrated stretch of Berkeley street art with People's Park as the historic anchor.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. Ever-changing community art on driftwood and concrete, best on a sunset walk, open dawn to dusk.

Emeryville Greenway — Horton St and the Bay Street area, Emeryville. Rotating public art along the greenway, easy to combine with the marina walk.

Richmond Greenway — Richmond Greenway rail-trail, Richmond. Three miles of murals every quarter mile, where the bike route doubles as the art route.

Eight walks where the walls do the curating: Downtown Oakland, Lake Merritt, Mandela Parkway, Fruitvale, Berkeley's Telegraph, the Albany Bulb, the Emeryville Greenway, and the Richmond Greenway. Which mural stops you every time?

item.title: East Bay Book Clubs
item.description: The East Bay runs on independent bookstores, and most of them host a book club you can just walk into. Marcus Books, the oldest Black-owned bookstore in th
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Book Clubs

The East Bay runs on independent bookstores, and most of them host a book club you can just walk into. Marcus Books, the oldest Black-owned bookstore in the country, is one of them. Six East Bay book clubs that welcome new members.

Pegasus Books — 1855 Solano Ave, Berkeley. A rotating club runs out of the Solano store; the schedule is on their site and the first meeting is walk-in friendly. @pegasusbooks

East Bay Booksellers — 6022 College Ave, Oakland. Multiple genre clubs, literary fiction, mystery, and BIPOC voices, meeting monthly with sign-up at the counter. @eastbaybooksellers

Marcus Books — 3900 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Oakland. The oldest Black-owned bookstore in the country, with regular author events and discussion groups on the calendar. @marcus.books

Friends of the Berkeley Public Library — 2090 Kittredge St, Berkeley. A free, library-hosted club that meets monthly, selections rotating through staff picks and member nominations. @friendsbpl

Diesel, A Bookstore — 5433 College Ave, Oakland. Multiple genre clubs and rotating author conversations; the fiction club has a real waitlist for a seat. @dieselabookstore

Mrs — Dalloway's. 2904 College Ave, Berkeley. An Elmwood shop with garden-themed and literary-fiction clubs and a writer-in-residence series. @mrsdallowaysberkeley

Six clubs with an open seat: Pegasus, East Bay Booksellers, Marcus, Friends of Berkeley, Diesel, and Mrs. Dalloway's. What are you reading right now?

item.title: East Bay Group Activity Spots
item.description: When nobody in the group can agree on dinner, the fix is an activity that does the deciding for you. The East Bay has axe lanes, go-kart tracks, and Japane
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Group Activity Spots

When nobody in the group can agree on dinner, the fix is an activity that does the deciding for you. The East Bay has axe lanes, go-kart tracks, and Japanese entertainment complexes that solve the whole night. Five East Bay group-activity spots for when the vote is deadlocked.

Bay Area Axe Throwing — 2510 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Multi-lane axe throwing with coaching for first-timers and league play for regulars, group rates for six or more.

K1 Speed — 6400 Sierra Ct, Dublin. Indoor electric go-kart racing up to 45 mph, plus an arcade and a lounge; the Italian karts are the draw.

Round1 — 185 Sunvalley Mall, Concord. A 50,000-square-foot Japanese entertainment complex, bowling, karaoke, arcade, darts, and ping pong, open to 2am.

Lucky Strike Alameda — 300 Park St, Alameda. The former Bowlero on Park Street, bowling plus arcade plus a sports bar in the back.

Harvest Park Bowl — 5000 Balfour Rd, Brentwood. Thirty-two lanes out in east county, the group move when half the crew is coming from Antioch or Brentwood.

Five for the deadlocked vote: Bay Area Axe Throwing, K1 Speed, Round1, Lucky Strike Alameda, and Harvest Park Bowl. What activity earns your standing group booking?

item.title: East Bay Escape Rooms
item.description: Red Door in Concord runs nine escape-room experiences under one roof, its most interactive to date. Most of what the aggregators list around it does not ac
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Escape Rooms

Red Door in Concord runs nine escape-room experiences under one roof, its most interactive to date. Most of what the aggregators list around it does not actually exist. Five real East Bay escape rooms worth the booking.

Escape Oakland — 522 7th St, Oakland. A downtown Oakland room with story-driven puzzles, open Wednesday through Sunday, good for first-timers and teams.

Clockwise Escape Room — 1720 Broadway, Oakland. Second-floor downtown rooms with a linear plot; the detective and heist themes are the regulars' rebooks.

Diablo Escapes — 1948 Mt Diablo Blvd, Walnut Creek. A Walnut Creek spot open late Friday and Saturday, mid-difficulty rooms that suit mixed groups.

Red Door Escape Room — 2075 Diamond Blvd, Concord. Nine experiences inside the Veranda in Concord, their most interactive rooms to date.

Clockwise Pleasanton — 4713 First St, Pleasanton. Clockwise's Tri-Valley location downtown, the option when the group is coming from the 680 side.

Five for the booking: Escape Oakland, Clockwise in Oakland, Diablo Escapes, Red Door in Concord, and Clockwise in Pleasanton. What is the hardest room you ever solved?

item.title: East Bay Wildflower Spots
item.description: Black Diamond Mines has 158 recorded wildflower species, and it is one of eight East Bay ridges that light up when the spring bloom hits, usually April int
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Wildflower Spots

Black Diamond Mines has 158 recorded wildflower species, and it is one of eight East Bay ridges that light up when the spring bloom hits, usually April into May. Most people drive right past the trailheads. Eight East Bay wildflower spots to catch the spring bloom.

Sunol Regional Wilderness — 1895 Geary Rd, Sunol. Flag Hill Trail above the visitor center holds California poppy and lupine into mid-May; weekday mornings beat the heat. @ebrpd

Mount Diablo State Park — 96 Mitchell Canyon Rd, Clayton. Mitchell Canyon into Deer Flat is shaded and shows globe lilies, Chinese houses, and Ithuriel's spear in spring. @castateparks

Black Diamond Mines — 5175 Somersville Rd, Antioch. Stewartville Trail carries bush poppy and Mt. Diablo globe tulip late into May, with 158 wildflower species recorded.

Mission Peak — Stanford Ave staging area, Fremont. The Hidden Valley Trail is lined with poppies and lupine in spring; go at dawn to dodge the permit-parking crush.

Pleasanton Ridge — 9895 Foothill Rd, Pleasanton. Checkerbloom and shooting stars hold through May along the Bay Leaf Trail, with the newer Tyler Ranch lands stretching the season.

Vargas Plateau — 2536 Morrison Canyon Rd, Fremont. Upland grassland that stays cooler than the valley floor, with poppies, sun cup, and blue-eyed grass along the Golden Eagle Trail.

Sibley Volcanic Preserve — 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. The Volcanic Trail loop turns up monkeyflower and pennyroyal in the wind-shaded volcanic bowls.

Tilden Regional Park — Quarry Trail off Wildcat Canyon Rd, Berkeley. Poppies, silver lupine, and California buttercup run through mid-May; park at the Quarry picnic site.

Eight for the spring bloom: Sunol, Mount Diablo, Black Diamond Mines, Mission Peak, Pleasanton Ridge, Vargas Plateau, Sibley, and Tilden. Where did you find your favorite bloom?

item.title: East Bay Run Clubs
item.description: You do not finish your first 10K alone. The East Bay has running clubs going back to 1977 where the beginner pace is the point and the long-run regulars kn
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Run Clubs

You do not finish your first 10K alone. The East Bay has running clubs going back to 1977 where the beginner pace is the point and the long-run regulars know your name by week three. Eight East Bay run clubs that welcome the first-timer.

Lake Merritt Joggers and Striders — Lake Merritt, Oakland. A nonprofit club since 1977 that runs a beginning-running program plus sliding-scale races around the lake. @lmjs_run

Berkeley Running Club — Berkeley Marina. Tuesday 7am from the waterfront, splitting into pace groups, walkers welcome, coffee after.

Women's Run Club East Bay — Oakland and rotating East Bay. A come-as-you-are women's club with weekday Oakland runs and weekend long runs. @wrceastbay

East Bay Front Runners and Walkers — Lakeside Dr, Oakland. An LGBTQ+ club meeting Saturday mornings, with 2-to-8-mile runs and 1-to-4-mile walk options. @ebfrw

Oakland Track Club — Lake Merritt, Oakland. Multiple weekly runs across all paces; Strava is the easiest way to catch which run is happening when. @oaklandtrackclub

November Project Oakland — Lake Merritt Boating Center, Oakland. A free Wednesday 6:30am workout, with the last Wednesday of the month on the Cleveland Cascade stairs. @novemberprojectoakland

Bay Bandits — Skyline Gate, Redwood Regional Park, Oakland. A trail crew meeting Monday evenings at Redwood, plus rotating Thursday and Saturday runs. @baybandits

Trail Sisters East Bay — Berkeley and Tilden hills. A volunteer-led no-drop women's trail group with 6:30am Berkeley meetups. @trailsisters_eastbay

Eight clubs that welcome week one: Lake Merritt Joggers, Berkeley Running Club, Women's Run Club, East Bay Front Runners, Oakland Track Club, November Project, Bay Bandits, and Trail Sisters. Which club did you start with?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Tattoo Studios
item.description: Serious collectors do not pick a tattoo shop by walking past it, they travel for the artist. Temple Tattoo on Telegraph has been Freddy Corbin's institutio
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Tattoo Studios

Serious collectors do not pick a tattoo shop by walking past it, they travel for the artist. Temple Tattoo on Telegraph has been Freddy Corbin's institution for decades. Eight East Bay studios worth the appointment.

Premium Tattoo — 4130 Broadway, Oakland. A custom appointment shop since 2008 with a deep bench of artists and rotating walk-in flash days. @premiumtattoooakland

Temple Tattoo — 4228 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Freddy Corbin's institution; black-and-grey lettering and religious iconography are the house specialty. @templetattoo13

Old Crow Tattoo — 2812 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. An award-winning shop with rotating guest artists across blackwork, botanical, and ornamental. @oldcrowtattoo

Dark Water — 2035 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. An appointment-only atelier known for fine-line and blackout work, with lead artists booked months out. @darkwater.ink

Studio Noir — 471B 9th St, Oakland. A woman-owned Old Oakland collective doing custom traditional plus permanent cosmetics and piercings, walk-ins welcome. @studionoiroakland

East Bay Tattoo — 516 E 18th St, Oakland. Joe Parker and Barnaby Williams, heavy on Traditional Japanese and Neotraditional, walk-ins welcome. @eastbaytattoo

Sacred Rose Tattoo — 1960 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. Woman-owned since 1998, a bench of artists with art degrees, walk-ins 12 to 8 daily. @sacredrosetattoo

Zebra Tattoo and Piercing — Walnut Creek. A Bay Area institution since 1984; the Walnut Creek piercing counter is a regional destination for jewelry. @zebratattoos

Eight worth the appointment: Premium, Temple, Old Crow, Dark Water, Studio Noir, East Bay Tattoo, Sacred Rose, and Zebra. What was your first piece, and where?

item.title: East Bay Stargazing Spots
item.description: The Mount Diablo Astronomical Society runs free public star parties on the summit most months, and 90 minutes past it there are dark-sky spots where the Mi
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Stargazing Spots

The Mount Diablo Astronomical Society runs free public star parties on the summit most months, and 90 minutes past it there are dark-sky spots where the Milky Way shows up with the naked eye. Eight stargazing spots, from the East Bay hills out to the dark-sky drives.

Mount Diablo State Park — 96 Mitchell Canyon Rd, Clayton. The Mount Diablo Astronomical Society runs free public star parties monthly, March through October. Bring a chair. @castateparks

Chabot Space and Science Center — 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. Free Friday and Saturday telescope viewing on the observation deck, 7:30 to 10:30pm. Check the weather page first. @chabotspace

Del Valle Regional Park — 7000 Del Valle Rd, Livermore. The Tri-Valley Stargazers' permanent observing site, with a dark south view and almost no light pollution. @ebrpd

Lick Observatory — 7281 Mt Hamilton Rd, Mount Hamilton. Public evening tours and Music of the Spheres run through 2026 while the historic dome is repaired; book on Eventbrite. @lickobservatory

Mount Tamalpais Astronomy Program — Mountain Theater, Mill Valley. A free Saturday-night talk, then amateur astronomers wheel scopes into Rock Spring, April through October.

Henry W — Coe State Park. 9100 E Dunne Ave, Morgan Hill. The reserved Hunting Hollow astronomy lot is one of the darkest accessible spots in the greater Bay Area. @henrywcoesp

Pinnacles National Park — 5000 Hwy 146, Paicines. A designated Dark Sky Park; the day-use area behind the campground store has the cleanest horizon. @pinnaclesnps

Point Reyes National Seashore — Lighthouse end, Point Reyes. The closer you park to the lighthouse, the darker it gets, just under 90 minutes out on a clear night. @pointreyesnps

Eight for the Milky Way: Mount Diablo, Chabot, Del Valle, Lick Observatory, Mount Tam, Henry Coe, Pinnacles, and Point Reyes. When did you last see the Milky Way?

item.title: East Bay Specialty Grocers
item.description: There is a Japanese market on San Pablo Avenue in Berkeley that has hand-cut sashimi-grade fish since 1962, and most East Bay shoppers walk right past it f
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Specialty Grocers

There is a Japanese market on San Pablo Avenue in Berkeley that has hand-cut sashimi-grade fish since 1962, and most East Bay shoppers walk right past it for the chain. Eleven East Bay specialty grocers worth the rotation.

99 Ranch Market — 34444 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. The flagship East Bay store, with the biggest pan-Asian seafood counter and a live tank. @99ranchmarket

KP Asian Market — 2370 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. An East Bay Korean institution since 1973, formerly Koreana Plaza; the banchan counter and hard-to-find Japanese brands are the draw. @kp_oakland

Vik's Market — 2390 4th St, Berkeley. The Indian grocer attached to Vik's Chaat, with fresh paneer, spices, and snacks alongside the famous chaat house. @viksmarketberkeley

New India Bazar — 5113 Mowry Ave, Fremont. A South Asian one-stop with Pakistani and Sri Lankan staples plus fresh produce daily. @new_india_bazar

Apna Bazar — 41081 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. An Indian grocer known for the in-store snack and sweets counter and weekly produce drops. @apnabazarmarket

Supermercado Mi Tierra — 2758 Fruitvale Ave, Oakland. A Ramirez-family market since 1998, with a full carniceria and a fresh tortilleria daily. @supermercadomitierra_

Middle East Food Market — 4097 Peralta Blvd, Fremont. A halal market with a Muslim-owned in-house bakery turning out fresh Arabic pastries and pita daily.

Island Pacific Supermarket — 4122 Dyer St, Union City. A Filipino grocer with a hot-food counter, lechon, and a deep seafood selection. @islandpacificmarket

Tokyo Fish Market — 1220 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A Japanese grocery and seafood market with sashimi-grade fish and a deli. @tokyofishmarket

Berkeley Bowl — 2020 Oregon St, Berkeley. The legendary produce and grocery hall with a variety no chain matches.

Monterey Market — 1550 Hopkins St, Berkeley. A North Berkeley produce institution with the deepest fruit-and-vegetable bins in the Bay.

Eleven for the rotation: 99 Ranch, KP Asian, Vik's, New India Bazar, Apna, Mi Tierra, Middle East Food, Island Pacific, plus Tokyo Fish, Berkeley Bowl, and Monterey Market. Where do you shop for the hard-to-find?

item.title: East Bay Fishing Spots
item.description: There is a 315-acre stocked lake 30 minutes from downtown Oakland that takes a fresh load of trout on a schedule, and most Bay Area anglers have never wet
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Fishing Spots

There is a 315-acre stocked lake 30 minutes from downtown Oakland that takes a fresh load of trout on a schedule, and most Bay Area anglers have never wet a line in it. Eight East Bay fishing spots worth the rod.

Lake Chabot — 17936 Lake Chabot Rd, Castro Valley. A 315-acre stocked lake with rod and boat rentals at the marina; trout in the cool months, catfish in summer.

Point Pinole Pier — 5551 Giant Hwy, Richmond. A long pier with shuttle service from the lot; striped bass and sturgeon in fall, jacksmelt and perch year-round. @ebrpd

Lake Del Valle — 7000 Del Valle Rd, Livermore. The best trout action is the southwest end from the marina down to West Swim Beach; shore casters do well off the West Shore dock.

San Pablo Reservoir — 7301 San Pablo Dam Rd, El Sobrante. EBMUD's standout trout fishery, with weekly stockings and boat rentals onsite.

Lafayette Reservoir — 3849 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A 126-acre EBMUD reservoir, trout-heavy winter through spring, with rowboat and pedal-boat rentals at the dock.

Shadow Cliffs — 2500 Stanley Blvd, Pleasanton. An old Kaiser gravel quarry stocked weekly, trout in the cool months and catfish in summer, shore-fishable all the way around.

Big Break Pier — 69 Big Break Rd, Oakley. A 100-foot Delta pier for largemouth and striped bass plus the occasional sturgeon; a California fishing license is required.

Robert W — Crown Memorial State Beach. Alameda. Surfperch, jacksmelt, and the occasional striper from the shoreline; fish the incoming tide near the Crab Cove groin.

Eight for the rod: Lake Chabot, Point Pinole, Del Valle, San Pablo Reservoir, Lafayette Reservoir, Shadow Cliffs, Big Break, and Crown Beach. Where do you fish?

item.description: Sunday self-care should not mean a 90-minute scroll for a bad chair massage. Piedmont Springs has rented private outdoor hot tubs and a Finnish sauna on Pi
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Day Spas

Sunday self-care should not mean a 90-minute scroll for a bad chair massage. Piedmont Springs has rented private outdoor hot tubs and a Finnish sauna on Piedmont Ave since 1981. Six East Bay spas worth the actual splurge.

Piedmont Springs — 3939 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Private outdoor hot tubs, a Finnish sauna, and a steam room since 1981, the original urban oasis. @piedmont_springs

The Spa at the Claremont — 41 Tunnel Rd, Berkeley. A Forbes-rated spa inside the historic resort; the eucalyptus steam and a pool day pass are the signature. @claremontresort

Lafayette Park Hotel, Spa at the Park — 3287 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A chateau-style adults-only spa with outdoor pool and hot-tub access included with treatments.

Rockridge Day Spa — 5413 College Ave, Oakland. A full-service house of facials, massage, and salon, a multi-time Best of Oakland winner. @rockridgedayspa

Cocoon Day Spa — 5377 College Ave, Oakland. The Rockridge spot for couples massage and waxing, with the back-to-back combo booking most weekends. @cocoon_spa

Kume Float and Cryo — 584 Grand Ave, Oakland. Sensory-deprivation float tanks plus cryo, infrared sauna, and red light, Oakland's recovery destination. @kume_float

Six for the splurge: Piedmont Springs, the Claremont, Lafayette Park Hotel, Rockridge Day Spa, Cocoon, and Kume Float. Where do you book first?

item.title: East Bay Rec Leagues
item.description: The adult who joins a rec league at 32 makes more new friends in eight weeks than in the previous two years. The East Bay has leagues with open sign-ups an
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Rec Leagues

The adult who joins a rec league at 32 makes more new friends in eight weeks than in the previous two years. The East Bay has leagues with open sign-ups and a beginner division that actually means it. Seven East Bay rec leagues taking new players this season.

Bay Area Adult Soccer League — Tom Bates Sports Complex, Berkeley. Eleven-a-side coed and eight-a-side futsal, community-first, all skill levels welcome.

East Bay Over Thirty Soccer — Estuary Park, 200 Mosley Ave, Alameda. A coed rec league since 2003 for men 30-plus and women 21-plus, Saturday-morning games, fun over competition. @ebots_soccer

Neighborhood Sports Club — 100 Second St, Oakland. A Jack London soccer cafe and small-sided pitch with a Community league and drop-in matches, opened in 2026.

Bay Area Disc Association — Gilman Fields, Berkeley. A nonprofit running adult ultimate frisbee leagues, tournaments, and pickup all over the East Bay. @bayareadisc

Walnut Creek Adult Softball — Heather Farm Park, 301 N San Carlos Dr, Walnut Creek. Running since 1976, with over-40, men's, and coed competitive plus rec divisions.

Oakland Parks and Recreation — Citywide, Oakland. The city department running adult basketball and softball at neighborhood centers, the cheapest entry into organized play. @oakparksrec

Berkeley YMCA — 2001 Allston Way, Berkeley. Pickup basketball, pickleball open play, and member-organized league signups downtown near BART.

Seven leagues taking players: Bay Area Adult Soccer, East Bay Over Thirty, Neighborhood Sports Club, Bay Area Disc, Walnut Creek Softball, Oakland Parks and Rec, and the Berkeley YMCA. What are you signing up for?

item.title: East Bay Public Golf Courses
item.description: There is a public course on the San Leandro shoreline where the SF skyline is visible from every hole, and most East Bay residents have never teed it up. E
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Public Golf Courses

There is a public course on the San Leandro shoreline where the SF skyline is visible from every hole, and most East Bay residents have never teed it up. Eight East Bay public courses worth the round.

Lake Chabot Golf Course — 11450 Golf Links Rd, Oakland. A 27-hole muni in the Oakland Hills with Bay Bridge views and a disc-golf overlay on the same fairways. @lakechabotgolf

Tilden Park Golf Course — 10 Golf Course Dr, Berkeley. A 1937 WPA-built course winding through eucalyptus and pine, regarded as the best 18-hole value in the East Bay. @tildenparkgolf

Metropolitan Golf Links — 10051 Doolittle Dr, Oakland. A public links-style course by the airport with constant breeze, pot bunkers, and planes overhead the whole round. @playmetro

Corica Park — 1 Clubhouse Memorial Rd, Alameda. The South Course is a Rees Jones links ranked among the top municipal courses in America, plus a newer North Course. @coricapark

Boundary Oak — 3800 Valley Vista Rd, Walnut Creek. The most-played course in the East Bay at 65,000 rounds a year, 7,000-plus yards of rolling oak fairways under Mount Diablo. @boundaryoakgolfcourse

Callippe Preserve — 8500 Clubhouse Dr, Pleasanton. A course routed through a nature preserve of native grasses and wildflowers, with regular wild-turkey sightings. @playcallippe

Diablo Creek — 4050 Port Chicago Hwy, Concord. An affordable Concord muni with a covered, lighted driving range that stays open after sunset. @diablo_creek_golf

Monarch Bay Golf Club — 13800 Monarch Bay Dr, San Leandro. A John Harbottle Scottish links on the marina shoreline, the one with the SF skyline from every hole. @monarchbaygolfclub

Eight for the round: Lake Chabot, Tilden Park, Metropolitan, Corica Park, Boundary Oak, Callippe, Diablo Creek, and Monarch Bay. Where do you tee up?

item.title: East Bay Antique Stores
item.description: The Alameda Point Antiques Faire runs 800-plus vetted dealers on the old naval air station the first Sunday of every month, the largest antiques show in No
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Antique Stores

The Alameda Point Antiques Faire runs 800-plus vetted dealers on the old naval air station the first Sunday of every month, the largest antiques show in Northern California. And it is not the only place to dig. Eight East Bay antique stores worth the Saturday.

Alameda Point Antiques Faire — 2900 Navy Way, Alameda. The largest antiques show in Northern California, 800-plus dealers with everything 20-plus years old, the first Sunday monthly. @alamedaantiquesfaire

Toy Safari — 1410 Park St, Alameda. A family-owned institution since 1992, floor-to-ceiling vintage and collectible toys alongside new product. @toysafaritoys

Antique Center — 6519 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A fixture since 1947 with a constantly rotating inventory of furniture, jewelry, and clothing sourced globally. @theantiquecenter

Mixed Pickles Antiques — 6395 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Wednesday-to-Saturday shop of repurposed vintage, clothing alongside antique home goods. @mixedpicklesantiques

Talisman Antiques — 6007 College Ave, Oakland. A shop since 1994 known for Japanese tansu chests, early American furniture, and handpicked vintage jewelry. @talismantiques

Lost in the Attic — 37663 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A Niles district gem of rotating jewelry, antique dishes, board games, and small ephemera. @lost_in_the_attic_fremont

Mantiques — 37671 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A Niles Blvd co-op with 100,000-plus items spanning vintage toys, comics, records, and oddities. @mantiquesbayarea

Antique Corner — 500 Ferry St, Martinez. A downtown Martinez shop of autographed cards, retro matchbooks, crystals, and bold costume jewelry.

Eight for the dig: the Alameda Point Faire, Toy Safari, Antique Center, Mixed Pickles, Talisman, Lost in the Attic, Mantiques, and Antique Corner. What did you bring home from your last dig?

item.title: East Bay Paint and Pottery Studios
item.description: Clayroom in Oakland runs open wheel-throwing rooms and six-week courses for anyone who wants clay under their nails by Friday. A creative block does not al
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Paint and Pottery Studios

Clayroom in Oakland runs open wheel-throwing rooms and six-week courses for anyone who wants clay under their nails by Friday. A creative block does not always need another screen, sometimes a brush and a glass of wine. Six East Bay paint-and-pottery night spots.

Color Me Mine — 2205 South Shore Center, Alameda. A paint-your-own-pottery studio with hundreds of bisque shapes and dozens of glazes, big on handprint keepsakes. @cmmalameda

Color Me Mine — 350 Main St, Pleasanton. The downtown studio that runs adult Sip and Paint nights alongside the kid pottery painting. @cmmpleasanton

Pinot's Palette — 153 S L St, Livermore. A Tri-Valley paint-and-sip on First Street, BYO wine from the neighboring tasting rooms. @pinotspalette_livermore

The Hot Spot Studios — 39111 Paseo Padre Pkwy, Fremont. A no-studio-fee craft studio with pottery painting plus candle making, mosaics, and succulent gardening under one roof. @thehotspotfremont

Clayroom — 4268 Broadway, Oakland. A community wheel-throwing and hand-building studio with six-week courses, one-time classes, and memberships. @clayroomoakland

Studio One Art Center — 365 45th St, Oakland. A City of Oakland art center in a renovated 1920s building, drop-in ceramics and sculpture for all ages.

Six for the creative night: Color Me Mine in Alameda and Pleasanton, Pinot's Palette, the Hot Spot, Clayroom, and Studio One. Where do you create?

item.title: East Bay Mini-golf and Family Fun
item.description: Subpar in Alameda built a 19-hole indoor mini-golf course where every hole is a tribute to a different East Bay landmark. The rainy Saturday with the kids
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Mini-golf and Family Fun

Subpar in Alameda built a 19-hole indoor mini-golf course where every hole is a tribute to a different East Bay landmark. The rainy Saturday with the kids does not have to be another screen. Six East Bay mini-golf and family fun spots.

Boomers Livermore — 2400 Kitty Hawk Rd, Livermore. A full outdoor fun park with go-karts, two 18-hole mini-golf courses, bumper boats, and a big arcade. @boomerslivermore

Subpar Miniature Golf — 1600 Park St, Alameda. A 19-hole indoor handmade course where every hole is a tribute to a different East Bay landmark, arcade and snack bar attached. @subparminigolf

Tipsy Putt — 5690 Bay St, Emeryville. Indoor nine-hole mini golf with a sports bar and a casual menu, family-welcoming before 6pm. @tipsyputteb

Putter's Country Club — 1275 S California Blvd, Walnut Creek. An outdoor 24-hole handmade course, low-tech and beloved for kids' birthdays. @putterscountryclub

Pixieland Amusement Park — 2740 E Olivera Rd, Concord. A tiny-tot outdoor amusement park in Willow Pass Park since 1955, with the preschool-sized Dragon Roller Coaster. @pixielandamusementpark

Rockin' Jump — 1631 Challenge Dr, Concord. A trampoline park with a stunt bag, a dodgeball arena, and a dedicated little-jumper area for kids six and under. @rockinjump_concord

Six for the family day: Boomers, Subpar, Tipsy Putt, Putter's, Pixieland, and Rockin' Jump. Where do you take the kids?

item.title: East Bay Florists Who Deliver
item.description: Lee's has run its own Berkeley flower shop since 1946 and still delivers same day if you call before eleven. Most people default to the same chain bouquet
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Florists Who Deliver

Lee's has run its own Berkeley flower shop since 1946 and still delivers same day if you call before eleven. Most people default to the same chain bouquet everyone else sends. Ten East Bay florists who build the arrangement for your moment.

J — Miller Flowers. 4416 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Third generation and sixty plus years on the avenue, the shop that knows the difference between Tuesday flowers and Sunday flowers.

Lee's Florist and Nursery — 1420 University Ave, Berkeley. Family run since 1946, same day across Berkeley if you order before eleven, short hours and a long memory. @leesflorist

Wisteria — 6307 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge boutique of made to order arrangements, delivering across Oakland, Berkeley, Piedmont, and Emeryville. @wisteriarockridge

Naho's Floral Design — 7080 Westmoorland Dr, Berkeley. Refined Japanese aesthetic bouquets, same day from Berkeley out to Lafayette, Moraga, and Walnut Creek. @nahos_floral

Red Bud Florals — 1652 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A green certified studio that refuses plastic and floral foam, daily runs across the inner East Bay. @red_bud_florals

Seulberger's Florist — 562 14th St, Oakland. The downtown Oakland institution, weekday mornings to four, the office delivery veterans who have seen every occasion.

Florali — 2345 Boulevard Cir, Walnut Creek. A second generation shop with its own flower farm, seasonal arrangements that look like they were just cut. @florali

Forget Me Not Flowers and Gifts — 1402 N Main St, Walnut Creek. Family owned with same day Walnut Creek delivery and reliable Lamorinda runs.

Floral Arts Florist — 3584 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A veteran family florist serving Lamorinda since 1970, the corridor's most established. @floralartslafayette

Flower Bowl Florist — 2325 Boulevard Cir, Walnut Creek. A Boulevard Circle shop with dependable same day across central Contra Costa.

Ten who deliver: J. Miller, Lee's, Wisteria, Naho's, Red Bud, Seulberger's, Florali, Forget Me Not, Floral Arts, and Flower Bowl. Tell them the moment, not the flowers.

item.title: East Bay Comic Shops
item.description: The comic shop you walk past on Sunday is also where the local D&D campaign meets on Wednesday. The East Bay has eight with a real weekly-events calendar.
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Comic Shops

The comic shop you walk past on Sunday is also where the local D&D campaign meets on Wednesday. The East Bay has eight with a real weekly-events calendar. Eight East Bay comic shops worth the pull list.

Dr — Comics and Mr. Games. 4014 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. A Piedmont Ave shop since 1988 pairing a full comics inventory with board games and weekly Magic and tabletop events. @drcomicsmrgames

Cape and Cowl Comics — 1601 Clay St, Oakland. An Eisner Spirit of Retail winner running Drink and Draws, signings, book clubs, and its own con. @capecowlcomics

Fantastic Comics — 1708A Martin Luther King Jr Way, Berkeley. A downtown shop with an outsized graphic-novel section and a dedicated New Comic Day push. @fantasticcomics

The Escapist Comic Bookstore — 3090 Claremont Ave, Berkeley. Dark Carnival's sister store, with the largest graphic-novel and kids-comics selection in the East Bay. @escapistcomics

Flying Colors Comics — 1170 Concord Ave, Concord. An Eisner Retailer winner run by the originator of Free Comic Book Day, weekly new-release Wednesdays. @flycojoe

Crush Comics — 2869 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. Running since 1990, new releases and rare back issues with a Magic the Gathering table, open to 8pm on Wednesdays. @crushcomics

Treasure Island Comics — 37244 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. A shop by the ACE station with a standing 25-percent-off deal on all trades and hardcovers. @ticomics

Cosmic Slop Comics — 5 E 16th St, Antioch. The downtown Antioch shop the far-east-county collectors drive to, new comics, video games, and longboxes worth digging.

Eight for the pull list: Dr. Comics, Cape and Cowl, Fantastic, the Escapist, Flying Colors, Crush, Treasure Island, and Cosmic Slop. Where do you read?

item.description: If your kid still asks to walk into a toy store instead of browsing Amazon, the East Bay has independents that have earned the trip, one of them going sinc
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Independent Toy Stores

If your kid still asks to walk into a toy store instead of browsing Amazon, the East Bay has independents that have earned the trip, one of them going since 1962. Five East Bay independent toy stores.

Five Little Monkeys — 1810 4th St, Berkeley. A family-run mini-chain with hands-on demo culture and Friday craft and storytime events. @fivelittlemonkeystoys

Mr — Mopps' Toy Shop. 1405 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Berkeley. A Berkeley classic since 1962, with a connected children's bookshop next door for a one-stop kid trip.

Montclair Toyhouse — 6115 La Salle Ave, Oakland. Oakland's oldest independently owned toy store, family-run since 1969, with free gift wrapping and on-site assembly.

Lakeshore Learning Store — 1929 Mt Diablo Blvd, Walnut Creek. The flagship for the educational-supply chain, with free in-store Saturday craft events for young kids.

Learning Express Toys — 136 Market Pl, San Ramon. A locally owned franchise at City Center Bishop Ranch with free personalization and a birthday club. @learningexpresssanramon

Five for the trip: Five Little Monkeys, Mr. Mopps', Montclair Toyhouse, Lakeshore Learning, and Learning Express. Where do you shop?

item.title: East Bay Adult Education
item.description: The most underrated thing about the East Bay might be how cheap and serious the adult education is, from free ESL to Cal faculty teaching retirees. Eight E
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Adult Education

The most underrated thing about the East Bay might be how cheap and serious the adult education is, from free ESL to Cal faculty teaching retirees. Eight East Bay schools with public-access classes.

Berkeley Adult School — 1939 Ward St, Berkeley. The BUSD adult-ed anchor, with free ESL, high-school diploma, and career classes plus low-fee enrichment.

Oakland Adult and Career Education — 7929 Ney Ave, Oakland. OUSD adult ed across multiple campuses, ESL and career pathways at free or near-free tuition for residents.

OLLI at UC Berkeley — 1995 University Ave, Berkeley. Osher Lifelong Learning at Cal for learners 50 and up, study groups and short courses taught by Berkeley faculty. @berkeley_olli

OLLI at Cal State East Bay — 4700 Ygnacio Valley Rd, Concord. Lifelong learning for 50 and up, the one OLLI that meets primarily east of the Caldecott. @olli_calstateeastbay

Mt — Diablo Adult Education. Pleasant Hill and Concord. Trades apprenticeships, GED, ESL, and a robust wood shop and wood-turning program across many levels, a @kirsten_joy_t note.

Diablo Valley College Community Education — 321 Golf Club Rd, Pleasant Hill. Not-for-credit enrichment classes in art, photography, languages, and cooking, open to all ages. @diablovalleycollege

Berkeley Art Studio — 2495 Bancroft Way, Berkeley. Community-open studios for ceramics, photography, printmaking, and textiles at the UC student union. @berkeleyartstudio

Richmond Art Center — 2540 Barrett Ave, Richmond. A West County art school since 1936, with adult painting, ceramics, and printmaking plus free public galleries. @richmondartcenter

Eight for the class: Berkeley Adult School, Oakland Adult and Career, OLLI at Cal, OLLI at CSU East Bay, Mt. Diablo Adult Ed, DVC Community Ed, Berkeley Art Studio, and the Richmond Art Center. What would you learn next?

item.title: East Bay Campgrounds Within a Short Drive
item.description: There is a campground 35 minutes from downtown Oakland with full-hookup RV sites and hike-in tent sites overlooking a swimmable lake, and most East Bay par
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Campgrounds Within a Short Drive

There is a campground 35 minutes from downtown Oakland with full-hookup RV sites and hike-in tent sites overlooking a swimmable lake, and most East Bay parents have never booked it. Six campgrounds within a short drive.

Anthony Chabot Regional Park — 9999 Redwood Rd, Castro Valley. A 75-site campground 35 minutes from downtown Oakland, full-hookup RV sites plus hike-in tent sites above Lake Chabot. @ebrpd

Dumbarton Quarry Campground — 9400 Quarry Rd, Fremont. The park district's first full-service campground, 63 sites at Coyote Hills, most with full hookups.

Mount Diablo State Park — 96 Mitchell Canyon Rd, Clayton. Three campgrounds climbing the East Bay's 3,849-foot peak, with summit views to the Sierra on clear winter days. @castateparks

Del Valle Regional Park — 7000 Del Valle Rd, Livermore. The park district's largest family campground, 150 sites on a five-mile swimmable lake, with cabins and equestrian sites.

Sunol Regional Wilderness — 1895 Geary Rd, Sunol. Backpack camps along the Ohlone Wilderness Trail for the group that wants to hike in and sleep under the oaks.

Samuel P — Taylor State Park. Lagunitas. A creekside redwood campground in west Marin worth the drive, sites under second-growth redwoods.

Six for the tent: Anthony Chabot, Dumbarton Quarry, Mount Diablo, Del Valle, Sunol, and Samuel P. Taylor. Where do you pitch it?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Game Stores with Active Tables

The weekly social plan that actually sticks is the one with a standing crew and a table. The East Bay has game stores that host open D&D nights and match newcomers to a campaign. Six East Bay game stores with active tables.

Games of Berkeley — 2510 Durant Ave, Berkeley. The Bay Area's premier game shop, hosting open D&D tables and matching newcomers to existing groups. @gamesofberkeley

It's Your Move Games — 4920 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Temescal shop since 2003 with RPG nights Friday from 7, multiple GMs running concurrent tables. @itsyourmovegames

D20 Games — 1502 Park St, Alameda. A Park Street shop with weekly D&D, Pathfinder, and one-off Call of Cthulhu events. @d20gamesalameda

Victory Point Cafe — 1797 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A board-game cafe with a huge library and a small all-day fee to play, staff who teach the rules. @victorypointcafe

Phoenix Games — 4607 Clayton Rd, Concord. A Concord tabletop shop with weekly RPG night and a dedicated event space. @phoenixgameswc

The Adventure Begins — Oakley. An East County game store with rotating RPG sessions, open-table nights, and beginner one-shots on Sundays.

Six for the table: Games of Berkeley, It's Your Move, D20 Games, Victory Point Cafe, Phoenix Games, and the Adventure Begins. Where do you roll?

item.title: East Bay Skateparks
item.description: Town Park at DeFremery was built by Oakland skaters themselves and became the center of the city's street scene. The smoothest concrete is never the parkin
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Skateparks

Town Park at DeFremery was built by Oakland skaters themselves and became the center of the city's street scene. The smoothest concrete is never the parking lot the new neighbor is rolling. Six East Bay skateparks worth the wheels.

Town Park — DeFremery Park, 1651 Adeline St, Oakland. A community-built park with bowls, ledges, and stair sets, the center of Oakland street-skate culture. @townpark_official

Berkeley Skatepark — 711 Harrison St, Berkeley. An outdoor concrete park near the Marina with bowls, a mini ramp, and a smooth flow course; the sunset session is the move.

The Big O Skatepark — Heather Farm Park, 1747 Heather Dr, Walnut Creek. A municipal park with a full bowl, a street section, and some of the smoothest concrete in the East Bay.

Alameda Skatepark — 1101 W Redline Ave, Alameda. An outdoor concrete park with bowls and a street course, Bay views from the deep end.

Hayward Skatepark — 28377 Huntwood Ave, Hayward. A tessellated bowl plus a street section, one of the deeper East Bay bowls.

Pleasanton Skatepark — Pleasanton. The Tri-Valley's main outdoor park, smooth flow and clean ledges.

Six for the wheels: Town Park, Berkeley, the Big O, Alameda, Hayward, and Pleasanton. Which park has the smoothest concrete?

item.title: East Bay Outdoor Movie Nights
item.description: The summer evening lineup does not have to be another stream. The East Bay runs free outdoor film series in the parks all summer, plus one of California's
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Outdoor Movie Nights

The summer evening lineup does not have to be another stream. The East Bay runs free outdoor film series in the parks all summer, plus one of California's last drive-ins. Six East Bay outdoor cinema spots for summer.

Movies in the Park — Redwood Heights Park, 3883 Aliso Ave, Oakland. Free city-run screenings rotating through Mosswood, San Antonio, and Lakeside Parks all summer. @oakparksrec

Berkeley Movies in the Park — Live Oak Park and Cesar Chavez Park, Berkeley. The city's free Friday-night summer film series at the waterfront and the north-side parks.

Civic Park Movie Nights — Civic Park, 1375 Civic Dr, Walnut Creek. A free outdoor movie series on Friday nights, June through August.

Sunset Cinema — Lake Chabot Regional Park, 17600 Lake Chabot Rd, Castro Valley. An EBRPD Sunday-evening series with floating screens on the lake, book ahead. @ebrpd

Cinema by the Lake — Lakeside Park, 666 Bellevue Ave, Oakland. Outdoor screenings on the Lake Merritt amphitheater lawn, Saturdays June through August. @movienightatthelake

West Wind Solano Drive-In — 1611 Solano Way, Concord. One of California's last drive-ins, double features nightly. @westwinddriveins

Six for the summer screen: Movies in the Park, Berkeley Movies in the Park, Civic Park, Sunset Cinema, Cinema by the Lake, and the Solano Drive-In. What are you bringing the blanket for?

item.title: East Bay Dog Beaches
item.description: If your dog pulls toward the water on every walk, the East Bay shoreline has the fix, starting with Point Isabel's 23 off-leash acres. Six East Bay dog-fri
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Dog Beaches

If your dog pulls toward the water on every walk, the East Bay shoreline has the fix, starting with Point Isabel's 23 off-leash acres. Six East Bay dog-friendly beaches.

Point Isabel Regional Shoreline — 2701 Isabel St, Richmond. Twenty-three acres of off-leash shoreline with beach access along the whole perimeter, plus the Mudpuppy's wash at the gate. @ebrpd

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. An off-leash area with a beach section that stays accessible at low tide, dawn to dusk.

Crown Memorial State Beach Dog Beach — 8th St and Otis Dr, Alameda. A designated off-leash dog area at the south end of the beach, away from the main swim zone.

Hayward Regional Shoreline — 3010 W Winton Ave, Hayward. Long stretches of dog-friendly shoreline on leash, with room on the marsh boardwalk.

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. A 17-acre off-leash dog area at the Berkeley Marina, with shoreline paths and Bay views.

Coyote Hills Regional Park — 8000 Patterson Ranch Rd, Fremont. Dog-friendly trails on leash with marsh and Bay views, far less crowded than Point Isabel.

Six for the water dog: Point Isabel, the Albany Bulb, Crown Beach, Hayward Shoreline, Cesar Chavez, and Coyote Hills. Where does your dog swim?

item.title: East Bay Coworking and Maker Spaces
item.description: The Crucible in West Oakland teaches public classes in welding, glassblowing, blacksmithing, and neon, the most established maker space in the East Bay. Th
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Coworking and Maker Spaces

The Crucible in West Oakland teaches public classes in welding, glassblowing, blacksmithing, and neon, the most established maker space in the East Bay. The work-from-home rut needs a new scene, not just a new chair. Six East Bay coworking and maker spaces.

The Crucible — 1260 7th St, Oakland. The most established maker space in the East Bay, with public classes in welding, glassblowing, blacksmithing, and neon. @the_crucible

Pacific Workplaces — 1300 Clay St, Oakland. Coworking with desks, private offices, and rotating member events, the former NextSpace network.

The Port Workspaces — 344 20th St, Oakland. Several downtown Oakland buildings of coworking, meeting rooms, and a genuinely active member community. @portworkspaces

Forage Kitchen — 478 25th St, Oakland. A culinary incubator and shared commercial kitchen, coworking for food entrepreneurs. @foragekitchen.oak

Berkeley Public Library Maker Space — Claremont Branch, 2940 Benvenue Ave, Berkeley. A free maker space with 3D printers, sewing machines, and recording gear.

NIMBY — Oakland. An industrial creative warehouse for fabrication, art, and event production, with member access. @nimbyspace

Six for the workday: the Crucible, Pacific Workplaces, the Port, Forage Kitchen, the Berkeley library maker space, and NIMBY. Where do you build?

item.title: East Bay LGBTQ+ Spaces
item.description: The place you walk into on a random Tuesday that feels like home matters, and the East Bay has kept those spaces going, one gay bar since 1933. Six East Ba
item.content:encoded:
East Bay LGBTQ+ Spaces

The place you walk into on a random Tuesday that feels like home matters, and the East Bay has kept those spaces going, one gay bar since 1933. Six East Bay LGBTQ+ spaces worth knowing.

The White Horse — 6551 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The oldest continuously operating gay bar in the country, since 1933, with weekly drag and DJ nights. @whitehorsebar

FLUID510 — 1544 Broadway, Oakland. A downtown Oakland queer bar and event space that now carries much of the East Bay's drag and dance-night programming.

Oakland LGBTQ Community Center — 3207 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland. The Lake Merritt district center, now home to Oakland Pride, with support groups and a lending library. @oaklandlgbtqcenter

La Pena Cultural Center — 3105 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A Latine-led cultural center hosting queer Latin nights and community events. @lapenaculturalcenter

Pacific Center — 2712 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. The East Bay's longest-running LGBTQ+ community center, with support groups, events, and peer counseling. @pacificcenter

Rainbow Community Center — Concord. The Contra Costa County LGBTQ+ center, with youth, family, and adult community programs.

Six that feel like home: the White Horse, FLUID510, the Oakland LGBTQ Center, La Pena, the Pacific Center, and the Rainbow Center in Concord. Which one is yours?

item.title: East Bay Burmese Kitchens
item.description: Burma Superstar built the Bay Area's Burmese scene on Telegraph, and the tea leaf salad is still worth the wait. Six East Bay Burmese kitchens for the tea
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Burmese Kitchens

Burma Superstar built the Bay Area's Burmese scene on Telegraph, and the tea leaf salad is still worth the wait. Six East Bay Burmese kitchens for the tea leaf salad and coconut noodles.

Burma Superstar — 4721 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The Temescal flagship that built the Bay Area's Burmese scene; the tea leaf salad and rainbow salad are the order, no reservations. @burmasuperstar

Teni East Kitchen — 4015 Broadway, Oakland. A Michelin Bib Gourmand kitchen doing Burmese with a California spin, the tea leaf salad comes with kale and the roti lands flaky and golden. @tenieastkitchen

Burma Berkeley — 2826 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. A traditional Burmese kitchen that opened in 2025 in the former Royal Rangoon space, samosas, garlic noodles, and tea leaf salad.

Aung Burma — 2151 Salvio St, Concord. A Concord Burmese spot facing Todos Santos Plaza, open seven days, the samusa soup and coconut chicken noodle. @aungburma_ca

Burma! Burma! 7294 San Ramon Rd, Dublin — A Tri-Valley Burmese with tableside tea leaf salad, ohn no khao swe, and a deep vegetarian list, plus weekend live music. @burmaburma.ca

Burma Bear — Second Act Marketplace, Oakland. A Burmese-Caribbean hybrid, the tea leaf salad alongside jerk chicken, in the Second Act food hall.

Six for the tea leaf salad: Burma Superstar, Teni East, Burma Berkeley, Aung Burma, Burma! Burma!, and Burma Bear. What is your Burmese order?

item.description: If your seafood standard has not been reset by ceviche done right, the East Bay has real Peruvian, from Oakland out to the Tri-Valley. Five East Bay Peruvi
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Peruvian Kitchens

If your seafood standard has not been reset by ceviche done right, the East Bay has real Peruvian, from Oakland out to the Tri-Valley. Five East Bay Peruvian spots that recalibrate the menu.

La Costa Peruvian Cuisine — 3625 International Blvd, Oakland. A family-run Fruitvale spot where the ceviche, lomo saltado, and aji de gallina are the standing orders. @lacostaperuvian

Asu Mare — 6211 Shattuck Ave, Oakland. A Peruvian kitchen on the Oakland-Berkeley line, closed Tuesdays, the ceviche and saltado plates the draw. @asumare81

Bravazo — 428 Main St, Pleasanton. A downtown Pleasanton Peruvian with breakfast and empanadas, opened in 2025 across from Nonni's. @bravazo.foods

El Tunante Peruvian Cuisine — San Leandro. A family-run spot with the saltado dishes and Peruvian-Chinese chifa fusion plates.

El Chalan — 3748 San Pablo Dam Rd, El Sobrante. A family-owned Italian-Peruvian by the San Pablo Reservoir, the saltado and the seafood the draw. @elchalanrestaurantt

Five for the ceviche: La Costa, Asu Mare, Bravazo, El Tunante, and El Chalan. What is your Peruvian order?

item.title: East Bay Picnic Spots
item.description: Inspiration Point in Tilden lines up picnic tables with the full East Bay panorama, the sunset spot most baskets never reach. Every East Bay picnic lands a
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Picnic Spots

Inspiration Point in Tilden lines up picnic tables with the full East Bay panorama, the sunset spot most baskets never reach. Every East Bay picnic lands at the same four parks instead. Eight East Bay picnic spots past the usual four.

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. Bay-view picnic tables at the trailhead, the spot for a sunset picnic with the full East Bay panorama. @ebrpd

Joaquin Miller Park — 3450 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. Multiple picnic groves under redwood canopy; the Sequoia Bayview area is the under-the-radar pull.

Anthony Chabot Regional Park — 9999 Redwood Rd, Castro Valley. Lake-adjacent picnic areas with Lake Chabot views and reservation options for groups.

Lafayette Reservoir — 3849 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. The 4.7-mile loop has bench-and-table spots overlooking the water, an easy walk to a quiet one.

Briones Regional Park — Bear Creek Rd, Lafayette. Ridge-top picnic spots with Mount Diablo views; the Sindicich Lagoons area is the photogenic pull.

Coyote Hills Regional Park — 8000 Patterson Ranch Rd, Fremont. Marsh-edge picnic tables with Bay Trail access and the Tuibun Ohlone village site nearby.

Round Valley Regional Preserve — 19450 Marsh Creek Rd, Brentwood. An east-county picnic spot of rolling grassland with the Murphy Meadow group area.

Mount Diablo Junction — Mt Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. A mid-elevation picnic spot with summit views, near the Mitchell Canyon and Junction areas. @castateparks

Eight for the basket: Inspiration Point, Joaquin Miller, Anthony Chabot, Lafayette Reservoir, Briones, Coyote Hills, Round Valley, and the Mount Diablo Junction. Where do you spread the blanket?

item.title: East Bay Free Outdoor Spots
item.description: The Saturday that costs zero dollars can still feel like a full day. The East Bay's best free days are outdoors, no reservation and no entry fee. Eight Eas
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Free Outdoor Spots

The Saturday that costs zero dollars can still feel like a full day. The East Bay's best free days are outdoors, no reservation and no entry fee. Eight East Bay outdoor spots that cost nothing but the drive.

Lake Merritt — Oakland. The most-walked, most-jogged loop in the East Bay, free year-round, with the bird sanctuary and the Sunday drum circle.

Berkeley Marina and Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. Free parking, an off-leash dog lawn, a kite-flying hill, and sunset Bay views, the 5pm Saturday move.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. A landfill peninsula of public art and off-leash trails, dawn to dusk, with ever-changing installations.

Tilden Regional Park — Berkeley Hills. Free entry to 2,000-plus acres of trails; the Steam Train and Little Farm are paid extras but the trails are free. @ebrpd

Mountain View Cemetery — 5000 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. The 226-acre Frederick Law Olmsted-designed grounds, free and open for walking, jogging, and quiet views. @mountainviewcemetery.oakland

Joaquin Miller Park — 3450 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. Free redwood-canopy trails; the Sequoia Bayview and Sunset Loop are the highlights.

Point Isabel Regional Shoreline — 2701 Isabel St, Richmond. Free entry to 23 acres of off-leash shoreline, the largest dog park in the country.

Crab Cove — 1252 McKay Ave, Alameda. Free entry to the visitor center, the tide pools, and the swim beach, with free weekend nature talks.

Eight for the free Saturday: Lake Merritt, the Berkeley Marina, the Albany Bulb, Tilden, Mountain View Cemetery, Joaquin Miller, Point Isabel, and Crab Cove. Where do you go for free?

item.content:encoded:
