Yoshi's has booked national jazz acts in Jack London Square for decades, but the East Bay jazz room does not stop at the supper club. Six East Bay jazz rooms worth the booking.

Yoshi's — 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland. The flagship East Bay jazz supper club in Jack London Square, national touring acts nightly, with dinner upstairs. @yoshisoakland

California Jazz Conservatory — 2087 Addison St, Berkeley. The jazz school's public concert series in the downtown arts district, student and faculty nights. @calijazzconservatory

The Sound Room — 3022 Broadway, Oakland. An intimate listening room with the most-curated jazz calendar in the East Bay. @thesoundroomoak

Geoffrey's Inner Circle — 410 14th St, Oakland. A Black-owned downtown jazz and event lounge, the Friday jazz-and-soul rotation.

The Back Room — 1984 Bonita Ave, Berkeley. A small Berkeley music room, Thursday through Sunday, deep on jazz and acoustic.

Freight and Salvage — 2020 Addison St, Berkeley. A nonprofit music hall since 1968, jazz alongside folk and roots, all ages.

Six for the set: Yoshi's, the Cal Jazz Conservatory, the Sound Room, Geoffrey's, the Back Room, and the Freight. Where do you sit?

item.title: East Bay Cycling Routes
item.description: The Iron Horse Trail runs 32 uninterrupted paved miles from Concord to Pleasanton, most of it without a single traffic crossing. The weekend ride does not
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Cycling Routes

The Iron Horse Trail runs 32 uninterrupted paved miles from Concord to Pleasanton, most of it without a single traffic crossing. The weekend ride does not have to be the commute in reverse. Eight East Bay cycling routes past the commute.

Iron Horse Trail — Concord to Pleasanton. A 32-mile paved rail-trail, the longest uninterrupted bike route in central Contra Costa, mostly flat. @ebrpd

Lafayette-Moraga Trail — Lafayette to Moraga. A 7.65-mile paved rail-trail with a mild climb and redwood-canopy sections.

Bay Trail, Richmond to Albany — Point Isabel to Marina Bay. Long flat shoreline riding with Bay Bridge views and the Berkeley Marina turnaround. @sfbaytrail

Skyline Boulevard — Oakland Hills. The ridge-route road ride, cool air and redwood canopy with multiple summit options.

Coyote Hills and Don Edwards loop — Fremont and Newark. Flat marsh-and-refuge bike paths with birding scenery, an easy family loop.

Mount Diablo summit ride — Walnut Creek. An 11-mile road climb to the 3,849-foot summit, the East Bay's serious challenge ride.

Mines Road — Livermore to Mount Hamilton. A 50-mile remote climbing ride through Tri-Valley ranchland, for experienced cyclists.

Bridge Yard Loop — Oakland. A 12-mile loop from the Bay Bridge approach around Treasure Island and back, the most-photographed urban Bay ride.

Eight for the weekend ride: the Iron Horse, Lafayette-Moraga, the Bay Trail, Skyline, Coyote Hills, Mount Diablo, Mines Road, and the Bridge Yard. Where do you pedal?

item.description: The live theater habit does not require a bridge to a downtown SF house. The East Bay has stages from Tony-winning regional theaters to 70-year-old volunte
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Community Theaters

The live theater habit does not require a bridge to a downtown SF house. The East Bay has stages from Tony-winning regional theaters to 70-year-old volunteer playhouses. Eight East Bay theaters worth the season ticket.

Berkeley Repertory Theatre — 2025 Addison St, Berkeley. A Tony Award-winning regional theater with a multi-show season across two houses. @berkeleyrep

Shotgun Players — 1901 Ashby Ave, Berkeley. A long-running Berkeley company of experimental and contemporary work, with lower-priced tickets for new voices. @shotgunplayers

Contra Costa Civic Theatre — 951 Pomona Ave, El Cerrito. A longtime El Cerrito community playhouse with a full main stage season plus a summer concert series. @ccct_elcerrito

Center Repertory Company — Lesher Center, 1601 Civic Dr, Walnut Creek. A professional company inside the Lesher Center, Broadway-style musicals and classics. @centerrepwc

Berkeley Playhouse — 2640 College Ave, Berkeley. Family-friendly musical theater with strong youth programs alongside the main stage. @berkeleyplayhouse

Town Hall Theatre — 3535 School St, Lafayette. A long-running Lafayette community theater with a full season plus an open-mic series. @townhalltheatre

Altarena Playhouse — 1409 High St, Alameda. One of the oldest continuously operating community theaters in the Bay Area, since 1938. @altarenaplayhouse

Chanticleers Theatre — 3683 Quail Ave, Castro Valley. A community playhouse in Castro Valley Community Park, founded 1963. @chanticleerstheatre

Eight for the season: Berkeley Rep, Shotgun, Contra Costa Civic, Center Rep, Berkeley Playhouse, Town Hall, Altarena, and Chanticleers. What is the last play that stuck with you?

item.title: East Bay Hot Springs Within Driving Distance
item.description: The weekend that ends in 102-degree mineral water under the stars is a drive, not a flight. Seven hot springs within a few hours of the East Bay.
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Hot Springs Within Driving Distance

The weekend that ends in 102-degree mineral water under the stars is a drive, not a flight. Seven hot springs within a few hours of the East Bay.

Calistoga — Napa County. A hot-springs town of resort pools and historic mud baths at the top of Napa Valley, 90 minutes from Oakland. @visitcalistoga

Indian Springs — 1712 Lincoln Ave, Calistoga. The oldest continuously operating pool and spa in California, geothermal mineral water and mud baths.

Wilbur Hot Springs — 3375 Wilbur Springs Rd, Williams. An off-grid resort of clothing-optional pools and silent flumes, 2.5 hours north.

Orr Hot Springs — 13201 Orr Springs Rd, Ukiah. A small off-grid springs with private soaking tubs and a steam room, 2.5 hours north.

Vichy Springs Resort — 2605 Vichy Springs Rd, Ukiah. The original carbonated mineral springs, operating since 1854, two hours north.

Esalen Institute — 55000 Highway 1, Big Sur. Cliffside hot springs over the Pacific, with night soaking sessions, three hours south. @esalen

Travertine Hot Springs — Bridgeport. Free natural public hot springs on BLM land with Sierra Nevada views, a four-hour drive and no facilities.

Seven for the soak: Calistoga, Indian Springs, Wilbur, Orr, Vichy, Esalen, and Travertine. Where does your phone stay in the cabin?

item.content:encoded:

East Bay Meditation Center — 285 17th St, Oakland. A donation-based center with weekly classes and retreats, the flagship East Bay sangha. @ebmc_oakland

Berkeley Buddhist Monastery — 2304 McKinley Ave, Berkeley. A Theravada monastery with weekly meditation classes and multi-day retreats.

Nyingma Institute — 1815 Highland Pl, Berkeley. A Tibetan Buddhist center in the hills since 1972, with meditation, yoga, and study open to the public.

Berkeley Zen Center — 1931 Russell St, Berkeley. A Soto Zen center with daily zazen and newcomer instruction, in a residential compound since 1967.

Empty Gate Zen Center — Berkeley. A Korean Zen center with weekly practice and beginner sittings.

item.title: Casinos Near the East Bay
item.description: There is a card room a mile from downtown Oakland that has dealt on the same San Pablo corner since the 1890s, the oldest in Northern California. You do no
item.content:encoded:
Casinos Near the East Bay

There is a card room a mile from downtown Oakland that has dealt on the same San Pablo corner since the 1890s, the oldest in Northern California. You do not have to cross a bridge, let alone fly to Vegas, for a table. Six card rooms within a short drive of the East Bay.

Oaks Card Club — 4097 San Pablo Ave, Emeryville. A longtime Emeryville card room about a mile from Oakland, roughly 40 poker tables.

San Pablo Lytton Casino — 13255 San Pablo Ave, San Pablo. A tribal casino with around 1,500 slot-style machines and table games, ten miles up the shore.

California Grand Casino — 5988 Pacheco Blvd, Pacheco. A card room off Highways 680 and 4, poker and California games, about twenty minutes out.

The Palace Poker Casino — 22821 Mission Blvd, Hayward. A Hayward poker room open 24 hours with tournaments most days.

Lucky Chances Casino — Colma. A 60-table card room in Colma with blackjack, pai gow, and poker, about a half hour from Oakland.

Cache Creek Casino Resort — Brooks. A full resort casino a little over an hour north, the day-trip option with a hotel and golf.

Six for the table: Oaks, San Pablo Lytton, California Grand, the Palace, Lucky Chances, and Cache Creek. Which one is your spot?

item.description: Everyone tells you the good whiskey list is across the bridge in the city. Nobody tells you the Berkeley bar that has poured from an award-winning wall of
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Whiskey Bars

Everyone tells you the good whiskey list is across the bridge in the city. Nobody tells you the Berkeley bar that has poured from an award-winning wall of whiskey and mezcal since 2002. Five East Bay bars that take the pour seriously.

Acme Bar and Company — 2115 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A Berkeley bar since 2002 with an award-winning whiskey and mezcal selection and no attitude.

Bar Shiru — 1611 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A downtown Oakland hi-fi listening bar with a deep spirits list played on an all-analog sound system.

Prizefighter — 6702 Hollis St, Emeryville. An Emeryville cocktail bar with a broad spirits shelf and a big covered patio.

The Alley — 3325 Grand Ave, Oakland. A dim Grand Lake piano bar with stiff pours and a live sing-along most nights.

Cafe Van Kleef — 1621 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A downtown Oakland institution with strong drinks and a wall of curiosities.

Five for the pour: Acme, Bar Shiru, Prizefighter, the Alley, and Cafe Van Kleef. What is your bar?

item.description: There is a wedding venue in Berkeley that Julia Morgan designed in 1930, vaulted ceilings over an indoor pool courtyard. Most couples tour hotel ballrooms
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Wedding Venues

There is a wedding venue in Berkeley that Julia Morgan designed in 1930, vaulted ceilings over an indoor pool courtyard. Most couples tour hotel ballrooms and never find it. Six East Bay wedding venues with real history.

Berkeley City Club — 2315 Durant Ave, Berkeley. A Julia Morgan landmark from 1930 with vaulted ceilings and an indoor pool courtyard.

The Faculty Club — UC Berkeley, Berkeley. A 1902 Maybeck-designed hall on campus, the Great Hall plus the Faculty Glade lawn.

Brazilian Room — Shasta Rd at Wildcat Canyon Rd, Berkeley. A 1930s hardwood hall in Tilden Park with a garden terrace. @brazilianroomevents

The Terrace Room — 1800 Madison St, Oakland. An Art Deco room over Lake Merritt with a downtown skyline view.

Camron-Stanford House — 1418 Lakeside Dr, Oakland. An 1876 Victorian landmark on Lake Merritt with a veranda and garden lights.

Claremont Club and Spa — 41 Tunnel Rd, Berkeley. A 1915 resort landmark in the hills on 22 acres with a bay view.

Six with real history: the Berkeley City Club, the Faculty Club, the Brazilian Room, the Terrace Room, Camron-Stanford, and the Claremont. Which would you say yes in?

BIBO Salon — 2509 Broadway, Oakland. An Uptown Oakland salon with a long-trusted crew of stylists.

L'amor Salon — Oakland. A well-reviewed Oakland salon for cut, color, and styling.

Shawl-Anderson Dance Center — 2704 Alcatraz Ave, Berkeley. A Berkeley modern-dance institution since 1958 with drop-in adult classes.

East Bay Dance Center — 1318 Glenfield Ave, Oakland. A Montclair-edge studio with jazz, ballet, tap, and hip hop for adults and kids.

Danspace — 473 Hudson St, Oakland. A Rockridge studio near BART with a supportive all-levels adult program.

SilKi Movements Studio — 1035 22nd Ave, Oakland. An Oakland studio with heels, hip hop, samba, and yoga. @silkimovements

In Lak'ech Dance Academy — Oakland. An Oakland academy for Afro-Latin dance, bachata and salsa, with a warm community, an @alyssagalyssag add.

Berkeley Ballet — Berkeley. The adult open division runs beginner to advanced with live accompaniment.

There is a nonprofit on Telegraph Avenue where a warehouse of donated fabric, buttons, and vintage clothing sells for a few dollars. Most people pay full retail for what it holds secondhand. Five East Bay vintage and secondhand shops.

Mercy Vintage — 5505 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge shop of curated vintage clothing.

Empress Vintage — Berkeley. Pre-loved everyday and special-occasion finds, with trunk shows.

Five for the racks: Crossroads, Mercy Vintage, the Creative Reuse Depot, Indigo, and Empress. Where do you thrift?

item.title: East Bay Record Stores
item.description: There is a record store in El Cerrito that has stocked roots music, folk, blues, gospel, zydeco, since 1976. When I posted a shorter list, the comments fil
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Record Stores

There is a record store in El Cerrito that has stocked roots music, folk, blues, gospel, zydeco, since 1976. When I posted a shorter list, the comments filled in the rest. Ten East Bay record stores, half of them yours.

Amoeba Music — 2455 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. A Telegraph institution with walls of vinyl across every genre.

Down Home Music — 10341 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito. A roots-music mecca since 1976, folk, blues, gospel, and zydeco.

1-2-3-4 Go! Records — 420 40th St, Oakland. A Temescal shop strong on punk and local pressings.

Stranded Records — 5488 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge shop of curated sounds from around the world.

Open Mind Music — 5521 College Ave, Oakland. A College Ave shop deep in used vinyl.

Contact Records — 484 Alley 49, Oakland. A tiny Temescal Alley shop with a sharp selection.

Hercules Records — 1734 Alcatraz Ave, Berkeley. A South Berkeley vinyl shop.

Tone Army Records — 1460 Washington Blvd, Concord. Used vinyl out in Concord.

The Stacks Record Shop — 965 B St, Hayward. A downtown Hayward vinyl shop.

Up The Creek Records — Walnut Creek. An all-vinyl, pirate-themed shop out in Walnut Creek.

Ten to dig through: Amoeba, Down Home, 1-2-3-4 Go, Stranded, Open Mind, Contact, Hercules, Tone Army, the Stacks, and Up The Creek. Six came from you. Which did I still miss?

item.title: East Bay Filipino Kitchens
item.description: Most people meet Filipino food one lumpia at a time from a stall. A Fruitvale kitchen turned its G Fire wings and silog plates into a full institution, and
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Filipino Kitchens

Most people meet Filipino food one lumpia at a time from a stall. A Fruitvale kitchen turned its G Fire wings and silog plates into a full institution, and Union City quietly became one of the densest Filipino corridors in the Bay. Eight East Bay Filipino kitchens, Oakland to Union City.

Lucky Three Seven — 2868 Fruitvale Ave, Oakland. The Fruitvale kitchen whose G Fire wings pull a line to the sidewalk, lumpia and silog to round the plate out, cash or Venmo, closed Mondays.

FOB Kitchen — 5179 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A queer and POC owned Temescal room where the lechon comes crackling and the kare kare is the one you order for the whole table.

Tita Becca's — 400 15th St, Oakland. The downtown late night diner for when the bars empty and you still want garlic rice and something fried.

The Lumpia Company — 288 9th Ave, Oakland. Lumpia by the dozen and Filipino plates with a cold beer, tucked near Jack London Square.

Gerry's Grill and Bar — 31005 Courthouse Dr, Union City. A Philippine restaurant group's US outpost in Union Landing, sizzling sisig, crispy pata, and a bar that runs late on weekends. @gerrysgrillunioncity

Tribu Grill — 32208 Dyer St, Union City. The Dyer Street party room built for a long table and a crowd, grilled plates and comfort food the whole neighborhood books for catering. @thetribugrill

Lechon Manila — 32104 Alvarado Blvd, Union City. The one you call before a party, whole roast lechon sold by the pound with the skin shattering off the top.

Tipunan — Oakland. A homestyle spot serving kamayan feasts you eat with your hands off banana leaves.

Eight to feast: Lucky Three Seven, FOB, Tita Becca's, the Lumpia Company, Gerry's, Tribu, Lechon Manila, and Tipunan. Kamayan or crispy pata first?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Persian and Iranian Tables
item.description: Good Persian food in the East Bay is not where you would look for it. The 50-year anchor is a Berkeley grocery on San Pablo Avenue, not a white-tablecloth
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Persian and Iranian Tables

Good Persian food in the East Bay is not where you would look for it. The 50-year anchor is a Berkeley grocery on San Pablo Avenue, not a white-tablecloth room, and it just opened its own cafe. Seven East Bay Persian and Iranian tables.

Middle East Market and Cafe — 2054 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. The 1974 Persian grocery, now with a father-and-son cafe serving koobideh and stews behind it. @memberkeley

Alborz — 1829 Mt Diablo Blvd, Walnut Creek. Persian cooking in the Bay since 1988, baghali polo and fesenjoon done right. @alborz.us

Persian Nights — 248 Grand Ave, Oakland. Persian stews and brunch on Lake Merritt, across from Children's Fairyland. @_persiannights_

Daryoush Persian Cuisine — 1534 Locust St, Walnut Creek. Berkeley-rooted, now downtown Walnut Creek, known for its tahdig and charbroiled kabobs. @daryoushrestaurant

Kabob House — 1250 Newell Ave, Walnut Creek. A small family kabob house, koobideh and slow lamb shank over saffron basmati. @kabobhousewalnutcreek

Razi Foods — 1740 Monument Blvd, Concord. Family halal Persian kitchen, kababs and home-style plates, big on catering. @razi.foods

Mazeh Persian Cafe — Sunvalley Mall, Concord. Persian sandwiches like kotlet and kabob, plus home-style daily specials. @mazeh_persian_cafe

Seven from Berkeley to Concord: Middle East Market, Alborz, Persian Nights, Daryoush, Kabob House, Razi, and Mazeh. Whose tahdig gets the corner piece?

item.title: East Bay Surf Spots and Schools Within a Day's Drive
item.description: Six-story waves, twenty-five miles from your door. That is Mavericks off Pillar Point in Half Moon Bay, the far end of a coast that also hides the gentlest
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Surf Spots and Schools Within a Day's Drive

Six-story waves, twenty-five miles from your door. That is Mavericks off Pillar Point in Half Moon Bay, the far end of a coast that also hides the gentlest beginner beaches around. Six surf spots and schools within a day's drive.

Linda Mar, Pacifica State Beach — Pacifica. The Bay Area's premier learn-to-surf beach, gentle whitewater rolling in at the creek mouth.

NorCal Surf Shop — 5440 Coast Hwy, Pacifica. Linda Mar's main lesson provider, board and wetsuit included with every lesson. @norcalsurfshop

Cowell's Beach — Santa Cruz. Long, slow rollers called one of the best beginner breaks in the world, second only to Waikiki.

Bolinas Surf Lessons — 22 Brighton Ave, Bolinas. The Bay Area's original surf school since 1998, on the gentlest beach in Marin. @surfbolinas

Steamer Lane — Santa Cruz. A world-famous cold-water point off West Cliff Drive, four reef breaks, for the experienced only.

Mavericks — Pillar Point, Half Moon Bay. The legendary big-wave break, first surfed solo by Jeff Clark in 1975, a watch-only wonder for nearly everyone.

Six on the coast: Linda Mar, NorCal Surf Shop, Cowell's, Bolinas, Steamer Lane, and Mavericks. The water is cold year-round, so who is booking a lesson?

item.description: Everyone knows the big-box pet chains. Nobody mentions that the oldest and largest reptile store in the entire country sits on Fifth Street in Berkeley, op
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Specialty Pet Shops

Everyone knows the big-box pet chains. Nobody mentions that the oldest and largest reptile store in the entire country sits on Fifth Street in Berkeley, open since 1970. Six East Bay specialty pet shops.

East Bay Vivarium — 1827 5th St, Berkeley. The oldest and largest reptile and amphibian store in the country, open since 1970. @theeastbayvivarium

Your Basic Bird — 2940 College Ave, Berkeley. A rare thing, a shop dedicated entirely to birds and their keeping, in the Elmwood. @yourbasicbird

Alameda See Spot Run — 1320 Park St, Alameda. Family-run natural and holistic food with full grooming, and kitten adoptions on weekends. @alameda.seespotrun

Concord Aquarium — 1776 Arnold Industrial Way, Concord. The Bay Area's oldest fish store, since 1988, where you grab a bucket and net your own fish. @concordaquarium

Bay Bridge Aquarium and Pet — 2400 Filbert St, Oakland. Runs a 2000-gallon quarantine system with a microscope before any fish is sold. @baybridgeaquarium

Aquatic Collection — 1212 W Winton Ave, Hayward. A saltwater and freshwater shop heavy on coral, in business since 2006. @aquaticcollection

Six that go deep: the Vivarium, Your Basic Bird, See Spot Run, Concord Aquarium, Bay Bridge, and Aquatic Collection. What is in your tank or terrarium?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Outdoor Gear Shops

Skip the big-box outdoor aisle. The North Face was born here, a 1966 San Francisco shop that crossed to Berkeley in 1968 and started building its own gear. Six East Bay outdoor gear shops.

The North Face — 1238 Fifth St, Berkeley. Where the brand set up in 1968 and started designing its own gear, now the Berkeley outlet. @thenorthface

REI — 1338 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. The member-owned co-op has outfitted the East Bay since 1975, and it rents tents and climbing gear. @rei

Sports Basement — 1881 Ygnacio Valley Rd, Walnut Creek. A homegrown Bay Area shop that gives ten percent of earnings back to local schools. @sportsbasement

Young's Backpacking and Mountaineering — 2508 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. A family shop with the largest selection of backpacks in the Bay Area. @youngsbackpacking

Sunrise Mountain Sports — 2184 First St, Livermore. A family-owned independent serving the Tri-Valley since 1975. @sunrisemountainsports

Berkeley Ironworks Pro Shop — 800 Potter St, Berkeley. The climbing-gym shop stocked for real climbers, ropes, cams, and shoes. @berkeleyironworks

Six over the big box: North Face, REI, Sports Basement, Young's, Sunrise, and Berkeley Ironworks. Where do you kit up?

item.title: East Bay Salvadoran Kitchens and Pupuserias
item.description: The best pupusa in the East Bay is not in Fruitvale. It is in Old Oakland, where Popoca griddles them over a live wood fire and cooked its way into the Mic
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Salvadoran Kitchens and Pupuserias

The best pupusa in the East Bay is not in Fruitvale. It is in Old Oakland, where Popoca griddles them over a live wood fire and cooked its way into the Michelin Guide. Seven Salvadoran kitchens, Oakland to Concord.

Los Cocos — 1449 Fruitvale Ave, Oakland. Griddling pupusas in Fruitvale since 1985, cash only, curtido piled on the side. @loscocos510

Popoca — 906 Washington St, Oakland. Salvadoran cooking over a wood fire in Old Oakland, in the Michelin Guide, a 2020 pop-up now a Tuesday-to-Saturday dinner. @popoca.oakland

Pupusas Salvadorenas — 1462 High St, Oakland. Classic fillings from pork and cheese to loroco, 9 to 9 daily, with fried fish when a pupusa is just the opener.

Pupuseria Rosita — 1335 E 17th St, Oakland. Open from seven thirty in the morning to past ten at night, the breakfast pupusa and the late one off the same griddle.

Platano — 2042 University Ave, Berkeley. A Salvadoran pupuseria on University Avenue, revueltas and loroco with a mound of curtido and salsa roja. @platanoberkeley

Restaurante Bahia de Jiquilisco — 4633 Clayton Rd, Concord. Named for El Salvador's biggest bay, loroco and revuelta pupusas and a crisp whole tilapia.

Xinia's Bakery — 3550 San Pablo Dam Rd, El Sobrante. A Salvadoran bakery where the pupusas share the counter with pan dulce, open daily in West County. @xiniasbakery

Seven griddles, Oakland to Concord: Los Cocos, Popoca, Pupusas Salvadorenas, Rosita, Platano, Bahia de Jiquilisco, and Xinia's. Which one has your standing pupusa order?

item.title: East Bay Cambodian Kitchens
item.description: The family that opened one of the Bay Area's first Cambodian restaurants survived the Khmer Rouge, then were granted asylum in the United States. Phnom Pen
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Cambodian Kitchens

The family that opened one of the Bay Area's first Cambodian restaurants survived the Khmer Rouge, then were granted asylum in the United States. Phnom Penh House has served amok in Alameda since 1986. Five East Bay Cambodian kitchens.

Phnom Penh House — 1514 Webster St, Alameda. One of the Bay Area's first Cambodian restaurants, family-run since 1986, from an Oakland Chinatown start.

Battambang — 850 Broadway, Oakland. In Oakland Chinatown since 1993, named for Cambodia's rice province, known for amok and red curry. @battambangrestaurant

Cambodian Street Food — 2045 Foothill Blvd, Oakland. A small Foothill storefront that built a following of tens of thousands on prahok ktiss and sour beef soup. @cambodianstreetfood

Sitha's Khmerkitchen — 1001 Canal Blvd, Richmond. Sitha Yim taught herself Khmer cooking from her mother and pours it into a weekend pop-up at East Brother Beer. @sithaskhmerkitchen

Kathiew House — A and R Market, 3615 Foothill Blvd, Oakland. A weekend stall for kuy teav, Cambodian beef noodle soup, Saturday and Sunday until it sells out. @kathiewhouseofoakland

Five Cambodian kitchens: Phnom Penh House, Battambang, Cambodian Street Food, Sitha's, and Kathiew House. Who is pouring your first bowl of kuy teav?

item.description: Fruit pie, cream pie, a worker-owned pie cooperative. The East Bay pie case runs deeper than you think, starting with FatApple's olallieberry, its best-sel
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Pie Shops

Fruit pie, cream pie, a worker-owned pie cooperative. The East Bay pie case runs deeper than you think, starting with FatApple's olallieberry, its best-seller since 1969. Six spots for a real slice.

FatApple's — 1346 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Berkeley. Baking since 1969, the olallieberry pie the year-round best-seller, also in El Cerrito. @fatapplesrestaurantbakery

Niles Pie Company — 32990 Alvarado-Niles Rd, Union City. A worker-owned pie cooperative, sweet and savory, on a seasonal rotating menu. @nilespieco

Pie Dreams — 5855 Jarvis Ave, Newark. A dedicated pie shop, whole pies by pre-order, open Thursday to Sunday. @pie.dreams

Uhuru Pies — 7911 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. Baking pies in Oakland since 1981, the proceeds funding the Uhuru Movement, limited walk-in hours. @uhurufoodsandpiesoakland

The Original Hick'ry Pit — 1495 S Main St, Walnut Creek. A BBQ and breakfast spot with a warm marionberry and apple pie by the wedge. @hickrypit

Buttercup — 660 Ygnacio Valley Rd, Walnut Creek. A diner known for a house upside-down apple-walnut pie and a rotating fruit and cream board. @buttercupdiner

Six for a slice: FatApple's, Niles Pie, Pie Dreams, Uhuru, the Hick'ry Pit, and Buttercup. Whose pie case do you raid?

item.title: East Bay Craft Distilleries
item.description: You have driven past the Alameda hangar a hundred times. Inside it, St. George has distilled since 1982, the first American craft distillery since Prohibit
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Craft Distilleries

You have driven past the Alameda hangar a hundred times. Inside it, St. George has distilled since 1982, the first American craft distillery since Prohibition and the birthplace of Hangar 1 vodka. Seven East Bay distilleries.

St — George Spirits. 2601 Monarch St, Alameda. America's original craft distillery, in an Alameda hangar since 1982, and it made the first legal American absinthe. Tasting room Wednesday to Sunday. @stgeorgespirits

Wright and Brown Distilling — 2715 Magnolia St, Oakland. The first distillery in Oakland since Prohibition, grain-to-glass bourbon and rye, tasting bar Wednesday to Saturday. @wrightandbrown

Russell City Distillery — 22549 Foothill Blvd, Hayward. Vodka, gin, and rum on a hand-built copper still, named for the historic Russell City, tasting room Friday to Sunday. @russellcitydistillery

Sidewinder Spirits — 2405 Research Dr, Livermore. A family-run Livermore distillery since 2014, spirits and cocktails Thursday through Sunday on the Tri-Valley side of the hills. @sidewinderspirits

Falcon Spirits — 3701 Collins Ave, Richmond. Known for its Botanica gin, tastings by appointment in the West Richmond flats. @falconspirits

Mosswood Distillers — 2619 7th St, Berkeley. Barrel-aged whiskey and rum, including a signature espresso-barrel whiskey, tastings at events. @drinkmosswood

Home Base Spirits — 2619 7th St, Berkeley. Sustainable California craft whiskey, aged and blended in a West Berkeley warehouse, private tastings. @homebasespirits

Seven to sip: St. George, Wright and Brown, Russell City, Sidewinder, Falcon, Mosswood, and Home Base. Which tasting room gets your Saturday?

item.title: East Bay Electronic and Dance Floors
item.description: Nobody gives the East Bay credit for its dance floors. The oldest continuously running gay bar in America has been one of them since 1933, on Telegraph Ave
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Electronic and Dance Floors

Nobody gives the East Bay credit for its dance floors. The oldest continuously running gay bar in America has been one of them since 1933, on Telegraph Avenue in Oakland. Six East Bay spots to dance.

The White Horse — 6551 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The oldest continuously operating gay bar in the country, in the same spot since 1933, with weekend DJ dance nights. @whitehorsebar

Crybaby — 1928 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A 600-capacity dance club in the old Uptown Nightclub space, home to the Hella Gay Dance Party. @crybabyoakland

Fluid510 — 1544 Broadway, Oakland. Downtown Oakland's largest queer club, DJ dance parties, drag, and performance. @fluid510

The New Parish — 1743 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. A 450-capacity Uptown music hall booking electronic and bass acts alongside global sounds. @thenewparish

Cornerstone — 2367 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A 600-plus-capacity Berkeley beer hall and venue with a stage that runs electronic nights. @cornerstoneberkeley

The UC Theatre — 2036 University Ave, Berkeley. A 1,400-capacity nonprofit hall with a Meyer sound system that programs EDM and electronica. @theuctheatre

item.title: East Bay Camera Shops and Film Labs
item.description: Film photography was supposed to be dead. Berkeley never got the memo: Looking Glass has sold cameras and developed rolls since 1971, one of the last full-
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Camera Shops and Film Labs

Film photography was supposed to be dead. Berkeley never got the memo: Looking Glass has sold cameras and developed rolls since 1971, one of the last full-service shops standing. Eight East Bay camera shops and film labs.

Looking Glass Photographic — 2095 Rose St, Berkeley. Berkeley's camera store since 1971, new and used gear, lens rentals, film drop-off, and workshops. @lookingglassphotoberkeley

Photolab — 2235 Fifth St, Berkeley. Hand-processes black-and-white, C-41, and E-6 from 110 up to 8x10 sheet film, with a 24-hour drop box. @photolab.berkeley

Foto Shop — 131 Berkeley Sq, Berkeley. The little downtown Berkeley counter that still sells cameras, develops film, and prints photos, all in one stop.

Underdog Film Lab — 1625 16th St, Oakland. A West Oakland lab developing film in-house for 35mm, 120, and large format, in a building that once held a saloon. @underdogfilmlab

Royal We Film Lab — 2121 Peralta St, Oakland. Next-day in-house developing and scanning, and one of the few labs that also runs motion-picture film. @royalwefilmlab

Chater Camera — 1336 Ninth St, Berkeley. An independent cinema camera and lens rental house for film and video pros, since 2007. @chatercamera

Montclair Photo — 6170 Antioch St, Oakland. The Montclair Village photo shop since 1981, a traditional in-house lab for film, scanning, and prints. @montclairphoto

Mike's Camera — 2170 Contra Costa Blvd, Pleasant Hill. A full retail camera store with new and used gear, film, and developing, the Contra Costa option. @mymikescamera

Eight for the shutterbug: Looking Glass, Photolab, Foto Shop, Underdog, Royal We, Chater, Montclair Photo, and Mike's. Are you still shooting film?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Circus and Aerial Arts
item.description: Modern aerial dance was invented in Berkeley. Terry Sendgraff hung the first single point spinning trapeze here in 1975 and launched a whole art form, and
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Circus and Aerial Arts

Modern aerial dance was invented in Berkeley. Terry Sendgraff hung the first single point spinning trapeze here in 1975 and launched a whole art form, and her low flying trapeze is still taught a mile away. Seven East Bay studios where you can actually leave the ground.

Kinetic Arts Center — 785 7th St, Oakland. A full nonprofit circus school since 2008, trapeze, silks, rope, hoop, and hand balancing under one West Oakland warehouse roof, drop in or sign up. @kineticartscenter

UpSwing Aerial Dance — 2525 Eighth St, Berkeley. Carrying Terry Sendgraff's low flying Motivity trapeze lineage since 2005, small classes in the Sawtooth Building. @upswingdance

Athletic Playground — 4770 San Pablo Ave, Emeryville. Fifty plus movement classes a week since 2008, silks, trapeze, lyra, acro, even parkour, for total beginners on up. @athleticplayground

Berkeley Pole and Dance — 1636 University Ave, Berkeley. Pole and aerial from true beginner to advanced on a sliding scale that keeps it open to everyone. @berkeleypoleanddance

Oakland Pole and Dance — 366 Grand Ave, Oakland. The Adams Point studio where a first timer books pole, silks, or lyra and learns to trust their own grip.

Skyhigh Odditorium — 1 W Barrett Ave, Richmond. An adults focused silks and hoop school that also stages dark circus variety shows, since 2012. @skyhighodditorium

The Crucible — 1260 7th St, Oakland. The country's largest nonprofit industrial arts school, where the aerial rig shares a building with fire performance and fire dancing. @the_crucible

Seven to fly: Kinetic Arts, UpSwing, Athletic Playground, Berkeley Pole, Oakland Pole, Skyhigh, and the Crucible. Silks, trapeze, or fire?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Brazilian Tables
item.description: A Brazilian cafe has served feijoada out of an 1800s Victorian in downtown Oakland for over twenty years, and most people walk right past the porch. Rio Ca
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Brazilian Tables

A Brazilian cafe has served feijoada out of an 1800s Victorian in downtown Oakland for over twenty years, and most people walk right past the porch. Rio California hides in plain sight. Six East Bay Brazilian spots.

Rio California — 1233 Preservation Park Way, Oakland. Brazilian home cooking inside a historic Victorian for over twenty years, from a Rio-born owner. @riocaliforniacafe

Paulista — 4239 Park Blvd, Oakland. A Brazilian kitchen and taproom, bobo de camarao and feijoada alongside two dozen taps. @paulista510

Casa do Petisco — 2642 Ashby Ave, Berkeley. A women-owned Brazilian lanchonete, coxinhas and pao de queijo, plus a vegan kibe. @casadopetisco.usa

Galpao Gaucho — 1444 N California Blvd, Walnut Creek. Full rodizio, eighteen fire-grilled cuts carved tableside, with a big salad bar. @galpaogauchousa

Espetus Churrascaria — 2025 Diamond Blvd, Concord. The East Bay outpost of San Francisco's original churrascaria, rodizio since 2003, opened in Concord in 2025. @espetus

Cantinho do Brazil — 370 Hartz Ave, Danville. A casual cafe from a Minas Gerais native, known for a thick real-Brazilian acai bowl. @corner_of_brazil

Six for Brazil: Rio California, Paulista, Casa do Petisco, Galpao Gaucho, Espetus, and Cantinho do Brazil. Rodizio or acai for you?

item.title: East Bay Woodworking Classes
item.description: Before you buy a garage full of tools, know this: a West Oakland shop built out of stacked shipping containers will teach you to build. Lower 48 is woman o
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Woodworking Classes

Before you buy a garage full of tools, know this: a West Oakland shop built out of stacked shipping containers will teach you to build. Lower 48 is woman owned and aimed at the makers woodworking usually skips. Seven East Bay places to learn the craft.

Lower 48 Woodshop — 1212 19th St, Oakland. A woman owned nonprofit grown out of stacked shipping containers, heavy on woodturning, pens to bowls, and on the makers the craft overlooks. @lower48woodshop

Strong Wood Studio — 2225 6th St, Berkeley. Sara Strong, a third generation woodworker, runs a two day beginner workshop where you build a solid hardwood cutting board and meet the table saw, router, and sander.

Laney College Wood Technology — 900 Fallon St, Oakland. One of the best equipped teaching shops in Northern California, avocational furniture and cabinetmaking classes that fit around a job, hand tools to CAD. @laneywoodtech

Ace Makerspace — 6050 Lowell St, Oakland. A member run wood and metal shop where a one hour shop basics class unlocks the tools to anyone. @ace_makerspace

Hands On Woodshop — West Oakland. Shop class for adults, a membership community woodshop with classes on the kind of tools most people never get to touch. @handson_wood

Mt — Diablo Adult Education. One Santa Barbara Rd, Pleasant Hill. A public adult ed woodshop running tuition woodworking and woodturning for every level.

Diablo Woodworkers — One Santa Barbara Rd, Pleasant Hill. A volunteer club since 1997 on the same campus, beginning and advanced classes open to any adult.

Seven to learn the craft: Lower 48, Strong Wood, Laney, Ace Makerspace, Hands On, Mt. Diablo Adult Ed, and Diablo Woodworkers. What do you build first?

item.description: You have walked under the neon blade sign on Park Street a hundred times. It belongs to the last grand movie palace built in the Bay Area, the 1932 Alameda
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Alameda, Park Street

You have walked under the neon blade sign on Park Street a hundred times. It belongs to the last grand movie palace built in the Bay Area, the 1932 Alameda Theatre, dark for thirty years and lit again since 2008. Seven stops on Park Street, Alameda.

Alameda Theatre — 2317 Central Ave, Alameda. A 1932 art deco movie palace, the last grand one built in the Bay Area, restored and reopened in 2008. @alamedatheatres

Tucker's Super Creamed Ice Cream — 1349 Park St, Alameda. Scooping on Park Street since 1941, an eighty-year island institution. @tuckersicecream

Books Inc — 1344 Park St, Alameda. The Alameda branch of the West's oldest independent bookseller. @booksinc_alameda

Signal Coffee Roasters — 2318A Central Ave, Alameda. The island's small-batch specialty roaster, a block off Park. @signalcoffeeroasters

Crispian Bakery — 1700 Park St, Alameda. French-inspired breads and pastries, baked small-batch and daily. @crispianbakery

Alameda Brewing — 1716 Park St, Alameda. A family brewery on Park Street and a 2025 World Beer Cup silver medalist. @alamedabrewingco

Toy Safari — 1410 Park St, Alameda. An independent toy store, a couple of decades on Park. @toysafaritoys

Seven on Park Street: the Theatre, Tucker's, Books Inc, Signal, Crispian, Alameda Brewing, and Toy Safari. What is your Park Street stop?

item.content:encoded:
Oakland, Grand Lake

A 1926 movie palace, a 1933 piano bar papered in tens of thousands of business cards, a worker-owned bakery. The Grand Lake district wears its history on Grand Avenue. Seven stops around Grand Lake, Oakland.

Grand Lake Theatre — 3200 Grand Ave, Oakland. A 1926 movie palace whose rooftop sign is the largest chasing-light sign west of the Mississippi. @grandlaketheater

The Alley — 3325 Grand Ave, Oakland. A 1933 piano bar with walls papered in tens of thousands of stapled business cards. @the_alley_of_oakland

Grand Lake Kitchen — 576 Grand Ave, Oakland. An all-day cafe and full bar a block from the lake. @grandlakekitchen

Red Bay Coffee — 3206 Grand Ave, Oakland. The Black-owned Oakland roaster, two doors from the theater. @redbaycoffee

Walden Pond Books — 3316 Grand Ave, Oakland. A family-owned independent bookstore since 1973. @waldenpondbooks

Arizmendi Bakery — 3265 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland. A worker-owned cooperative baking bread and a daily co-op pizza. @arizmendilakeshore

Grand Lake Farmers Market — Splash Pad Park, Grand Ave at Lake Park Ave, Oakland. A Saturday market of a hundred vendors beside the theater.

Seven around the lake: the Theatre, the Alley, Grand Lake Kitchen, Red Bay, Walden Pond, Arizmendi, and the Saturday market. What draws you to Grand Ave?

item.content:encoded:
Oakland, Rockridge and College Avenue

The best thing on College Avenue is not a restaurant. It is Rockridge Market Hall, a covered European food emporium at the BART mouth since 1987 where the cheese, pasta, wine, and coffee counters all live under one roof. Seven stops in Rockridge, Oakland.

Rockridge Market Hall — 5655 College Ave, Oakland. A covered European food emporium at the Rockridge BART mouth since 1987. @markethallfoods

Wood Tavern — 6317 College Ave, Oakland. A New American brasserie in the Michelin Guide, a Rockridge institution since 2007. @tavern_oakland

La Farine — 6323 College Ave, Oakland. A French bakery on College since 1977, famous for its morning bun. @lafarinebakery

Highwire Coffee Roasters — 5615 College Ave, Oakland. The flagship cafe of a roaster launched in Rockridge in 2011. @highwirecoffee

Pegasus Books — 5560 College Ave, Oakland. A new-and-used independent bookseller, a Rockridge fixture since 1971. @pegasusbooks

Bad Walter's Bootleg Ice Cream — 5800 College Ave, Oakland. A pandemic pop-up turned storefront in 2024, spun fresh daily. @badwalters

Ben 'N Nick's Bar and Grill — 5612 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge pub with a deep craft-beer list since 1997. @benandnicks

Seven on College: Market Hall, Wood Tavern, La Farine, Highwire, Pegasus, Bad Walter's, and Ben 'N Nick's. Where do you get off at Rockridge BART?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Livermore

You do not have to drive to Napa for wine country. Livermore has grown wine grapes since 1883, and you can taste it on foot downtown, at tasting rooms a block from the Bankhead Theater. Seven stops in downtown Livermore.

Bankhead Theater — 2400 First St, Livermore. A performing arts center that anchored downtown when it opened in 2007. @thebankheadlva

First Street Wine Company — 2211 First St, Livermore. A downtown tasting bar pouring Livermore Valley and beyond, three hundred wines deep. @1ststreetwineco

Range Life — 2160 Railroad Ave, Livermore. A farm-to-table restaurant in the Michelin Guide, a block off First Street. @rangelife_livermore

Panama Bay Coffee — 2115 First St, Livermore. A downtown coffee original on the First Street corner since 1993. @panamabaycoffeeco

First Street Alehouse — 2106 First St, Livermore. A downtown gastropub since 2000, twenty-eight rotating taps. @firststreetalehouse

Lappert's Ice Cream — 2130 First St, Livermore. The Kauai super-premium brand, scooping downtown since 2025. @lappertsicecreamlivermore

Therapy Stores — 2200 First St, Livermore. A family-owned, woman-led gift and lifestyle boutique since 1994. @therapystores

Seven downtown: the Bankhead, First Street Wine, Range Life, Panama Bay, the Alehouse, Lappert's, and Therapy. What is your First Street stop?

item.description: They call this stretch of Shattuck the Gourmet Ghetto, and it earned the name. Chez Panisse, the restaurant credited with inventing California cuisine, ope
item.content:encoded:
Berkeley, the Gourmet Ghetto

They call this stretch of Shattuck the Gourmet Ghetto, and it earned the name. Chez Panisse, the restaurant credited with inventing California cuisine, opened here in 1971 and the whole food scene grew up around it. Seven stops in the Gourmet Ghetto, Berkeley.

Chez Panisse — 1517 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Alice Waters opened it in 1971, the birthplace of California cuisine. @chezpanisse

The Cheese Board Collective — 1504 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A worker-owned cheese shop and bakery since 1967, with a cult pizzeria next door. @thecheeseboardcollective

Peet's Coffee — 2124 Vine St, Berkeley. The very first Peet's, opened in 1966, where American specialty coffee started. @peetscoffee

The Local Butcher Shop — 1600 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A whole-animal butcher from a Chez Panisse alum, worker-owned since 2021. @thelocalbutchershop

Masse's Pastries — 1469 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A French patisserie in North Berkeley since 1997.

Caravaggio Gelato Lab — 1797 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. An Italian gelateria run by a family that emigrated from Italy.

Epicurious Garden — 1511 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. An indoor gourmet food arcade of small vendors, open since 2006.

Seven in the Gourmet Ghetto: Chez Panisse, the Cheese Board, the first Peet's, the Local Butcher, Masse's, Caravaggio, and Epicurious Garden. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:

You have driven under the old Oaks marquee on Solano Avenue for years. The 1925 movie palace went dark in 2011 and reopened in 2024 as a climbing gym built inside the auditorium, marquee still lit. Six stops on Solano Avenue.

Zachary's Chicago Pizza — 1853 Solano Ave, Berkeley. The deep-dish institution since 1984, now employee-owned. @zacharyspizza

iScream — 1819 Solano Ave, Berkeley. A family shop making organic ice cream fresh daily. @iscreaminberkeley

Five Little Monkeys — 1240 Solano Ave, Albany. An independent toy store, the flagship since 2001. @fivelittlemonkeystoys

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Walnut Creek

Everyone knows Broadway Plaza for the chain stores. The better downtown Walnut Creek is a block over, anchored by the Lesher Center for the Arts, three theaters that draw 350,000 people a year. Seven stops in downtown Walnut Creek.

Lesher Center for the Arts — 1601 Civic Dr, Walnut Creek. Three theaters and 900 shows a year, downtown's cultural anchor since 1990. @leshercenter

Va de Vi Bistro and Wine Bar — 1511 Mt Diablo Blvd, Walnut Creek. Global small plates under a century-old oak in a hidden lane. @vadevibistro

The Model Bakery — 1315 N Main St, Walnut Creek. The Napa bakery whose English muffins made Oprah's Favorite Things. @modelbakery

Rooted Coffee Co — 1321 Locust St, Walnut Creek. A family-owned, plant-based coffee shop that started at farmers markets. @rootedcoffeeco

Milky Flakes — 1399 N Main St, Walnut Creek. Korean shaved ice and Hokkaido milk soft serve, new in 2026. @milkyflakeswc

Massimo Ristorante — 1604 Locust St, Walnut Creek. A family-owned Italian kitchen on Locust Street.

Seven downtown: the Lesher Center, Va de Vi, the Model Bakery, Rooted, Milky Flakes, King's Jewelers, and Massimo. What draws you to Walnut Creek?

Artis Coffee — 1717B Fourth St, Berkeley. A family-owned micro-roaster roasting on site since 2013. @artiscoffee

Builders Booksource — 1817 Fourth St, Berkeley. An independent bookstore for architecture and design since 1982. @buildersbooksource

item.content:encoded:
Oakland, Jack London Square

A broke teenager named Jack London borrowed money for college from the bartender at a tiny waterfront saloon, then put the place in his books. Heinold's First and Last Chance has poured at Jack London Square since 1883, its floor still tilted from the 1906 quake. Seven stops at Jack London Square, Oakland.

Heinold's First and Last Chance Saloon — 48 Webster St, Oakland. An 1883 waterfront bar where Jack London drank and studied, its floor tilted since the 1906 earthquake, a National Literary Landmark. @heinoldsoakland

Scott's Seafood Grill and Bar — 2 Broadway, Oakland. A waterfront seafood room known for its Sunday jazz brunch. @scottsseafood_jls

Cellarmaker Brewing — 300 Webster St, Oakland. A brewery and pizza taproom in the old Blue Bottle warehouse. @cellarmaker.oakland

Kitsch Coffee — 590 2nd St, Oakland. A new cafe tucked in the historic Narrative building. @kitschcoffeeoakland

Narrative — 590 2nd St, Oakland. The Bay Area's largest vintage design collective, in the old Iron Works building. @narrativeoakland

Jack London Square Farmers Market — Water Street, Oakland. A Sunday waterfront market running thirty-plus years. @jacklondonsqfm

USS Potomac — FDR Pier, Water St, Oakland. FDR's restored presidential yacht, the Floating White House, now a museum.

Seven on the waterfront: Heinold's, Scott's, Cellarmaker, Kitsch, Narrative, the Sunday market, and the USS Potomac. What pulls you to the square?

item.content:encoded:
Oakland, Uptown

A 1928 movie palace, a 1931 Art Deco landmark, a bakery in an old candy factory. Uptown Oakland is a few blocks of restored grandeur and late nights. Seven stops in Uptown Oakland.

Paramount Theatre — 2025 Broadway, Oakland. A 1931 Art Deco palace and National Historic Landmark, home of the Oakland Symphony. @oakparamount

item.title: East Bay Downtown Pleasanton
item.description: The illuminated PLEASANTON arch has spanned Main Street since 1932, put up by the Women's Improvement Club for 532 dollars in the depths of the Depression.
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Pleasanton

The illuminated PLEASANTON arch has spanned Main Street since 1932, put up by the Women's Improvement Club for 532 dollars in the depths of the Depression. It is one of the last original gateway arches left in California. Seven stops in downtown Pleasanton.

The Pleasanton Arch — Main Street at West Angela, Pleasanton. The neon gateway sign strung over Main since 1932, restored in 2005.

Meadowlark Dairy — 57 West Neal St, Pleasanton. A walk-up soft-serve counter serving the town since 1919, now fourth-generation family. @meadowlarkdairy

The Rose Hotel — 807 Main St, Pleasanton. A thirty-four-room European-style boutique hotel in the heart of Main. @therosehotelpleasanton

Inklings Coffee and Tea — 530 Main St, Pleasanton. A longtime downtown gathering spot pouring Stumptown coffee. @inklingscoffee

Primrose Bakery — 350 Main St, Pleasanton. A European dessert bakery known for its sculpted art cakes. @primrosebakeryusa

Strizzi's Restaurant — 649 Main St, Pleasanton. The longest-running downtown restaurant, Italian on Main for thirty-five years. @strizzis

Towne Center Books — 555 Main St, Pleasanton. An independent bookstore on Main since 1993. @townecenterbks

Seven on Main: the arch, Meadowlark, the Rose Hotel, Inklings, Primrose, Strizzi's, and Towne Center Books. What is your downtown Pleasanton stop?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: Oakland, Old Oakland
item.description: The brick storefronts along 9th Street went up between 1868 and 1884. Most people cut through Old Oakland to get somewhere else and never look up at them.
item.content:encoded:
Oakland, Old Oakland

The brick storefronts along 9th Street went up between 1868 and 1884. Most people cut through Old Oakland to get somewhere else and never look up at them. Seven stops around 9th and Washington, the Victorian blocks downtown.

Swan's Market — 510 9th St, Oakland. A public market hall since 1917, now a dozen food stalls under one roof, closed Sundays. @swansmarket

The Cook and Her Farmer — Inside Swan's Market, Oakland. An oyster bar and natural wine cafe, coastal Southern cooking, garden seats by the Washington St door. @thecookandherfarmer

Delage — 536 9th St, Oakland. An eight course omakase from chef Chikara Ono, in the Michelin Guide, Thursday through Sunday only. @delage_oakland

Huangcheng Noodle House — 911 Washington St, Oakland. Shanxi knife shaved noodles cut to order, regulars go for the Chongqing bowl. @huangchengnoodles

Oeste — 722 Clay St, Oakland. A rooftop deck bar and kitchen, Latin and Southern plates, DJs on weekends. @oeste.bar.cafe

Sante Adairius Oakland Arbor — 460 8th St, Oakland. The Capitola cult brewery's taproom for saisons and wild ales, in the old Trappist space. @rusticales_oaklandarbor

Studio Noir — 471B 9th St, Oakland. A woman owned tattoo and permanent cosmetics collective, walk ins welcome. @studionoiroakland

Old Oakland in two blocks: Swan's Market, the Cook and Her Farmer, Delage, Huangcheng, Oeste, Sante Adairius, Studio Noir. Which one gets your Friday night?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Point Richmond
item.description: Point Richmond is a five block triangle wrapped around a hotel that opened in 1911. It sits between the bay and the hills, and most of the East Bay has nev
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Point Richmond

Point Richmond is a five block triangle wrapped around a hotel that opened in 1911. It sits between the bay and the hills, and most of the East Bay has never walked it. Seven stops in the old town.

Hotel Mac — 50 Washington Ave, Point Richmond. The 1911 landmark on the National Register, now home to Biancoverde for Italian plates and a real bar. @biancoverde_at_hotelmac

Kaleidoscope Coffee — 109 Park Place, Point Richmond. Coffee and ice cream by day, open mic and live music by night, since 2015. @kaleidoscope__coffee

Little Louie's Cafe — 49 Washington Ave, Point Richmond. Breakfast and lunch with house baked breads, the corner the regulars claim. @littlelouiescafe

Yoly's Roma Caffe and Bar — 401 S Garrard Blvd, Point Richmond. Family owned, pours Peet's, breakfast and lunch plus beer and wine across from the Plunge. @romacaffeandbar

Up and Under Pub and Grill — 2 W Richmond Ave, Point Richmond. A rugby tavern with American pub grub and DJ nights on Thursdays. @upandunderpub

Masquers Playhouse — 105 Park Place, Point Richmond. An all volunteer community theatre that has staged shows since 1955. @masquersplayhouse

Point Richmond Market and Deli — 160 Washington Ave, Point Richmond. A family corner market with Boar's Head sandwiches and a deep beer and wine wall, open to 10pm. @pointrichmondmarketanddeli

Point Richmond in one loop: Hotel Mac, Kaleidoscope, Little Louie's, Yoly's Roma, Up and Under, Masquers, the Market and Deli. What would you hit first in the triangle?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Downtown Martinez
item.description: Martinez has been the Contra Costa county seat since 1850, and Joe DiMaggio was born downtown in 1914. Most people know it as a name on the freeway sign an
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Martinez

Martinez has been the Contra Costa county seat since 1850, and Joe DiMaggio was born downtown in 1914. Most people know it as a name on the freeway sign and nothing more. The regulars know Main Street. Eight stops downtown.

Barrelista Coffee House — 736 Main St, Martinez. Downtown's coffee anchor since 2014, pours wine and beer too. @barrelistacoffee

Barrel Aged — 736 Main St, Martinez. The craft cocktail bar on the same corner, voted Best of Martinez 2025. @barrelagedbar

Roxx on Main — 627 Main St, Martinez. Farm to table American with live music on weekends, a Readers' Choice winner four years running. @roxx_on_main

Troy Greek Cuisine — 720 Main St, Martinez. Gyros and Mediterranean plates, open daily. @troygreekcuisine

Del Cielo Brewing — 701 Escobar St, Martinez. A Latino owned family brewery since 2018, eighteen rotating taps a block off Main. @delcielobrewing

Slow Hand BBQ — 601 Main St, Martinez. Wood smoked barbecue with sixteen craft taps. @slowhandbbq_mtz

Fair Arrow Books and Goods — 816 Main St, Martinez. An independent bookshop and curated goods, open Wednesday through Sunday. @fairarrowbooks

Le Marche Emporium — 516 Ferry St, Martinez. Twelve thousand square feet of vintage and antiques, weekends only. @lemarcheemporium

Downtown Martinez end to end: Barrelista, Barrel Aged, Roxx, Troy, Del Cielo, Slow Hand, Fair Arrow, Le Marche. Which corner of the county seat are you starting on?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Downtown San Leandro
item.description: There is an 800 seat Art Deco movie palace from 1946 still running shows on East 14th Street. Downtown San Leandro gets written off as a BART stop between
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown San Leandro

There is an 800 seat Art Deco movie palace from 1946 still running shows on East 14th Street. Downtown San Leandro gets written off as a BART stop between Oakland and Hayward. It is more than that. Seven stops.

Bal Theatre — 14808 E 14th St, San Leandro. An 800 seat Art Deco house that opened in 1946, now live music and events. @baltheatre

Fieldwork Brewing — 1495 E 14th St, San Leandro. The brewery's largest beer garden, thirty two taps built around a seventy five year old olive tree. @fieldwork_sanleandro

Slice House by Tony Gemignani — 135 Parrott St, San Leandro. Pizza by the slice from a thirteen time world pizza champion. @slicehouse_sanleandro

Smack Burgers — 160 W Juana Ave, San Leandro. The pop up's first brick and mortar, smash burgers downtown. @smackburgers

Pelton Cafe — 194 Pelton Center Way, San Leandro. A breakfast and brunch diner in the Pelton Center walk. @thepeltoncafe

Zocalo Coffeehouse — 645 Bancroft Ave, San Leandro. A woman owned cafe and roastery, a twenty year neighborhood institution. @zocalocoffee

Paradiso — 685 Bancroft Ave, San Leandro. Italian with a Wine Spectator list, going on thirty years. @paradisosanleandro

Downtown San Leandro, more than a BART stop: Bal Theatre, Fieldwork, Slice House, Smack, Pelton Cafe, Zocalo, Paradiso. Which one changes your mind about the place?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Alameda, Webster Street
item.description: Park Street gets all of Alameda's attention. The West End, along Webster Street, quietly runs a pinball hall of a hundred machines and dim sum carts going
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Alameda, Webster Street

Park Street gets all of Alameda's attention. The West End, along Webster Street, quietly runs a pinball hall of a hundred machines and dim sum carts going since 1985. Seven stops most visitors skip.

Pacific Pinball Museum — 1510 Webster St, Alameda. A nonprofit hall of a hundred playable machines from the 1940s on, founded 2004. @pacificpinball

East Ocean Seafood — 1713 Webster St, Alameda. Hong Kong style cart dim sum, running since 1985. @east_ocean_seafood_restaurant

Domenico's Italian Deli — 1407 Webster St, Alameda. Hot pastrami and Chicago style Italian beef, a deli since 1982. @domenicositaliandeli

Calafia Taqueria — 1445 Webster St, Alameda. Family run since 2003, the owner is from Ensenada. @calafia.taqueria.oficial

Cafe Jolie — 1500 Webster St, Alameda. French American breakfast and brunch on the West End corner. @cafejolie

Coven of Stitches — 1602 Webster St, Alameda. A queer and BIPOC owned yarn shop, opened 2024. @covenofstitchesalameda

Cookiebar Scoop Shop — 1608 Webster St, Alameda. Small batch ice cream with non dairy scoops. @cookiebarscoopshop

Alameda's West End on Webster Street: Pacific Pinball, East Ocean, Domenico's, Calafia, Cafe Jolie, Coven of Stitches, Cookiebar. Park Street or Webster, where do you land?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Downtown Hayward, B Street
item.description: America's first modern brewpub opened on B Street in Hayward in 1983. Buffalo Bill's is still there, and the rest of downtown grew up around that stretch.
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Hayward, B Street

America's first modern brewpub opened on B Street in Hayward in 1983. Buffalo Bill's is still there, and the rest of downtown grew up around that stretch. Seven stops on B Street and the block beside it.

Buffalo Bill's Brewery — 1082 B St, Hayward. Bill Owens opened it in 1983 as America's first modern brewpub, back under new owners since 2023. @buffalobillsbrewery

Books on B — 1014 B St, Hayward. An independent bookstore run by a longtime local bookseller. @booksonb

The Bistro — 1001 B St, Hayward. Craft beer and live music nightly since 1994, open mic on Mondays. @thebistro.hayward

The Dirty Bird Lounge — 926 B St, Hayward. Argentinian plates and craft cocktails, trivia and karaoke nights. @thedirtybirdlounge

Con Azucar Cafe — 1099 B St, Hayward. A Latin cafe known for supersized conchas, opened downtown in 2026. @conazucarcafe

Ghazni Afghan Kabobs — 1235 A St, Hayward. Family run halal Afghan kabobs a block over on A Street. @ghazniafghankabobs

Hayward Public Library — 888 C St, Hayward. The 21st Century Library, an airy community hub with a cafe and bookable rooms. @haywardlibrary

Downtown Hayward on and around B Street: Buffalo Bill's, Books on B, the Bistro, the Dirty Bird, Con Azucar, Ghazni, the library. Which one surprises you most?

item.title: Berkeley, Telegraph Avenue
item.description: Records, used books, and a slice at 1am. Four blocks of Telegraph below the Berkeley campus have sold all three since before you were born. Amoeba opened i
item.content:encoded:
Berkeley, Telegraph Avenue

Records, used books, and a slice at 1am. Four blocks of Telegraph below the Berkeley campus have sold all three since before you were born. Amoeba opened its first ever store here in 1990, Moe's has been around since 1959. Seven stops.

Amoeba Music — 2455 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. The original Amoeba, opened 1990 and now billed as the world's largest independent record store. @amoebaberkeley

Moe's Books — 2476 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. Four floors of used and new books since 1959, Moe Moskowitz's shop. @moes_books

Rasputin Music — 2401 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. The Bay Area's biggest indie record chain, founded right here in 1971. @rasputinmusicberkeley

Sliver Pizzeria — 2468 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. One rotating pizza a day, posted every morning. @sliverpizzeria

Blondie's Pizza — 2340 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. Grab and go slices, the late night Cal standby. @blondiespizzaberkeley

Top Dog — 2534 Durant Ave, Berkeley. Grilled sausages and dogs since 1966, open past 2am. @topdog_us

Kiraku — 2566B Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. A cozy izakaya for sake and small plates, dinner only. @kirakuberkeley

Southside Telegraph in Berkeley: Amoeba, Moe's, Rasputin, Sliver, Blondie's, Top Dog, Kiraku. Records first or a slice first?

item.title: East Bay Downtown Pleasant Hill
item.description: Before July 4, 2000, this corner of Pleasant Hill was blighted strip mall land. The city cleared it and built an open air Main Street from scratch. Twenty
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Pleasant Hill

Before July 4, 2000, this corner of Pleasant Hill was blighted strip mall land. The city cleared it and built an open air Main Street from scratch. Twenty five years later it is where the county goes on a Friday night. Six stops downtown.

Jack's Restaurant and Bar — 60 Crescent Dr, Pleasant Hill. The all day American anchor, breakfast through dinner. @welovejacks

Crescent Bistro — 45 Crescent Dr, Pleasant Hill. From scratch New American and craft cocktails in the middle of the town center. @crescentbistro

Zachary's Chicago Pizza — 140 Crescent Dr, Pleasant Hill. The employee owned deep dish institution Bay Area people argue about. @zacharyspizza

Batter N Icing — 65B Crescent Dr, Pleasant Hill. An independent cupcake and custom cake bakery, opened 2023. @batter_n_icing

The Royale — 2190 Contra Costa Blvd, Pleasant Hill. A contemporary American brunch and dinner destination. @theroyaleeatery.ph

The Golf Spot Bay Area — 714 Contra Costa Blvd, Pleasant Hill. Indoor golf with two Trackman bays and a putting green. @thegolfspotbayarea

Downtown Pleasant Hill, built from a parking lot: Jack's, Crescent Bistro, Zachary's, Batter N Icing, the Royale, the Golf Spot. What would you add to the list?

item.title: Oakland, Fruitvale
item.description: Every fall, more than a hundred thousand people fill the streets of Fruitvale for the Bay Area's biggest Dia de los Muertos, a tradition here since 1996. T
item.content:encoded:
Oakland, Fruitvale

Every fall, more than a hundred thousand people fill the streets of Fruitvale for the Bay Area's biggest Dia de los Muertos, a tradition here since 1996. The rest of the year the neighborhood feeds you just as well. Seven stops along International.

Tacos Sinaloa — 2138 International Blvd, Oakland. A taco truck that grew into a corner institution, al pastor off the trompo, open late. @tacos_sinaloa_oakland

Otaez — 3872 International Blvd, Oakland. A sit down Fruitvale mainstay for chile rellenos, carnitas, and pozole, full bar. @otaez_oakland

El Huarache Azteca — 3842 International Blvd, Oakland. Mexico City cooking since 2001, the namesake huaraches are the order. @elhuaracheazteca_

Nieves Cinco de Mayo — 3340 E 12th St, Oakland. Ice cream hand churned over ice and salt, mango chamoy and leche quemada, inside the Fruitvale Public Market. @nievescincodemayooak

Guadalajara Restaurant — 1001 Fruitvale Ave, Oakland. Open seven days from breakfast to late, known for the weekend menudo.

Fruitvale Public Market — 3340 E 12th St, Oakland. An indoor outdoor Latino food hall by the BART plaza, paletas to pupusas under one roof.

Peralta Hacienda Historical Park — 2465 34th Ave, Oakland. Six acres around an 1870 adobe, a museum of Oakland's early families, grounds open to sunset. @peraltahaciendahp

Fruitvale, more than a festival: Tacos Sinaloa, Otaez, El Huarache Azteca, Nieves, Guadalajara, the Public Market, Peralta Hacienda. Which one do you start with?

item.description: Berkeley has exactly one commercial movie house left, and it has been running on College Avenue since 1914. It anchors the Elmwood, six blocks that never t
item.content:encoded:
Berkeley, Elmwood

Berkeley has exactly one commercial movie house left, and it has been running on College Avenue since 1914. It anchors the Elmwood, six blocks that never turned into a mall. Seven stops.

Rialto Cinemas Elmwood — 2966 College Ave, Berkeley. The 1914 neighborhood theater, now with beer and wine, Berkeley's last commercial movie house. @rialtocinemaselmwood

Mrs — Dalloway's. 2904 College Ave, Berkeley. A literary and garden bookstore known for its author events. @mrsdalloways

La Mediterranee — 2936 College Ave, Berkeley. Serving the Elmwood since 1982, the chicken pomegranate and meza plates. @cafelamed_berkeley

Summer Kitchen Bake Shop — 2944 College Ave, Berkeley. A seasonal cafe and bakery, rotisserie chicken and pastries. @summerkitchenbakeshop

Cafenated Coffee — 2960 College Ave, Berkeley. An all day cafe and wine bar that revived the old coffee corner at College and Ashby. @cafenatedcoffeeco

In the Wood — 2930 College Ave, Berkeley. A neighborhood gastropub pouring local craft beer. @inthewoodberkeley

The Italian Homemade Company — 2905 College Ave, Berkeley. Fresh handmade pasta and focaccia at the counter. @italianhomemadecompany

The Elmwood on College Avenue: Rialto, Mrs. Dalloway's, La Mediterranee, Summer Kitchen, Cafenated, In the Wood, Italian Homemade. What is your Elmwood afternoon?

item.title: East Bay Stockton, the Miracle Mile
item.description: The palm trees along Pacific Avenue in Stockton were shipped up from a Los Angeles nursery in the 1920s so the street would match the original Miracle Mile
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Stockton, the Miracle Mile

The palm trees along Pacific Avenue in Stockton were shipped up from a Los Angeles nursery in the 1920s so the street would match the original Miracle Mile in LA. A century later the Mile is still Stockton's front porch. Seven stops.

Gian's Italian Deli — 2112 Pacific Ave, Stockton. Bolognini family Northern Italian deli, house made raviolis on homemade focaccia, forty years on the Mile. @giansdeli

Cocoro Bistro — 2105 Pacific Ave, Stockton. Sushi and izakaya plates, creative rolls in the heart of the Mile. @cocorobistro

Whirlow's Tossed and Grilled — 1926 Pacific Ave, Stockton. Build your own tossed salads and grilled sandwiches, a Mile mainstay. @whirlows

Taps Barrel House — 1924 Pacific Ave, Stockton. Twenty eight rotating taps and the High Water Brewing tasting room, food from Whirlow's next door. @tapsbarrelhouse

AVE on the Mile — 2333 Pacific Ave, Stockton. An upscale lounge and bistro, Sunday brunch with live music. @aveonthemile

Ululani's Hawaiian Shave Ice — 2130 Pacific Ave, Stockton. Maui founded shave ice with house made syrups. @ululanishawaiianshaveice.stkn

Creperie Le Pompon — 2319 N Pacific Ave, Stockton. French sweet and savory crepes, open daily for breakfast and lunch.

Stockton's Miracle Mile end to end: Gian's, Cocoro, Whirlow's, Taps, AVE, Ululani's, Le Pompon. Which is your first stop on Pacific?

item.description: Everyone points the car at Napa. Ninety minutes the other direction, Lodi has quietly been the Zinfandel capital, and it strung its Mission arch over the r
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Lodi

Everyone points the car at Napa. Ninety minutes the other direction, Lodi has quietly been the Zinfandel capital, and it strung its Mission arch over the road in 1907. School Street downtown is the reason to stay. Seven stops.

The Dancing Fox — 203 S School St, Lodi. A winery, brewery, bakery, and restaurant under one roof, breads from a wood fired oven. @dancingfoxwinery

Cheese Central — 11 N School St, Lodi. Over a hundred cheeses plus a local pantry, with tastings and classes. @cheesecentrallodi

Lodi Beer Company — 105 S School St, Lodi. A downtown brewpub since 2004, house brewed in an old tavern room. @lodibeerco

Papapavlo's — 223 N School St, Lodi. Greek and Mediterranean, a family business since 1988. @papapavloslodi

Smack Pie Pizza — 121 S School St, Lodi. Build your own pizza, one size one price, out in about four minutes. @smackpiepizza

Brick House Restaurant and Lounge — 27 W Elm St, Lodi. Italian American plates a half block off School Street. @brickhousedining

Scotto's Wine and Cider — 14 S School St, Lodi. Lodi appellation wines and small batch hard cider, live music on weekends.

Downtown Lodi on School Street: Dancing Fox, Cheese Central, Lodi Beer, Papapavlo's, Smack Pie, Brick House, Scotto's. Napa or Lodi this weekend?

There is an old downtown behind the Brentwood most people know from the freeway outlets. Oak Street runs through the heart of what was once some of the richest cherry and corn country in California. Seven stops in the old town.

MJ's Downtown Cafe and Bakery — 655 First St, Brentwood. Family run since 2010 with an onsite bakery, the town's top rated breakfast. @mjsdowntowncafe

Locanda Capri — 301 Oak St, Brentwood. House made pasta and wood fired pizza on the corner that was Sweeney's. @locanda.capri

Brentwood Craft Beer and Cider — 234 Oak St, Brentwood. A family owned all ages taproom, open since 2019. @brentwoodcraft

311 Oak Street Pub — 311 Oak St, Brentwood. A downtown pub with weekend brunch. @311oakst

The Lounge on Oak — 220 Oak St, Brentwood. A cocktail lounge, Sunday R and B brunch with mimosa flights. @thelounge.brentwood

Chrome Coffee — 637 First St, Brentwood. An independent coffee bar next to the historic Delta Theater. @chrome.coffee

La Costa Taqueria — 335 Oak St, Brentwood. Counter serve homestyle Mexican with a patio, open daily. @lacosta.brentwood

Old downtown Brentwood on Oak Street: MJ's, Locanda Capri, Brentwood Craft, 311 Oak, the Lounge, Chrome, La Costa. What is your stop in the old town?

item.content:encoded:

In 1996 the neighbors killed a Starbucks before it could open on Park Boulevard. That storefront is a wood fired Italian restaurant now, and the Glenview stayed independent. Six stops.

Bellanico — 4238 Park Blvd, Oakland. A seasonal Italian wine bar, on the corridor since 2008, named for the owners' daughters. @bellanicorestaurant_oakland

Park Burger — 4218 Park Blvd, Oakland. Grass fed burgers and a beer list of all Oakland breweries. @parkburgeroak

Paulista Brazilian Kitchen — 4239 Park Blvd, Oakland. A Brazilian cafe and taproom, acai bowls and coxinhas, since 2017. @paulista510

Glenview Taqueria — 4207 Park Blvd, Oakland. Tacos and burritos, opened 2024 from the owner of the neighborhood market. @glenviewtaqueria

IDIL VICE — 4193 Park Blvd, Oakland. An upscale streetwear boutique in a historic Tudor house. @idilvice

item.content:encoded:
Berkeley, the Downtown Arts District

A Tony winning theater, a folk music hall running since 1968, and a 1917 movie palace turned concert stage. They sit within three blocks of each other in downtown Berkeley, and most people come for one show and leave. Seven stops.

Berkeley Repertory Theatre — 2025 Addison St, Berkeley. The East Bay's Tony winning regional theater, two stages on the arts block. @berkeleyrep

The Freight — 2020 Addison St, Berkeley. Freight and Salvage, a nonprofit folk and world music coffeehouse running since 1968. @thefreightberkeley

The UC Theatre — 2036 University Ave, Berkeley. A 1917 movie palace reborn as an all ages concert hall. @theuctheatre

California Jazz Conservatory — 2087 Addison St, Berkeley. A jazz school with an intimate concert hall on the Addison arts block. @californiajazzconservatory

Comal — 2020 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Oaxaca leaning Mexican with a back bar and patio, a Michelin Bib Gourmand. @comalrestaurants

Jupiter — 2181 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Wood fired pizza and house beer in an 1890s livery stable, with a garden and live music. @jupiterberkeley

Angeline's Louisiana Kitchen — 2261 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. New Orleans cooking, beignets and gumbo, before or after the show. @angelineslouisianakitchen

Downtown Berkeley's arts blocks: Berkeley Rep, the Freight, the UC Theatre, the Jazz Conservatory, Comal, Jupiter, Angeline's. What show gets you across the bridge?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Orinda

Long before BART tunneled through the hills, Orinda already had a movie palace. The 1941 theater still lights its neon fin over Theatre Square, and the county's oldest restaurant has been frying chicken here since 1932. Six stops.

Orinda Theatre — 4 Orinda Theatre Square, Orinda. A 1941 Streamline Moderne cinema with a neon fin marquee, still showing films. @theorindatheatre

Casa Orinda — 20 Bryant Way, Orinda. Open since 1932, Contra Costa's oldest restaurant, famous for the fried chicken. @casaorinda

Loard's Ice Cream and Candies — 230 Brookwood Rd, Orinda. An Orinda scoop and candy shop since 1952. @loardsorinda

Zamboni's Pizza — 1 Camino Sobrante, Orinda. The neighborhood pizzeria off Theatre Square. @zambonispc

The Fourth Bore Tap Room and Grill — 2 Orinda Theatre Square, Orinda. A brewpub with twenty eight taps and live music, named for the Caldecott tunnel. @fourthboretaproom

Shelby's — 2 Theatre Square, Orinda. A scratch kitchen with a seasonal California menu in Theatre Square.

Orinda around Theatre Square: the 1941 theater, Casa Orinda, Loard's, Zamboni's, the Fourth Bore, Shelby's. What would you see at the Orinda?

item.title: East Bay Vegan Kitchens
item.description: Vegan in the East Bay is not a sad salad. It is New Orleans soul food, a Vietnamese kitchen gone meatless since 1996, and a Berkeley deli that out sandwich
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Vegan Kitchens

Vegan in the East Bay is not a sad salad. It is New Orleans soul food, a Vietnamese kitchen gone meatless since 1996, and a Berkeley deli that out sandwiches the butcher. Seven fully plant based spots that win over the skeptics at the table.

The Butcher's Son — 1954 University Ave, Berkeley. A fully vegan deli and bakery where the sandwiches and pastries convert the doubters, open seven days. @thebutchersson_official

Souley Vegan — 101 Broadway, Oakland. Chef Tamearra Dyson's plant based New Orleans soul food, running since 2009, now in Jack London Square. @souleyvegan

Golden Lotus Vegan — 1301 Franklin St, Oakland. One of Oakland's oldest vegan kitchens, family run in Chinatown since 1996, Vietnamese and pan Asian plates. @goldenlotusvegan

Timeless Coffee — 4252 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. A one hundred percent vegan coffee roaster and bakery on Piedmont Ave, with a second cafe on Webster. @timelesscoffee

Cha-Ya — 1686 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A fully vegan Japanese kitchen, tempura and noodle bowls done entirely plant based, lunch and dinner. @chayaberkeley

Blossom Vegan — 4000 Pimlico Dr, Pleasanton. A fully vegan soul food and Southern kitchen out in the Tri Valley, Wednesday through Sunday. @blossom_vegan_restaurant

Go Vegan — 2940 Delta Fair Blvd, Antioch. A dedicated plant based Vietnamese kitchen in East County, open every day but Saturday.

Seven plant based, Berkeley to Antioch: The Butcher's Son and Cha-Ya in Berkeley, Souley Vegan, Golden Lotus and Timeless in Oakland, Blossom in Pleasanton, and Go Vegan in Antioch. Which one converts your carnivore friend?

item.title: East Bay Caribbean and Jamaican Kitchens
item.description: Oakland jerk did not disappear when the famous names changed hands. The chef behind the old Kingston 11 fired his griddle back up in Uptown, and Trinidad a
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Caribbean and Jamaican Kitchens

Oakland jerk did not disappear when the famous names changed hands. The chef behind the old Kingston 11 fired his griddle back up in Uptown, and Trinidad and Jamaica still run this town, oxtail off the bone, curry goat, escovitch snapper. Five Caribbean kitchens, Oakland to Stockton.

Calabash — 2300 Valdez St, Oakland. Chef Nigel Jones, Kingston born and the name behind the old Kingston 11, reopened in Uptown in 2022 with jerk and curry done right. @calabasheats

Cocobreeze Caribbean Restaurant and Bakery — 2370 High St, Oakland. A Trinidadian kitchen from chef Annabelle Goodridge, curry goat and roti with a bakery case on the side, open limited days so check first. @cocobreezeco

Sweet Fingers — 1707 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The long running Jamaican spot for jerk chicken and oxtail, just reopened at a new Telegraph Avenue address in 2026. @sweetfingersjamaican

Fiya Spice Caribbean — 1343 Buchanan Rd, Pittsburg. A husband and wife kitchen in East County, oxtail and curry goat and jerk with escovitch red snapper, open daily. @fiyaspice

CJ's Jamaican and BBQ Kitchen — 4368 N Sutter St, Stockton. Jerk chicken and Jamaican curry up in San Joaquin, lunch hours only Monday through Wednesday so time it right.

Five for the oxtail: Calabash and Cocobreeze in Oakland, Sweet Fingers back on Telegraph, Fiya Spice in Pittsburg, and CJ's up in Stockton. Which plate do you order, oxtail or curry goat?
