item.title: East Bay Dog Parks
item.description: Point Isabel is the largest off-leash dog park on the West Coast, twenty three acres of Richmond shoreline with the San Francisco skyline across the water.
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Dog Parks

Point Isabel is the largest off-leash dog park on the West Coast, twenty three acres of Richmond shoreline with the San Francisco skyline across the water. Nine East Bay dog parks worth the drive.

Point Isabel Regional Shoreline — 2701 Isabel St, Richmond. Twenty three acres of off-leash Bay shoreline with the Mudpuppy's dog wash right at the entrance. @ebrpd

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. A ninety acre off-leash hilltop on the Berkeley Marina, kite hill and Bay Bridge views, shorter lines than Point Isabel.

Hardy Dog Park — 491 Hardy St, Oakland. A fenced off-leash run under the College Ave overpass, separate small and large dog sections, where the regulars know every dog by name.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3590 Sanborn Dr, Oakland. Off-leash trails inside the redwoods that most newcomers never explore, cooler in summer than the flatlands.

Hap Magee Ranch Park — 1025 La Gonda Way, Danville. Two fenced runs, small and large dogs separated, worth the drive even from Oakland.

Heather Farm Dog Park — 505 N San Carlos Dr, Walnut Creek. A big well kept run with a water station where most of the local dogs are regulars.

Mountain View Cemetery — 5000 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Leashed only, a 1.8 mile paved loop with Bay views and a quiet the dogs respond to. @mountainviewcemetery.oakland

Ohlone Dog Park — 1800 Hearst Ave, Berkeley. A fully fenced run, one of the first official off-leash dog parks in the country.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. Off-leash on the old landfill peninsula, with public art, Bay views, and a sculpture trail.

Nine East Bay dog parks: Point Isabel, Cesar Chavez, Hardy, Joaquin Miller, Hap Magee, Heather Farm, Mountain View, Ohlone, and the Albany Bulb. Where does your dog run?

item.title: East Bay Sunrise Hikes
item.description: Mission Peak releases its sunrise hike permits 24 hours ahead, and almost nobody knows the early window exists. Nine East Bay spots worth setting the alarm
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sunrise Hikes

Mission Peak releases its sunrise hike permits 24 hours ahead, and almost nobody knows the early window exists. Nine East Bay spots worth setting the alarm for, summits and ridges and shoreline before the city wakes.

Mission Peak — Stanford Ave staging, 43600 Mission Blvd, Fremont. Sunrise permits release 24 hours in advance, the 5am climb beats the crowd and the heat. @ebrpd

Mount Diablo summit — Summit Rd, Mount Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. Drive up and park at the visitor center, the Bay opens up by 6:30 most mornings. @castateparks

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The four mile paved Nimitz Way, easy at 5am, with the fog peeling off by 7.

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The highest point in the East Bay park system, a five minute walk from the lot off Grizzly Peak Blvd.

Wildcat Peak — Tilden Nature Area, Berkeley. A shorter, less crowded climb than Mission Peak with the same Bay wide payoff, a stone lookout at the top.

Joaquin Miller ridge — 3450 Joaquin Miller Rd, Oakland. The least visited sunrise spot here, park at the upper lots and walk five minutes to the view.

Sibley Volcanic Preserve — 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. The Round Top trail, where the bay haze burns off around 7:30 and the volcano ridge opens up.

Berkeley Marina kite hill — Cesar Chavez Park, 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. Flat and wide open, the sun comes up behind the hills and lights the whole bay.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. A flat ten minute walk out to the Bay's edge, the skyline catching first light across the water.

Nine before the city wakes: Mission Peak, Diablo, Inspiration Point, Vollmer, Wildcat Peak, Joaquin Miller, Sibley, the Berkeley kite hill, and the Albany Bulb. Which sunrise gets you up?

item.title: East Bay Sunset Spots
item.description: From Mount Diablo's summit on a clear day you can see over 8,500 square miles, parts of 40 California counties in one look. You do not need the summit thou
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sunset Spots

From Mount Diablo's summit on a clear day you can see over 8,500 square miles, parts of 40 California counties in one look. You do not need the summit though. Eight East Bay sunset spots, most a short walk or no walk at all.

Mount Diablo summit — Summit Rd, Mount Diablo State Park, Walnut Creek. The 3,849 foot peak, on the clearest evenings the view reaches the Sierra crest. @castateparks

Grizzly Peak Boulevard — Kensington to Skyline Blvd, Berkeley and Oakland hills. Pull off at any named viewpoint for the full Bay in one frame, the drive is the date.

Inspiration Point — Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. A paved ridge trail, thirty minutes round trip, to the bench locals call the seat of the East Bay. @ebrpd

Vollmer Peak — Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. The highest summit in the Berkeley hills, a 360 degree view, and an easy fire road climb.

Joaquin Miller Park — 3590 Sanborn Dr, Oakland. A eucalyptus path to a sunset bench, the local spot when Grizzly Peak is jammed.

Sibley Volcanic Preserve — 6800 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. A volcano you can hike, with Mount Tam turning pink across the Bay at sunset.

Cesar Chavez Park — 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley. Kite hill on the Berkeley Marina, a full Bay view and no climb required.

Albany Bulb — Foot of Buchanan St, Albany. The Bay's edge with a sculpture trail above, a different sunset every visit.

Eight for golden hour: Diablo, Grizzly Peak, Inspiration Point, Vollmer, Joaquin Miller, Sibley, Cesar Chavez, and the Albany Bulb. Where do you watch it drop?

item.title: East Bay Poke Counters
item.description: Poke stopped being a fad and settled into a real East Bay habit, from a chef run counter by the Berkeley campus to a 680 corridor cluster where Walnut Cree
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Poke Counters

Poke stopped being a fad and settled into a real East Bay habit, from a chef run counter by the Berkeley campus to a 680 corridor cluster where Walnut Creek alone has two. Sushi grade fish, build your own bowls, no bridge. Seven poke counters worth the lunch break.

Hashtag Poki — 3075 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. A sushi chef run poke spot near the campus since 2016, sushi grade fish and build your own bowls, weekdays only. @hashtagpoki

Poke Parlor — 2485 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. Build your own bowls with house made sauces and Asian and Latin twists, even poke tacos, on Telegraph near campus.

Oke Poke — 1529 Locust St, Walnut Creek. Seven signature bowls plus build your own and pokerritos, open daily on Locust. @okepokeco

Pokeatery — 1345 Newell Ave, Walnut Creek. A Walnut Creek poke shop since 2018 known for the Dole Whip float alongside the bowls. @pokeatery

Poke Don — 2491 San Ramon Valley Blvd, San Ramon. A San Ramon counter regulars praise for the ahi and albacore, lunch and early dinner, closed Sundays.

Poke Salad — 1213 W March Ln, Stockton. An independent Stockton poke shop, build your own bowls, Monday through Saturday. @pokesaladstockton

Ahipoki Bowl — 4932 Pacific Ave, Stockton. Open late daily on Pacific Ave for a build your own bowl past nine at night. @ahipoki

Seven bowls, Berkeley to Stockton: Hashtag Poki and Poke Parlor in Berkeley, Oke Poke and Pokeatery in Walnut Creek, Poke Don in San Ramon, and Poke Salad and Ahipoki in Stockton. What is in your bowl?

item.title: East Bay Peruvian Kitchens
item.description: The Bay's best ceviche is not across the bridge. Maria Fiestas brought the kitchens of Callao, Peru to Jack London Square in 1999, and the East Bay has run
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Peruvian Kitchens

The Bay's best ceviche is not across the bridge. Maria Fiestas brought the kitchens of Callao, Peru to Jack London Square in 1999, and the East Bay has run deep on ceviche and lomo saltado ever since. Seven East Bay Peruvian kitchens, Oakland to the Tri Valley.

La Furia Chalaca — 310 Broadway, Oakland. Maria Fiestas opened this Callao kitchen in Jack London Square in 1999, ceviche and lomo saltado with weekend live music. @chalacaoakland

La Costa Peruvian Cuisine — 3625 International Blvd, Oakland. A family run Fruitvale spot where the ceviche, lomo saltado, and aji de gallina are the standing orders. @lacostaperuvian

Asu Mare — 6211 Shattuck Ave, Oakland. A Peruvian kitchen on the Oakland Berkeley line, closed Tuesdays, the ceviche and saltado plates the draw. @asumare81

Lucuma Kitchen and Bar — 1700 Franklin St, Oakland. A downtown room known for anticuchos de corazon and a Peruvian cocktail bar. @lucumakitchenoak

Bravazo — 428 Main St, Pleasanton. A downtown Pleasanton Peruvian with breakfast and empanadas, opened in 2025. @bravazo.foods

El Mono — 11720 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito. A family owned fast casual Peruvian counter doing aji de gallina, lomo saltado, and ceviche.

El Tunante — San Leandro. A family run spot with the saltado dishes and Peruvian Chinese chifa fusion plates.

Seven for the ceviche: La Furia Chalaca, La Costa, Asu Mare, Lucuma, Bravazo in Pleasanton, El Mono in El Cerrito, and El Tunante in San Leandro. Which plate resets your standard?

item.title: East Bay Bike Shops
item.description: There is a shop on Piedmont Ave that stocks hand built Italian and titanium frames most people only ever see in magazines, and the mechanics will still fix
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Bike Shops

There is a shop on Piedmont Ave that stocks hand built Italian and titanium frames most people only ever see in magazines, and the mechanics will still fix your flat while you wait. Five East Bay bike shops for the ride and the repair.

Montano Velo — 4266 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. The high end room on Piedmont Ave, Moots titanium and Pinarello alongside a service bench that treats a commuter tune like a race build. Dream bikes and honest wrenching.

Alameda Bicycle — 1522 Park St, Alameda. The island's Park Street shop for decades, deep on families and commuters, the place that sets up a kid's first pedal bike right. @alamedabicycle

Mike's Bikes — 1824 University Ave, Berkeley. The Berkeley flagship of the local chain, a big floor of road, gravel, and electric with a trade in program and a no pressure fit. @mikesbikes

Tip Top Bike Shop — 4800A Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Temescal fixture strong on used bikes and quick repairs, the neighborhood spot that gets you rolling without the upsell. Bring the beater, leave on a bike that works.

Solano Avenue Cyclery — 1554 Solano Ave, Berkeley. The Solano Avenue shop that has quietly fixed North Berkeley's flats for years, knowledgeable, unfussy, and fast on a walk in.

Five for the ride and the repair: Montano Velo, Alameda Bicycle, Mike's Bikes, Tip Top, and Solano Avenue Cyclery. Who tunes your ride?

item.title: East Bay Juice, Smoothie and Acai Bars
item.description: Juice Appeal has cold pressed Berkeley's carrots and kale since 2000, back when a green juice still made people wince. The East Bay wellness run is real. S
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Juice, Smoothie and Acai Bars

Juice Appeal has cold pressed Berkeley's carrots and kale since 2000, back when a green juice still made people wince. The East Bay wellness run is real. Six juice bars and acai counters worth the reset.

Juice Appeal — 2144 Kala Bagai Way, Berkeley. Berkeley's original fresh press since 2000, cold pressed juice, green smoothies, and acai bowls a block off downtown BART. The ginger shot that clears your head.

Main Squeeze Organic Juicery — 2300 Central Ave, Alameda. Every juice, bowl, and enhancer certified organic, the island counter locals swear by for a clean start. Add the bee pollen and mean it.

Palm Acai Cafe — 2979 College Ave, Berkeley. The Elmwood cafe built around the bowl, the Hunter and the Gatherer piled with nut butter and fresh fruit. Sunny patio, no rush.

Brazuca Acai — 4500 Barrett Ave, Richmond. The real Brazilian thing, thick acai the way Rio serves it, plus pao de queijo and Brazilian pastries. Seven days a week, worth the Richmond drive. @brazuca.acaii

Minto's Jamaican Patties and Juice Bar — 1405 Franklin St, Oakland. Downtown Oakland's stop for sorrel, ginger, and soursop juices next to a hot beef patty. Lunch and a cure in one window.

Juice and Java Express — 55 W Angela St, Pleasanton. The Tri-Valley grab and go for fresh juice and organic coffee, the quick honest reset before the drive home.

Six for the reset, Berkeley to Pleasanton: Juice Appeal, Main Squeeze, Palm Acai, Brazuca, Minto's, and Juice and Java. What is in your go to blend?

item.title: East Bay Nepalese and Himalayan Kitchens
item.description: Cafe Tibet has been the East Bay's only Tibetan kitchen since 1999, and when the next generation took over they turned the whole menu vegan without losing
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Nepalese and Himalayan Kitchens

Cafe Tibet has been the East Bay's only Tibetan kitchen since 1999, and when the next generation took over they turned the whole menu vegan without losing a single momo. Seven Himalayan tables for momos, thukpa, and dal bhat.

Cafe Tibet — 2020 University Ave, Berkeley. The East Bay's Tibetan original since 1999, now fully vegan, fifty dishes deep, the steamed momos and the tingmo bread still the move. Downtown Berkeley, unhurried. @cafe.tibet

Shangri-La Vegan — 4905 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Tibetan Buddhist vegan kitchen in Temescal with a daily changing set menu, homemade and calm, the momos and greens done fully without meat.

Taste of the Himalayas — 1700 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. North Berkeley Nepali since 2004, the momo and the goat curry regulars order without looking at the menu. Lunch specials that feed you twice.

Mount Everest — 2598 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. The Telegraph mainstay for Nepali and Indian side by side, garlic naan and a thali that arrives in a dozen little bowls. Closed Wednesdays, plan around it.

The Gurkha Kitchen — 855 B St, Hayward. Downtown Hayward's Indo Nepali halal room, the chatamari and the sekuwa built by cooks who grew up on it. Bring the table, order wide. @thegurkhaskitchen

Namastey Patio — 5500 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge patio for momos and Nepali plates when the sun is out, Himalayan comfort a block from BART. The jhol momo in broth is the sleeper. @namasteypationepalese

Himalayan Bite — 4378 Thornton Ave, Fremont. The Fremont bite for momos and thukpa noodle soup, a warm bowl and a short menu done right. Worth the drive south for the real thing. @himalayanbitefremont

Seven for the momo run, Berkeley to Fremont: Cafe Tibet, Shangri-La, Taste of the Himalayas, Mount Everest, the Gurkha Kitchen, Namastey Patio, and Himalayan Bite. Which momo is your favorite?

item.title: East Bay Museums for Curious Kids
item.description: Children's Fairyland on Lake Merritt opened in 1950, and a young Walt Disney walked it for ideas before he built Disneyland. Six East Bay museums built for
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Museums for Curious Kids

Children's Fairyland on Lake Merritt opened in 1950, and a young Walt Disney walked it for ideas before he built Disneyland. Six East Bay museums built for curious kids.

Children's Fairyland — 699 Bellevue Ave, Oakland. The storybook park on Lake Merritt since 1950, ten acres of fairy tale sets, a tiny carousel, and puppet shows, no character too commercial. The original that inspired the big one down south. @fairylandca

Lawrence Hall of Science — 1 Centennial Dr, Berkeley. The hands on science museum up in the Berkeley hills, earthquakes and planetarium shows and a giant DNA to climb, the whole bay laid out below. Stay for sunset.

Chabot Space and Science Center — 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland. Three big telescopes in the Oakland hills, free public star viewing on clear Friday and Saturday nights, planetarium shows all day. Look through the twenty inch refractor and gasp.

Lindsay Wildlife Experience — 1931 First Ave, Walnut Creek. The first wildlife rehab hospital in the country, where kids meet a live bald eagle and a bobcat up close. Every animal here was rescued.

USS Hornet — 707 W Hornet Ave, Alameda. A World War Two aircraft carrier you walk end to end, the ship that recovered Apollo 11, jets on the deck and a story in every passageway. Bring the kid who loves machines.

Oakland Museum of California — 1000 Oak St, Oakland. Three floors of California art, history, and natural science with a garden in the middle, plus the Friday night street food party all summer. The hands on gallery keeps the little ones busy.

Six for curious kids: Fairyland, Lawrence Hall, Chabot Space, Lindsay Wildlife, the USS Hornet, and the Oakland Museum. Which one first?

item.title: East Bay Flea Markets and Antique Faires
item.description: On the first Sunday of every month, more than 800 antique dealers set up on the old Alameda naval runway, and the treasure hunters line up before dawn. Fiv
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Flea Markets and Antique Faires

On the first Sunday of every month, more than 800 antique dealers set up on the old Alameda naval runway, and the treasure hunters line up before dawn. Five East Bay flea markets worth getting up early for.

Alameda Point Antiques Faire — 2900 Navy Way, Alameda. The biggest antiques market in Northern California, 800 plus vendors on the runway the first Sunday of the month, everything at least twenty years old. Come at six for the deals, ten for the shade.

Laney College Flea Market — 900 Fallon St, Oakland. Every Sunday in the Laney lots, a sprawling swap meet of tools, produce, records, and finds, cash and a sharp eye. The people watching is half the trip.

Berkeley Flea Market — 1937 Ashby Ave, Berkeley. The community market in the Ashby BART lot on weekends, reopened in 2025, incense and vinyl and African textiles, drumming in the afternoon.

Ohlone College Flea Market — 43600 Mission Blvd, Fremont. The second Saturday of the month on the Fremont campus, ninety plus vendors, garage sellers next to small businesses, kids crafts on the side. March through November.

Urban Ore — 900 Murray St, Berkeley. Not a market but a two acre salvage yard open daily, doors and windows and oddities rescued from the landfill, the ultimate slow treasure hunt. Bring a truck and time.

Five for the hunt: Alameda Point, Laney College, Berkeley Flea, Ohlone College, and Urban Ore. What is the best thing you ever scored?

item.title: East Bay Petting Farms and Animal Spots for Kids
item.description: At the Little Farm in Tilden you can still walk up and feed the cows and goats by hand, for free, with celery and lettuce you bring from home. Five East Ba
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Petting Farms and Animal Spots for Kids

At the Little Farm in Tilden you can still walk up and feed the cows and goats by hand, for free, with celery and lettuce you bring from home. Five East Bay spots where kids meet the animals.

Little Farm — Tilden Nature Area, Canon Dr, Berkeley. A free farmyard in Tilden where kids feed the cows, goats, sheep, and chickens by hand, bring celery or lettuce, no admission ever. The classic first farm visit.

Ardenwood Historic Farm — 34600 Ardenwood Blvd, Fremont. A working turn of the century farm run since 1985, draft horses, a blacksmith, a train, and animals in every pen. Come on a program day and the place runs like 1900.

Sulphur Creek Nature Center — 1801 D St, Hayward. A free little wildlife center and rehab hospital, owls and snakes and creek critters up close, thematic animal programs for the 4 to 12 crowd. Small, calm, and free.

Oakland Zoo — 9777 Golf Links Rd, Oakland. The big one in the Oakland hills, a children's zoo petting area, a gondola over the grounds, and a California trail of native bears and condors. Plan a full day.

Forest Home Farms — San Ramon Valley Blvd, San Ramon. A historic working ranch run by the city, farm animals, antique tractors, and walnut orchards, open for tours and seasonal events. The quiet Tri-Valley pick.

Five where kids meet the animals: Little Farm, Ardenwood, Sulphur Creek, the Oakland Zoo, and Forest Home Farms. Where do your kids go?

item.title: East Bay German and Central European
item.description: There is a Bavarian beer garden on the Oakland estuary where you can pull up in your own boat, tie off, and drink a monastery lager at a communal table on
item.content:encoded:
East Bay German and Central European

There is a Bavarian beer garden on the Oakland estuary where you can pull up in your own boat, tie off, and drink a monastery lager at a communal table on the water. Five East Bay German tables for schnitzel, wurst, and a proper stein.

Brotzeit Lokal — 1000 Embarcadero, Oakland. A waterfront Bavarian biergarten in Brooklyn Basin, house made sausages, monastery brews, and guest boat berthing at the dock. Communal tables and an estuary sunset. @brotzeitlokal

Speisekammer — 2424 Lincoln Ave, Alameda. The island's German anchor since 2002, a Flensburg trained chef, sixteen taps, and schnitzel done right, with live music some nights. Order the jaegerschnitzel and a dunkel. @speisekammer

Anja's — 1966 University Ave, Berkeley. The daytime successor to Gaumenkitzel from its former chef, lighter organic German cooking, the mushroom ragout and bread the regulars still ask for. Breakfast and lunch. @anjaskitchenberkeley

Schmidt's Pub — 1492 Solano Ave, Albany. A cozy German pub on Solano, bratwurst, rouladen, and a wall of imports, the neighborhood spot for a low key Oktoberfest any month of the year.

Teske's Germania — 255 12th St, Oakland. A downtown Oakland institution for decades, dark wood, potato pancakes, and a back beer garden that fills when the sun is out. Old world, unbothered by trends.

Five for the stein: Brotzeit, Speisekammer, Anja's, Schmidt's, and Teske's Germania. Where do you raise the first glass?

item.title: East Bay French Bistros
item.description: La Note has served Provencal breakfasts in downtown Berkeley for decades, and the weekend line for the lemon gingerbread pancakes still runs down Shattuck.
item.content:encoded:
East Bay French Bistros

La Note has served Provencal breakfasts in downtown Berkeley for decades, and the weekend line for the lemon gingerbread pancakes still runs down Shattuck. Five East Bay French bistros for the long lunch.

La Note — 2477 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Rustic Provencal cooking in a sun filled room, the weekend brunch famous for lemon gingerbread pancakes and lavender honey. Go early or plan to wait.

Chevalier — 960 Moraga Rd, Lafayette. A polished French room from a Lyon trained chef, escargot, duck, and a serious wine list, the Lamorinda anniversary standby. Dress up a little.

Gregoire — 2109 Cedar St, Berkeley. A tiny North Berkeley takeout window of French comfort, the crispy potato puffs that sell out and a menu that changes monthly. Grab a box, walk to the park.

Metro Lafayette — 3524 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A neighborhood bistro and bar with a Parisian tilt, steak frites and a burger regulars swear by, a patio out front. Easy, consistent, unpretentious.

Reve Bistro — Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A warm French hideaway for coq au vin and a Burgundy list, the kind of room that turns a Tuesday into an occasion. Sit by the window.

Five for the long lunch: La Note, Chevalier, Gregoire, Metro Lafayette, and Reve. Where is your French fix?

item.title: East Bay Yarn and Fabric Shops
item.description: There is a shop on San Pablo Avenue that grows its own dye garden out back and spins naturally dyed yarn from the plants it raises. Seven East Bay shops fo
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Yarn and Fabric Shops

There is a shop on San Pablo Avenue that grows its own dye garden out back and spins naturally dyed yarn from the plants it raises. Seven East Bay shops for knitters, sewists, and makers.

A Verb for Keeping Warm — 6328 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. A yarn and fabric shop with an indoor and outdoor natural dye studio and its own dye garden, plus classes in knitting, weaving, and sewing. The maker's clubhouse since 2011.

Stonemountain and Daughter Fabrics — 2518 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Three floors of garment fabric and notions with a clearance attic upstairs, the Berkeley institution sewists plan a whole afternoon around. Bring your pattern.

Avenue Yarns — Solano Ave, Albany. A bright, welcoming yarn shop on Solano with tightly curated skeins, sample knits, and a full class calendar. Small, warm, and expert.

Needle in a Haystack — 2433 Mariner Square Loop, Alameda. A gem of a needlework shop, fine needlepoint canvases, threads, and expert help for the cross stitch and embroidery crowd.

The ReCrafting Co — 2449 Santa Clara Ave, Alameda. The other half of that Alameda tip, recycled and consigned craft supplies far below retail, the sustainable way to restock the stash.

Lacis — 2982 Adeline St, Berkeley. Part lace and textile museum, part shop, a wonderland of tools for lacemaking, embroidery, and costume, with the collection in the back. Nowhere else like it.

Discount Fabrics — 3006 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A cavern of bolts at working prices, apparel to upholstery to oddball remnants, the pragmatic stop when the project is big and the budget is real.

Seven for the makers: A Verb, Stonemountain, Avenue Yarns, Needle in a Haystack, ReCrafting Co, Lacis, and Discount Fabrics. What are you making right now?

item.title: East Bay Ice and Roller Rinks
item.description: Paradise Skate in Antioch still runs a classic maple roller floor under disco lights, the kind of rink most towns tore out decades ago. Five Bay Area rinks
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Ice and Roller Rinks

Paradise Skate in Antioch still runs a classic maple roller floor under disco lights, the kind of rink most towns tore out decades ago. Five Bay Area rinks to lace up, ice and wheels.

Paradise Skate — 1201 W 10th St, Antioch. A classic wood floor roller rink with disco lights, cheap rentals, and all ages sessions, birthday central for east county. Old school and proud.

Yerba Buena Ice Skating — 750 Folsom St, SF. A downtown rink and bowling alley under Yerba Buena Gardens, public skate daily and a warm lobby, the city's cool escape. Skate then bowl.

Oakland Ice Center — 519 18th St, Oakland. Twin NHL sized sheets downtown, public skate daily, hockey and figure lessons, and a warm lobby to thaw out. The city rink hiding in plain sight.

Dublin Iceland — 7212 San Ramon Rd, Dublin. A community ice rink since 1970, public sessions and learn to skate, the coldest escape in the valley on a hundred degree day.

Sharks Ice at Fremont — 44388 Old Warm Springs Blvd, Fremont. A big multi sheet ice complex open seven days for public skate and drop in hockey, the south county rink where the leagues run late.

Five to lace up: Paradise Skate, Yerba Buena, Oakland Ice Center, Dublin Iceland, and Sharks Ice. Wheels or blades?

item.title: East Bay Arcades and Pinball
item.description: The Pacific Pinball Museum in Alameda lets you play more than 100 machines from the 1940s to today on a single all day pass, no quarters needed. Five East
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Arcades and Pinball

The Pacific Pinball Museum in Alameda lets you play more than 100 machines from the 1940s to today on a single all day pass, no quarters needed. Five East Bay arcades for the game night that beats a bar.

Pacific Pinball Museum — 1510 Webster St, Alameda. A nonprofit hall of over 100 playable pinball machines from the 1940s on, one flat admission and unlimited free play, murals and history on the walls. The rainy day and the birthday party both.

High Scores Arcade — 1414 Park St, Alameda. Forty five cabinets and more than 400 classic 80s games on Park Street, all on free play once you are in, the Donkey Kong and Galaga crowd's clubhouse. Bring your initials.

Emporium Arcade Bar — 1805 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A massive barcade in a restored old theater, rows of arcade and pinball plus pool, air hockey, and a full bar. The grown up game night headquarters in Uptown.

Tipsy Putt — 5690 Bay St, Emeryville. An indoor mini golf bar and barcade with craft beer, table golf, and a hidden speakeasy, the group hang with something for everyone. Come for the barcade.

Round1 Bowling and Arcade — 185 Sunvalley Mall, Concord. A huge indoor arcade and bowling floor with crane games, karaoke, and ticket redemption, the rainy afternoon kid magnet out in Concord. Load the card and go.

Five for game night: Pacific Pinball, High Scores, Emporium, Tipsy Putt, and Round1. High score or gutter ball?

item.title: East Bay Music and Instrument Shops
item.description: There is a shop on a Berkeley side street that bought up the liquidated factory stock of Gibson, Vox, and Ampeg and has sold guitars out of a psychedelic b
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Music and Instrument Shops

There is a shop on a Berkeley side street that bought up the liquidated factory stock of Gibson, Vox, and Ampeg and has sold guitars out of a psychedelic bungalow since 1968. Six East Bay shops for players and beginners alike.

Subway Guitars — 1800 Cedar St, Berkeley. A wonderland bungalow of over three thousand new and used guitars, basses, and amps, factory overstock and oddities since 1968, with lessons in the back. Ask Fatdog what to play.

Starving Musician — 2474 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The friendly indie alternative to the big box since 1985, buying, selling, trading, and renting guitars, amps, pedals, and drums. Fair prices and no attitude.

Mountain Music Store — 4444 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. A small Piedmont Avenue shop strong on vintage and new gear with in house string repairs, plus amps, synths, and turntables sent out for fixing. The neighborhood repair bench.

Oakland Guitars — 423 40th St, Oakland. The Temescal guitar shop with Green Day roots, formerly Broken Guitars, now doing sales and Dead Note repairs on the corner of 40th and Webster. Punk pedigree, real workbench.

Berkeley Musical Instrument Exchange — 2923 Adeline St, Berkeley. A South Berkeley institution since 1974, everything from full drum kits and bongos to violins and trumpets, used and consigned. The orchestra and the garage band both shop here.

Mighty Fine Guitars — 85 Lafayette Cir, Lafayette. A Lamorinda shop of collectible and boutique guitars with a listening room feel, the place to try the nice ones without a rush. Worth the drive for the browse.

Six for the players: Subway Guitars, Starving Musician, Mountain Music, Oakland Guitars, the Instrument Exchange, and Mighty Fine. What was your first instrument?

item.title: East Bay Vegan and Vegetarian
item.description: Oakland's Souley Vegan turned Southern soul food fully plant based and became a nationally known Black owned vegan kitchen. Eight East Bay vegan and vegeta
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Vegan and Vegetarian

Oakland's Souley Vegan turned Southern soul food fully plant based and became a nationally known Black owned vegan kitchen. Eight East Bay vegan and vegetarian spots.

Souley Vegan — 301 Broadway, Oakland. Southern soul food gone fully vegan, smothered plant based cutlets, mac, and cornbread in Jack London. Order the combo plate.

Vegan Mob — Oakland. The viral plant based barbecue and soul spot for smoked mushroom brisket, gumbo, and mobburritos. Get the smoked mob plate.

The Butcher's Son — 1954 University Ave, Berkeley. A fully vegan deli of turkey style clubs and mozzarella stuffed meatball subs. The sandwich fix.

Golden Lotus — 1301 Franklin St, Oakland. Longtime vegan Vietnamese for lemongrass soy chicken and pho with plant based beef. The comfort bowl.

Layonna Vegetarian — 419 9th St, Oakland. A Chinatown vegan Chinese kitchen and grocery, mock meats and clay pots. Stock the freezer too.

Udupi Palace — 1901 University Ave, Berkeley. A South Indian vegetarian institution for crackling dosas and idli. Get the masala dosa.

Vik's Chaat — 2390 4th St, Berkeley. A bustling mostly vegetarian Indian chaat house, chole bhatura and dosas in a warehouse. Come hungry at lunch.

Shangri-La Vegan — Oakland. A vegan Himalayan spot for momos and curries, warm and inexpensive. The dumpling stop.

Eight plant based: Souley Vegan, Vegan Mob, the Butcher's Son, Golden Lotus, Layonna, Udupi Palace, Vik's Chaat, and Shangri-La. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay A Day in Emeryville
item.description: Emeryville packed a global food hall, a punk rock diner, and a bayfront dim sum palace into a single square mile between Oakland and Berkeley. Eight Emeryv
item.content:encoded:
East Bay A Day in Emeryville

Emeryville packed a global food hall, a punk rock diner, and a bayfront dim sum palace into a single square mile between Oakland and Berkeley. Eight Emeryville stops.

Public Market Emeryville — 5959 Shellmound St, Emeryville. A global food hall of ramen, burgers, and cashew ice cream. Graze a few stalls.

Rudy's Can't Fail Cafe — 4081 Hollis St, Emeryville. A punk diner co founded by a Green Day member, breakfast all day. Get the breakfast plate.

Hong Kong East Ocean — 3199 Powell St, Emeryville. A waterfront banquet hall with cart dim sum and bay views. Come for weekend dim sum.

Bay Street Emeryville — 5616 Bay St, Emeryville. An open air shopping and dining center with a cinema. Pair a movie with dinner.

Prizefighter — 6702 Hollis St, Emeryville. A craft cocktail bar with a garden patio. Grab a patio seat.

Honor Kitchen and Cocktails — 1411 Powell St, Emeryville. A chef driven Emeryville kitchen and cocktail bar with bold plates and a warm, buzzy room. Settle in for a drink.

Doyle Street Cafe — 5515 Doyle St, Emeryville. A long running neighborhood brunch spot. Do weekend brunch.

Emeryville Marina — 3310 Powell St, Emeryville. A marina with a bay trail and a full skyline view. Walk the shoreline at sunset.

Eight in Emeryville: Public Market, Rudy's Can't Fail Cafe, Hong Kong East Ocean, Bay Street, Prizefighter, Honor Kitchen, Doyle Street Cafe, and the Marina. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay Fremont's Niles District
item.description: Fremont's Niles district is where Charlie Chaplin filmed silent movies in the 1910s, now an antique row of steam trains, a silent film museum, and a cowboy
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Fremont's Niles District

Fremont's Niles district is where Charlie Chaplin filmed silent movies in the 1910s, now an antique row of steam trains, a silent film museum, and a cowboy pizza palace. Eight Niles stops.

Bronco Billy's Pizza Palace — 37651 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A cowboy movie themed pizzeria on the antique strip. Split a pie under the posters.

Niles Canyon Railway — Niles Blvd, Fremont. A heritage steam railroad that runs through the canyon on weekends. Ride a weekend train.

Niles Essanay Silent Film Museum — 37417 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A museum in the old studio town where Chaplin filmed. Catch a silent film night.

Niles Boulevard antique shops — Niles Blvd, Fremont. A strip of antique stores and craft shops. Browse for an afternoon.

Devout Coffee — 37485 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A local coffeehouse with live music nights. Grab a coffee.

Joe's Corner — 37812 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A friendly neighborhood dive on the strip. Have a cold one.

Niles Town Plaza — 37592 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A little plaza that hosts the famous flea market. Time it to the flea market.

California Nursery Historical Park — 36501 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A historic nursery turned park with old groves. Wander the grounds.

Eight in Niles: Bronco Billy's, the Niles Canyon Railway, the Essanay Silent Film Museum, the antique shops, Devout Coffee, Joe's Corner, Niles Town Plaza, and the California Nursery park. Where do you start?

item.description: Montclair Village is Oakland's hidden hill town, a walkable pocket of a 1974 egg shop, a cheese and wine shop, and a Sunday market tucked in the redwood fo
item.content:encoded:
Oakland's Montclair Village

Montclair Village is Oakland's hidden hill town, a walkable pocket of a 1974 egg shop, a cheese and wine shop, and a Sunday market tucked in the redwood foothills. Eight Montclair Village stops.

Crogan's Montclair — 6101 La Salle Ave, Oakland. A clubby American bar and grill, the village's living room. Get the pot roast.

Montclair Egg Shop — 6126 Medau Pl, Oakland. A brunch institution since 1974 with rotating benedicts. Come for the eggs.

Farmstead Cheeses and Wines — 6218 La Salle Ave, Oakland. A cheese and wine shop built for a hillside picnic. Build a board.

Bica Coffeehouse — 2027 Mountain Blvd, Oakland. A neighborhood coffeehouse in the heart of the village. Grab a cortado.

Montclair Village Farmers Market — La Salle Ave, Oakland. A Sunday market in the center of the village. Go Sunday morning.

Montclair Park — 6300 Moraga Ave, Oakland. A shaded neighborhood park with a creek and courts. Bring the kids.

Montclair branch, Oakland Public Library — 1687 Mountain Blvd, Oakland. A cozy hill library and community hub. Browse a while.

Montclair Railroad Trail — Mountain Blvd, Oakland. A short trail on an old rail bed into the canyon. Walk it after lunch.

Eight in Montclair Village: Crogan's, the Egg Shop, Farmstead Cheeses and Wines, Bica Coffeehouse, the farmers market, Montclair Park, the library, and the Railroad Trail. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
Oakland's Dimond District

The Dimond District grew up around an 1870s German beer garden and still hides a redwood creek canyon right behind its MacArthur Boulevard storefronts. Eight Dimond stops.

Dimond Slice Pizza — 2208 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A vegetarian slice shop and neighborhood hang. Grab a slice and a salad.

La Farine Fruitvale — 3411 Fruitvale Ave, Oakland. A French bakery institution for morning buns and baguettes. Get a morning bun.

Two Star Market — 2020 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A corner market secretly serving some of the city's best late night soul food. Order a soul food plate.

Grand Lake Kitchen Dimond — MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A cheery all day cafe and deli with a full bar. Do weekend brunch.

Farmer Joe's Marketplace — 3501 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A beloved independent grocery with a great deli. Build a picnic.

Dimond Park — 3860 Hanly Rd, Oakland. A shaded park with a creek, a pool, and a stone rec building. Bring the kids.

Dimond Branch Library — 3565 Fruitvale Ave, Oakland. A historic hillside library and community hub. Browse a while.

Dimond Canyon Trail — Dimond Park, Oakland. A redwood creek canyon trail hidden right behind the storefronts. Walk up Sausal Creek.

Eight in the Dimond: Dimond Slice, La Farine, Two Star Market, Grand Lake Kitchen, Farmer Joe's, Dimond Park, the library, and the Dimond Canyon Trail. Where do you start?

item.description: The Laurel is among Oakland's most diverse strips, a stretch of MacArthur Boulevard where a 1986 Cambodian institution, a cheesecake patisserie, and a hous
item.content:encoded:
Oakland's Laurel District

The Laurel is among Oakland's most diverse strips, a stretch of MacArthur Boulevard where a 1986 Cambodian institution, a cheesecake patisserie, and a house made sausage diner sit side by side. Eight Laurel District stops.

Sequoia Diner — 3719 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. An all day diner with house made sausage, bread, and jam. Get the biscuits.

World Ground Cafe — 3726 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A warm corner coffeehouse with wine and light bites. Camp out with a latte.

Phnom Penh House — 3912 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A family Cambodian restaurant serving the Laurel since 1986. Order the amok.

Crumble and Whisk Patisserie — 4104 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A cheesecake bakery some call the Bay Area's best. Get a slice to go.

Cafe of the Bay — 4011 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A neighborhood breakfast and lunch spot. Come for the omelets.

Communite Table — 4171 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A Southern comfort brunch with chicken and waffles. Order the chicken and waffles.

Laurel Book Store — 3807 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A community bookstore and gathering spot. Grab a local read.

MacArthur Boulevard murals — MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A stretch of storefronts painted with neighborhood murals. Walk the mural block.

Eight in the Laurel: Sequoia Diner, World Ground Cafe, Phnom Penh House, Crumble and Whisk, Cafe of the Bay, Communite Table, Laurel Book Store, and the murals. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay A Day in Old Town Pittsburg

Pittsburg's Old Town sits right on the delta, an Italian fishing town turned Railroad Avenue strip of red sauce joints, a 1920 theater, and a marina where the water taxi still runs. Eight Old Town Pittsburg stops.

La Veranda Ristorante — Railroad Ave, Pittsburg. A downtown Italian room carrying the town's fishing village roots. Get the linguine and clams.

Wahsing — 2222 Railroad Ave, Pittsburg. A longtime Chinese American spot on the strip. Order the chow mein.

Johnny's Market — 625 Railroad Ave, Pittsburg. An old school deli and market for a big sandwich. Grab a sub.

Blue Saigon — Railroad Ave, Pittsburg. A neighborhood Vietnamese spot for pho and rice plates. Get a bowl of pho.

Touch of Soul — Railroad Ave, Pittsburg. A soul food kitchen for ribs and cornbread. Order the ribs.

Waterfront Grill and Cafe — 51 Marina Blvd, Pittsburg. A casual spot right on the marina water. Sit out by the boats.

California Theatre — 351 Railroad Ave, Pittsburg. A restored 1920 downtown theater and stage. Catch a show.

Pittsburg Marina — Marina Blvd, Pittsburg. A delta marina with a boardwalk and a summer water taxi. Walk the waterfront.

Eight in Old Town Pittsburg: La Veranda, Wahsing, Johnny's Market, Blue Saigon, Touch of Soul, the Waterfront Grill, the California Theatre, and the marina. Where do you start?

item.description: The East Bay hears live music in a lavish 1928 movie palace, a Jack London jazz club, and a Berkeley folk institution that has run since 1968. Eight East B
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Live Music Venues

The East Bay hears live music in a lavish 1928 movie palace, a Jack London jazz club, and a Berkeley folk institution that has run since 1968. Eight East Bay music venues.

Fox Theater — 1807 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A restored 1928 movie palace turned marquee concert hall. Get the balcony for the view.

Paramount Theatre — 2025 Broadway, Oakland. A stunning art deco theater for concerts and classic films. Take the deco tour.

Yoshi's — 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland. A Jack London jazz club and sushi room, world class acts nightly. Book a table up front.

The New Parish — 1743 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. An intimate club with a balcony for hip hop, soul, and reggae. Stand near the stage.

Freight and Salvage — 2020 Addison St, Berkeley. A nonprofit folk and Americana coffeehouse since 1968. Catch a bluegrass night.

The UC Theatre — 2036 University Ave, Berkeley. A 1917 theater reborn as an all ages music hall. Grab the front rail.

Ashkenaz — 1317 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A world music and dance hall where the crowd is the show. Take a dance lesson first.

The Ivy Room — 860 San Pablo Ave, Albany. A tiny dive with a stage and a loyal local scene. Catch a garage rock set.

Eight for live music: the Fox, the Paramount, Yoshi's, the New Parish, Freight and Salvage, the UC Theatre, Ashkenaz, and the Ivy Room. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay A Day in Hayward
item.description: The East Bay sleeps on Hayward, but B Street hides America's first brewpub, a world famous dive, and the oldest Japanese garden in California. Eight Haywar
item.content:encoded:
East Bay A Day in Hayward

The East Bay sleeps on Hayward, but B Street hides America's first brewpub, a world famous dive, and the oldest Japanese garden in California. Eight Hayward stops.

Buffalo Bill's Brewery — 1082 B St, Hayward. The first brewpub in America, pouring on B Street since 1983. Order a pint and the pizza.

Turf Club — 22519 Main St, Hayward. A world famous neighborhood bar readers call a can't miss. Post up at the bar. A @gregtrevizo add.

Kansai — 954 B St, Hayward. A downtown sushi spot named alongside the Turf Club as a must. Sit at the sushi bar. A @gregtrevizo add.

Stein Lounge — 939 B St, Hayward. A locals only bar with a killer jukebox and B horror movies on the screen. Feed the jukebox. A @gregtrevizo add.

Chai Thai Noodles — 20955 Mission Blvd, Hayward. A Thai kitchen readers put up with the East Bay's best. Get the boat noodles. A @rajhasacamera add.

Round1 — 551 Southland Mall Dr, Hayward. Bowling, arcade, and karaoke, the entrance is outside the mall not in. Roll a game. A @klauztrophobik add.

Hayward Japanese Gardens — 22373 N 3rd St, Hayward. The oldest traditional Japanese garden in California, free and quiet. Walk the koi pond loop.

Century at Hayward — 1069 B Street Cinema Pl, Hayward. The downtown movie house anchoring the B Street strip. Catch an evening show.

Eight in Hayward: Buffalo Bill's, the Turf Club, Kansai, the Stein Lounge, Chai Thai, Round1, the Japanese Gardens, and Century. Where do you start?

item.description: Berkeley readers are relentless in the comments, so here are the East Bay spots they refuse to let us leave off. Eight Berkeley and El Cerrito picks.
item.content:encoded:
Berkeley and El Cerrito Picks You Sent

Berkeley readers are relentless in the comments, so here are the East Bay spots they refuse to let us leave off. Eight Berkeley and El Cerrito picks.

Angeline's Louisiana Kitchen — 2261 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A downtown Cajun and Creole room readers named with real force. Get the gumbo and cornbread. A @eb_bob add.

Agrodolce Osteria — 1730 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A Sicilian osteria near the Gourmet Ghetto readers keep going back to. Order the handmade pasta. A @poppers_the_pony add.

Gordo Taqueria — 2989 College Ave, Berkeley. The Elmwood outpost of the burrito name people say to respect. Get a super burrito. A @sridhartheyaafa add.

Urban Ore — 900 Murray St, Berkeley. A giant salvage and reuse yard you can lose an afternoon in. Hunt for a door or a lamp. A @blogappetit add.

Photolab — 2235 5th St, Berkeley. A film and photo lab readers trust as much as Looking Glass. Drop off a roll. A @eb_bob add.

Sports Basement — 2727 Milvia St, Berkeley. Outdoor gear inside the historic old Berkeley Iceland rink building. Gear up for a trip. A @teepeeok add.

Dave's Record Shop — 1404 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A used vinyl shop on San Pablo readers added to the crate digging list. Flip through the dollar bins. A @misskimba add.

Fat Apple's — 7525 Fairmount Ave, El Cerrito. The sit down El Cerrito location for pie and breakfast, roomier than Berkeley. Get a slice of pie. A @risanye add.

item.title: East Bay Small Music Rooms
item.description: The East Bay's best live music is not in the big halls, it is in the tiny rooms readers keep flagging, a DownBeat top jazz room and a punk shrine that laun
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Small Music Rooms

The East Bay's best live music is not in the big halls, it is in the tiny rooms readers keep flagging, a DownBeat top jazz room and a punk shrine that launched Green Day. Eight East Bay music rooms.

The Sound Room — 3022 Broadway, Oakland. A listening room DownBeat named one of the best jazz spots in the world four years running. Sit close for the set. A @balldudejimmy add.

The Back Room — 1984 Bonita Ave, Berkeley. An intimate downtown Berkeley listening room with warm acoustics. Catch an Americana night. A @balldudejimmy add.

Cornerstone — 2367 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A craft beer hall and stage with 40 taps and a nightly lineup. Grab a beer near the stage.

Thee Stork Club — 2330 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A scrappy Telegraph dive with a back room stage. Stand up front for a garage set.

The Starry Plough — 3101 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. An Irish pub with live music and a long running poetry slam. Stay for the session.

924 Gilman — 924 Gilman St, Berkeley. The volunteer run all ages DIY hall that launched Green Day and Rancid. Catch an all ages show.

Cafe Van Kleef — Uptown, Oakland. A cluttered Uptown bar famous for its greyhounds and weekend bands. Order a greyhound and stay for the band.

Make Westing — 1741 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. An Uptown cocktail bar with indoor bocce for before or after the show. Grab a drink and roll bocce.

Eight for live music: the Sound Room, the Back Room, Cornerstone, Thee Stork Club, the Starry Plough, 924 Gilman, Cafe Van Kleef, and Make Westing. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay A Day in Castro Valley
item.description: Castro Valley is the East Bay town everyone drives through on the way to somewhere else, but the boulevard hides a 70 year deli and a food hall in an old d
item.content:encoded:
East Bay A Day in Castro Valley

Castro Valley is the East Bay town everyone drives through on the way to somewhere else, but the boulevard hides a 70 year deli and a food hall in an old department store. Eight Castro Valley stops.

Denica's Real Food Kitchen — 2723 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. A first come first serve breakfast spot feeding the valley since 1999. Get there early for the pancakes.

Lucca's Italian Delicatessen — 3121 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. A 70 year old Italian deli stacking top notch sandwiches. Build a sub to go. A @bdgrcrck add.

Norman's Grill — 3638 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. A longtime diner slinging pancakes and burgers. Take a counter stool.

Cordial Cellar and Lounge — 3295 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. A subterranean wine lounge under the marketplace with curated pours. Order a flight. A @deidre.heitman add.

Castro Valley Marketplace — 3295 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. A three story food hall in a former department store. Graze the vendors.

The Chabot Theater — 2853 Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. Among the last independent movie houses in the Bay Area. Catch a night showing.

Castro Village Bowl — 3501 Village Dr, Castro Valley. A classic neighborhood bowling alley off the boulevard. Roll a few frames. A @crafty13mum add.

Castro Valley Farmers Market — Castro Valley Blvd, Castro Valley. A Saturday market near the boulevard with produce and tamales. Shop then snack.

Eight in Castro Valley: Denica's, Lucca's, Norman's Grill, Cordial, the Marketplace, the Chabot, Castro Village Bowl, and the farmers market. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:

Concord's downtown wraps around Todos Santos Plaza, an East Bay square with Thursday concerts and a ring of Burmese, Mexican, and Italian kitchens. Eight downtown Concord stops.

Aung Burma — 2151 Salvio St, Concord. A downtown Burmese spot famous for tea leaf salad. Order the tea leaf salad.

Cocina Hijole Maria — 1819 Colfax St, Concord. A family Mexican kitchen a block off the plaza. Get the birria.

Luna Ristorante — 2118 Willow Pass Rd, Concord. A downtown Italian room with homemade pasta. Twirl the tagliatelle.

The Old Spaghetti Factory — 1955 Mount Diablo St, Concord. A family Italian favorite in a grand old building. Bring the kids.

Uncle Jay Burger House — 1990 Grant St, Concord. A downtown burger joint stacking messy classics. Get a chili burger.

Vinnie's Bar and Grill — 2045 Mount Diablo St, Concord. A block off the plaza dive with pub grub and live nights. Grab a beer.

Hop Grenade — Concord. A downtown taproom and bottle shop with a garden patio. Try a local pour.

Todos Santos Plaza — 2151 Salvio St, Concord. The downtown square with Thursday summer concerts and a market. Catch a show on the lawn.

Eight in downtown Concord: Aung Burma, Cocina Hijole Maria, Luna, the Old Spaghetti Factory, Uncle Jay, Vinnie's, Hop Grenade, and Todos Santos Plaza. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Antioch's Rivertown

Antioch's Rivertown is the East Bay's forgotten delta downtown, a grid of 1800s blocks running down to a marina on the San Joaquin River. Eight Rivertown stops.

Smith's Landing Seafood Grill — 1 Marina Plaza, Antioch. A waterfront seafood room in the old Humphrey's spot on the river. Book a window at sunset.

Monica's Riverview — 1 I St, Antioch. A riverside brunch and steak spot right on the water. Come for the weekend brunch.

Rivertown historic district — West 2nd St, Antioch. A walkable grid of 1800s storefronts and murals. Stroll the old blocks.

El Campanil Theatre — 602 West 2nd St, Antioch. A restored 1928 downtown theater and stage. Catch a show.

Lynn House Gallery — 809 West 1st St, Antioch. A community art gallery across from the train station. See a local exhibit.

Antioch Historical Society Museum — 1500 West 4th St, Antioch. A local history museum in a grand old building. Dig into delta history.

Waldie Plaza — West 2nd St, Antioch. A riverfront plaza for picnics and summer concerts. Watch the river go by.

Antioch Marina — 5 Marina Plaza, Antioch. A delta marina and boat launch at the foot of L Street. Walk the docks.

Eight in Rivertown: Smith's Landing, Monica's Riverview, the historic blocks, El Campanil, Lynn House Gallery, the history museum, Waldie Plaza, and the marina. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay A Day At San Ramon City Center

San Ramon's downtown is City Center Bishop Ranch, a Renzo Piano designed open air square in the East Bay packed with restaurants, a movie house, and a rooftop. Eight San Ramon stops.

Fieldwork Brewing — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. The brewery's busiest patio pouring Neapolitan pizza and fresh beer. Grab a pint on the patio.

The Slanted Door — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. The modern Vietnamese icon's East Bay outpost. Order the shaking beef.

The Lot — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. The center's ten screen luxury cinema with a full restaurant and bar, dinner and a movie in recliners. Catch a film with dinner.

Bamboo Sushi — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. A sustainable sushi bar in the center. Sit at the sushi counter.

Marugame Udon — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. Fresh udon pulled to order. Watch them cut the noodles.

Delarosa — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. A Roman style pizza and aperitivo spot. Share a pizza and a spritz.

Mendocino Farms — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. A California sandwich and salad shop. Grab a lunch sandwich.

City Center rooftop — 6000 Bollinger Canyon Rd, San Ramon. The open air square with a rooftop deck and an events lawn. Catch a weekend event.

Eight at City Center: Fieldwork, the Slanted Door, the Lot, Bamboo Sushi, Marugame Udon, Delarosa, Mendocino Farms, and the rooftop. Where do you start?

Danville's downtown runs along Hartz Avenue, an East Bay small town main street of white tablecloth rooms, a 1913 theater, and a rail depot museum. Eight downtown Danville stops.

Bridges Restaurant and Bar — 44 Church St, Danville. The white tablecloth room made famous by a scene in Mrs Doubtfire. Book the patio.

Esin Restaurant and Bar — 750 Camino Ramon, Danville. A farm to table favorite serving since 1998. Save room for the dessert.

Piatti — Hartz Ave, Danville. A bustling Italian trattoria with outdoor seating. Sit outside for the pasta.

The Peasant and the Pear — Hartz Ave, Danville. A cozy American bistro downtown. Try the pear salad.

Sideboard — Hartz Ave, Danville. A popular breakfast and brunch cafe. Get there early for pancakes.

Museum of the San Ramon Valley — 205 Railroad Ave, Danville. Local history in the restored 1891 Southern Pacific depot. Tour the old depot.

Village Theatre and Art Gallery — 233 Front St, Danville. A 1913 theater and gallery downtown. Catch a show or an exhibit.

Iron Horse Trail — Danville. The rail trail running through downtown for a walk or a bike. Stroll the old rail line.

Eight in Danville: Bridges, Esin, Piatti, the Peasant and the Pear, Sideboard, the museum, the Village Theatre, and the Iron Horse Trail. Where do you start?

Union City is the East Bay's under the radar food town, where a Filipino kitchen, a dumpling house, and a Cajun spot hide between the freeways. Eight Union City stops.

item.title: East Bay Downtown Livermore
item.description: Eight walkable downtown Livermore stops most of the Bay Area blows past on the way to the wineries. First Street runs the whole East Bay wine-country main
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Livermore

Eight walkable downtown Livermore stops most of the Bay Area blows past on the way to the wineries. First Street runs the whole East Bay wine-country main drag end to end, tasting room to taproom to a Michelin-listed kitchen, no car between them. Here's the walk.

Vine Cinema & Alehouse — 1722 First Street, Livermore. A single-screen movie house with table seating where you carry a beer to your seat, the anchor holding down the quiet end of First. Catch a matinee before the crowd wanders up the street. @vine_cinema

First Street Alehouse — 2106 First Street, Livermore. Twenty-six years downtown and still the room locals default to, with one of the biggest beer-can collections you'll ever eat a burger under. Grab the prime rib sandwich and whatever's rotating on tap. @firststreetalehouse

First Street Wine Company — 2211 First Street, Livermore. A family-run tasting bar that quietly got voted best in the East Bay, pouring Livermore Valley by the flight so you skip the drive out to the vineyards. Taste three, take home the one that surprised you. @1ststreetwineco

Sansar Indian Cuisine — 2220 First Street, Livermore. Tandoor-fired plates and a midday buffet right on the main walk, with an open-sky patio for when downtown warms up. Order the tandoori and something off the biryani list. @sansarindianrestaurant

Hops & Sessions — 2339 First Street, Livermore. A self-pour taphouse where you wristband in and work a rotating wall of local brewers a few ounces at a time. The move when your group can't agree on one beer. @hopsandsessions

Wingen Bakery & Restaurant — 50 South Livermore Avenue, Livermore. Naturally leavened sourdough and morning pastries that began as a home cottage bake, now a downtown corner that turns into sourdough pizza and lo-fi cocktails by night. Come early for the croissants. @wingenbakery

Uncle Yu's at the Vineyard — 39 South Livermore Avenue, Livermore. An established local institution since 2006, Asian cooking paired to a wine list that runs about 600 bottles deep, with corkage waived on Livermore wine every Monday. Bring a local bottle and make it a Monday.

Range Life — 2160 Railroad Avenue, Livermore. Californian cooking in an 1800s brick building from a chef who ran the Tartine and Bar Tartine line, the downtown table that landed Livermore in the Michelin guide. Book ahead and let the seasonal menu drive. @rangelife_livermore

Eight for a downtown Livermore walk: Vine, the Alehouse, First Street Wine, Sansar, Hops and Sessions, Wingen, Uncle Yu's, Range Life. First Street to Railroad, no freeway required. Which end do you start from?

item.title: East Bay Alameda, Park Street and Webster
item.description: Eight walkable Alameda stops most East Bay people miss, crossing the island for the beach and leaving before the good part. Park Street and Webster Street
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Alameda, Park Street and Webster

Eight walkable Alameda stops most East Bay people miss, crossing the island for the beach and leaving before the good part. Park Street and Webster Street run it end to end: a 1932 movie palace, an ice cream counter since 1941, a coffee roaster, a German beer garden. All on foot.

Julie's Coffee & Tea Garden — 1223 Park Street, Alameda. Organic coffee, loose-leaf tea, and a hidden back garden the regulars treat as their living room. Open every day 7 to 4, and if a local orders the lavender lemonade, follow their lead. @juliesteagarden

Highwire Coffee Roasters — 1234 Park Street, Alameda. The East Bay roaster that supplies half the good cafes keeps its own corner shop right on Park. Order the Core espresso, grab a bag to take home, and skip the chain two doors down. @highwirecoffee

Lucky 13 — 1301 Park Street, Alameda. On the corner of Park and Encinal, 20-plus drafts, no Bud or Coors, and a back beer garden built for a slow afternoon. There's a photo booth and a jukebox, so bring quarters and low standards for your song picks.

Tucker's Ice Cream — 1349 Park Street, Alameda. Scooping super-creamed ice cream on Park Street since 1941, an island institution your grandparents would recognize. Get the salted butter caramel in a fresh waffle cone and eat it on the patio out back.

Alameda Theatre — 2317 Central Ave, Alameda. The 1932 art deco movie palace whose neon blade sign anchors the bottom of Park Street, dark for decades and lit again since 2008. Catch a first-run film in the grand old room instead of a beige suburban multiplex.

Feel Good Bakery — 1650 Park Street, Alameda. Tucked inside the Alameda Marketplace, turning out European-style breads and macarons with organic, locally milled flour. Come early for the morning loaves; the best ones are gone by lunch.

Speisekammer — 2424 Lincoln Ave, Alameda. A German restaurant and biergarten a block off Park, established 2002, schnitzel and spatzle under new owners who kept the 16 taps. Live music some nights and a courtyard made for a long table. @speisekammer

Wescafe — 1518 Webster Street, Alameda. Cross to the Webster side for the family diner the locals lean on, pulling produce from the Tuesday and Saturday farmers market out front. Sit on the fountain patio and order breakfast past noon. @wescafe

Eight for one walkable island day: Julie's, Highwire, Lucky 13, Tucker's, the Theatre, Feel Good, Speisekammer, Wescafe. Which corner do you start on, Park or Webster?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: Oakland Temescal
item.description: Eight stops that prove Oakland's Temescal is the most walkable food corridor in the East Bay. Most people treat Telegraph Avenue as the road to somewhere e
item.content:encoded:
Oakland Temescal

Eight stops that prove Oakland's Temescal is the most walkable food corridor in the East Bay. Most people treat Telegraph Avenue as the road to somewhere else and miss that a brewery, a Burmese institution from 1992, and a whole hidden alley of shops sit in a few blocks. Here's the walk.

Temescal Brewing — 4115 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The taproom and beer garden anchor the south end of the corridor, open every day with a rotating cast of food trucks out front, so dinner changes with your mood. Their motto is Fresh Beer, No Jerks. That tells you the room. Come for the patio on a warm evening.

Burma Superstar — 4721 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The Temescal flagship of a Burmese kitchen that's fed the Bay since 1992, and the tea leaf salad tossed at your table is still the order everyone leans across for. The room reopened polished in 2026. Get the platha and thank yourself later.

Forma Bakery — 4920 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A tiny corner storefront turning out a serious croissant and a proper cup of coffee, the kind of morning stop that makes a walkable block feel like a gift. Pastries move fast, so the early walk wins the good stuff. @forma_bakery

Pizzaiolo — 5008 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Wood-fired pizza and pasta from an all-organic, all-local kitchen where the menu shifts with the season, so no two visits match. It's a Temescal institution, walk-ins only, dinner nightly. Grab a patio seat and let them decide. @pizzaiolooakland

Bakesale Betty — 5098 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The buttermilk fried chicken sandwich piled with jalapeno slaw is the East Bay lunch people plan their whole day around, and yes, there's a line. Open Thursday through Sunday only, so mark the calendar before the craving hits.

Curbside Creamery — 482 49th St, Oakland. Duck into Temescal Alley and this is the tiny parlor scooping house-made ice cream and fresh waffle cones, with cashew and coconut vegan options for the table that can't agree. The ice cream sandwich is the move. Open late nightly. @curbsidecreamery

Womb House Books — 470 49th St, Oakland. An inclusive feminist bookshop tucked in the alley, stacked with vintage first editions and a book club worth joining. Browse the plotless-fiction shelf, then the well-worn author hats. The kind of local shop that makes a neighborhood feel established. @wombhousebooks

Mira Flores — 486 49th St, Oakland. An Oakland embroidery label and tailor shop in the alley, designing workwear made in Peru and housing local vintage vendors under one roof. Bring a jacket and they will chain-stitch it on the spot. Closed Monday and Tuesday, so plan the stroll. @shopmiraflores

Eight for a Temescal afternoon: beer garden, Burmese classics, croissants, wood-fired pizza, that fried chicken sandwich, alley ice cream, a feminist bookshelf, and custom stitching, all on foot in a few Oakland blocks. Which stop starts your walk?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: Uptown Oakland
item.description: Eight Uptown Oakland spots inside a few walkable blocks, all under the Fox marquee where the East Bay comes to eat and stay out late. This Bay Area corrido
item.content:encoded:
Uptown Oakland

Eight Uptown Oakland spots inside a few walkable blocks, all under the Fox marquee where the East Bay comes to eat and stay out late. This Bay Area corridor along Telegraph and Broadway lets you park once and hit dinner, a show, and a nightcap on foot. Here's the local run.

Fox Theater — 1807 Telegraph Avenue, Oakland. The 1928 movie palace reopened in 2009 and now anchors the whole corridor, its glowing sign visible for blocks. Touring acts pack the 2,800-capacity room most nights, and the marquee alone is worth the walk over. Check the calendar before your crew picks a date. @foxoakland

Cafe Van Kleef — 1621 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The Uptown original, packed to the rafters with oddball art and lit by chandeliers, pouring its fresh-squeezed Greyhound with a cartoon-sized grapefruit slice. Live music on weekends, no cover, and the kind of room where strangers end up talking. Grab a stool early. @cafevankleef

Bar Shiru — 1611 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Right next door, the Bay Area's first hi-fi listening bar spins jazz and soul on vinyl, whole albums start to finish, through a wall of audiophile speakers. Craft cocktails, a deep Japanese whisky list, groups of six or fewer so the room stays calm. Come for the slow listen. @barshiruoakland

Make Westing — 1741 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Cavernous cocktail hall with an indoor bocce court, so your night has a built-in activity when conversation stalls. Happy hour runs 4 to 6 every day including weekends, the kitchen stays open late, and there's room for the whole group. Reserve a lane if you're rolling deep.

Itani Ramen — 1736 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Chef Kyle Itani's izakaya has been slinging bowls on this block for a decade, open till 9 most nights for a pre-show bowl or a late one after. Steamy, unfussy, and the kind of place regulars default to. Grab the Genki Room if your group runs big. @itaniramen

Aburaya — 362 17th Street, Oakland. Japanese fried chicken done loud, shio koji-marinated thighs fried crisp in potato starch, cold beer, and punk rock on the speakers since 2014. The whole kitchen is gluten-free with a stack of vegan options, so the picky friend has no excuse. Order the sando and the tots. @aburayaoakland

Alma Bar Cocina — 361 19th Street, Oakland. Small counter spot turning out street-style tacos at four bucks a piece, carne asada to pescado, with pozole verde on the board. Open late Thursday and Friday. That makes it a clutch stop after a show at the Fox. Split a few and add a super burrito. @almabarcocina

Modern Coffee — 381 19th Street, Oakland. The Leamington shop has poured quality coffee for the downtown crowd since 2009, with a pastry case worth arriving hungry for. Weekday mornings only, so it's the move before a matinee or a walk down Broadway. Established, unpretentious, exactly what a corridor needs. @moderncoffee

Eight for an Uptown Oakland night: Fox Theater, Cafe Van Kleef, Bar Shiru, Make Westing, Itani Ramen, Aburaya, Alma Bar Cocina, Modern Coffee. Dinner, a show, a nightcap, all walkable in one East Bay corridor. Which block do you start on?

item.title: East Bay Downtown Fremont, Capitol Avenue
item.description: Eight walkable stops on Capitol Ave, downtown Fremont, and most of the East Bay drives past it for a mall parking lot. The new downtown grew up around the
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Fremont, Capitol Avenue

Eight walkable stops on Capitol Ave, downtown Fremont, and most of the East Bay drives past it for a mall parking lot. The new downtown grew up around the event plaza, and the food quietly got good. Start at one end, work the block.

SLIVER Pizzeria — 3658 Capitol Ave, Fremont. Sourdough-crust pizza with a pie of the day that changes daily, so your usual order is a moving target. The Berkeley transplant that fits the walkable downtown. Grab a slice and eat it out on the plaza.

Honest Indian Vegetarian — 3658 Capitol Ave, Fremont. Mumbai street food, bhaji pav mopped up with buttery pav and a tawa pulav that earns the hype. All vegetarian, and the chaat counter is where regulars park. Come hungry, the portions do not apologize.

Din Ding Dumpling House — 3768 Capitol Ave, Fremont. Handmade xiao long bao and braised rib chop noodle in the Downtown Event Center plaza. Watch the crew fold soup dumplings through the window while you wait. That's its own dinner theater. @dindingdumplingbayarea

RAW Superfood Cafe — 3768 Capitol Ave, Fremont. Plant-based acai bowls, matcha, and a banh mi sando two doors from the dumplings, so the whole plaza turns into a meal crawl. The move when someone in the group swore off the fried stuff. @raw.superfoodcafe

Pour Decisions Craft — 3530 Beacon Ave, Fremont. Craft coffee and craft beer under one roof, open at 7am, with Vietnamese phin, matcha, and a rotating wall of local taps. One of the few spots you can get a good beer with breakfast and nobody blinks. @pourdecisionscraft

Ristorante il Porcino — 3339 Walnut Ave, Fremont. The old-guard Italian a block off Capitol, over 30 years in and still packed for the rack of lamb and the pasta. White tablecloths without the attitude, the established date-night anchor downtown. Book ahead on weekends.

Miga — 39033 State St, Fremont. Small Korean kitchen on State Street doing hot soups and cold noodles at a fair price, closed Sundays so plan around it. The walkable downtown pick when the group wants comfort food and no fuss. Low-key, cash-friendly, worth the wait.

Cakes and Bakes — 3143 Walnut Ave, Fremont. The Fremont branch of the Indian bakery for black forest pastry, butterscotch ice cream, and a cake counter that handles every birthday on the block. Dessert to close the crawl, or the reason you skip dinner and come straight here.

Eight for a downtown that stopped needing a bridge: SLIVER, Honest Indian, Din Ding, RAW, Pour Decisions, il Porcino, Miga, Cakes and Bakes. All walkable on and around Capitol Ave. Which end of the block are you starting on?

item.title: Oakland Chinatown
item.description: Eight Oakland Chinatown spots worth the walk, and not one sits across a bridge. Most of the Bay races to SF's Chinatown and forgets the East Bay grew its o
item.content:encoded:
Oakland Chinatown

Eight Oakland Chinatown spots worth the walk, and not one sits across a bridge. Most of the Bay races to SF's Chinatown and forgets the East Bay grew its own around 8th and Webster, blocks of dumpling houses, Hong Kong cafes, and bakeries that have fed regulars for decades. Park once and eat your way down the street.

Ying Kee Restaurant — 387 9th St, Oakland. A generation-old Cantonese room where the dumplings and wontons are folded by hand in small batches all day, nothing pre-mixed. Come for a hot bowl of noodle soup when the fog follows you across the bridge. The kind of steady corner spot a neighborhood keeps for a reason.

Ming's Tasty — 940 Webster St, Oakland. Dim sum without the rolling-cart chaos, order the turnip cake and the clay pot rice with preserved pork crisping at the bottom. Regulars swear it beats the big banquet halls for a fraction of the fuss. One catch, they close Wednesdays, so plan the craving around it.

Imperial Soup — 723 Webster St, Oakland. A one-of-a-kind spot built around slow-steamed Chinese soups, the kind Cantonese grandmothers swear will fix whatever ails you, rotated by the season. Get a medicinal soup with a rice plate and you have the most quietly restorative lunch in the neighborhood. Come hungry, leave convinced.

Chuan Yu — 388 9th St, Oakland. Tucked in the Pacific Renaissance Plaza, this is where you go when the craving is numbing, tongue-tingling Sichuan, not gentle Cantonese. Mala everything, and plenty of it. First-timers, ask for medium heat, the kitchen's idea of spicy runs a few notches past yours.

Ruby King Bakery — 718 Franklin St, Oakland. The glass case runs on Chinatown time, come early for the best picking, because by mid-afternoon the egg tarts and BBQ pork buns start vanishing. Grab a paper tray, point at what looks good, and walk out for pocket change. A morning ritual the whole block quietly shares.

Wonder Food Bakery — 340 9th St, Oakland. Baking Hong Kong style buns and pastries since 2001, over sixty items on a good day, with the crowd favorites marked by a little yellow star on the menu. Cocktail buns, pineapple buns, cocktail buns again because you'll want two. Cash-friendly and fast. @wonderfoodbakery

UC Dessert — 388 9th St, Oakland. Back in the Pacific Renaissance Plaza, this is the sit-down move for Hong Kong style dessert, mango sago, tofu pudding, black sesame soup, and milk tea done properly. The name comes from the idea that something beautiful makes you forget the day's stress. A sweet full stop on the walk. @ucdessert

Shooting Star Cafe — 1022 Webster St, Oakland. Your all-day, nearly all-night Hong Kong cafe, open to midnight for baked pork chop rice, milk tea, egg puffs, and snow ice when the sweet tooth strikes late. The menu is a novel, the portions are generous, and nobody rushes you out. The neighborhood's living room with a kitchen attached.

Eight for a Chinatown crawl you can do on foot: Ying Kee, Ming's Tasty, Imperial Soup, Chuan Yu, Ruby King, Wonder Food, UC Dessert, Shooting Star. Bakeries by morning, soups by noon, dessert whenever. Which corner do you start with?

item.title: East Bay Downtown Benicia, First Street
item.description: Eight First Street stops, and the whole strip runs downhill to the Carquinez Strait. Most Bay Area day-trippers blow past the 780 exit chasing Napa and ski
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Downtown Benicia, First Street

Eight First Street stops, and the whole strip runs downhill to the Carquinez Strait. Most Bay Area day-trippers blow past the 780 exit chasing Napa and skip the North Bay town with the walkable waterfront downtown. Benicia, from the top of the hill to the marina.

One House Bakery — 918 First Street, Benicia. The spot that put this town on the pastry map, a family operation turning out sourdough and those showpiece bread sculptures people drive in for. Get there early on a weekend or the good stuff is gone by ten. @onehousebakery

The Rellik Tavern — 726 First Street, Benicia. Craft cocktails, local micro-brews and a deep wine list in a room that has anchored this block since 2009. Live music most nights, and the name is Killer spelled backward if you look twice. @relliktavern

First Street Taphouse — 440 First Street, Benicia. Mare Island Brewing's downtown outpost, pouring their own beer with cocktails on tap and trivia every Tuesday. The old ferry-town brewery finally planted a flag on this side of the strait. @mareislandbrewing_firststreet

Lucca Bar and Grill — 439 First Street, Benicia. Gastropub burgers, a lively bar and a back beer garden that earns its keep once the fog burns off. Named Benicia's business of the year in 2025, so the locals clearly agree. @luccabarandgrill

Drift Benicia — 366 First Street, Benicia. A European-style cafe pulling Oakland's Mr. Espresso in the morning and slinging Roman-style pizza by the slice with beer and wine after eleven. Coffee, then a slab of focaccia, then the nap you earned. @driftbenicia

Baxters Restaurant and Bar — 280 First Street, Benicia. Beef Wellington and scallops in a proper white-tablecloth room, with a hidden piano speakeasy tucked in the back. This is the one you book when the occasion needs a little theater. @baxters.restaurant

Bella Siena — 127 First Street, Benicia. Modern Italian-American with windows so big every table turns into a lookout over the water. Locals call it the nicest seat downtown, and the eggplant parm backs the claim up. @bellasienarestaurant

Sailor Jack's — 123 First Street, Benicia. The marina-end anchor, seafood with a California turn inside an 1868 sea captain's house right over the Carquinez Strait. Oyster Mondays and two floors of water views, the last stop before your feet hit the dock. @sailorjacks_benicia

Eight for a full First Street crawl: pastry at One House, drinks at Rellik and the Taphouse, dinner at Baxters or Bella Siena, and Sailor Jack's where the street meets the strait. Which end of Benicia do you start from, top of the hill or the water?

item.title: Oakland Rockridge, College Avenue
item.description: Eight stops on College Avenue, the Rockridge stretch of Oakland most people ride the BART straight past. You can walk the whole run in about fifteen minute
item.content:encoded:
Oakland Rockridge, College Avenue

Eight stops on College Avenue, the Rockridge stretch of Oakland most people ride the BART straight past. You can walk the whole run in about fifteen minutes and eat, read, and shop your way from a candlelit French bar to a 1987 market hall without once moving your car. Start here.

A Cote — 5478 College Ave, Oakland. A candlelit Provencal small-plates room that has fed Rockridge since 2000, best known for mussels in Pernod and a wine list built for grazing. Come with three friends, order nine plates, argue over the last one. @acoterestaurant

Pegasus Books — 5560 College Ave, Oakland. A new-and-used bookshop that has held this corner since 1971, with a card and blank-book selection locals will tell you is the best in the East Bay. The kind of place you duck into for one thing and leave forty minutes later with four. @pegasusbooks

Belly — 5634 College Ave, Oakland. An Asian-Mexican kitchen whose breakfast burrito tucks tater tots inside for crunch and chipotle aioli for smoke, and this Rockridge counter is now its only location. Order it wrapped to go and eat it on the walk to BART.

Rockridge Market Hall — 5655 College Ave, Oakland. A European-style food hall open since 1987, nine shops under one roof: a fishmonger, a butcher, a cheese counter, a flower stall, a bakery, and Highwire coffee. You can build a whole dinner run without stepping back outside. @markethallfoods

Zachary's Chicago Pizza — 5801 College Ave, Oakland. The employee-owned deep-dish institution that has pulled weekend lines out the door for over forty years, stuffed pies so deep you eat one with a fork. Put your name in, walk the block, come back when it buzzes. @zacharyspizza

Ramen Shop — 5812 College Ave, Oakland. Three Chez Panisse alums turned this narrow room into one of the Bay Area's best bowls, broth and noodles made in house and produce that shifts with the season. Sit at the bar, watch the pass, order whatever special they push. @ramenshopoakland

Cole Coffee — 6255 College Ave, Oakland. A tiny roaster anchoring the College and 63rd corner since 2005, no laptops encouraged, regulars stacked two deep for the drip. Grab a cup, take the outdoor bench, watch the whole neighborhood walk by. @colecoffeeinc

La Farine — 6323 College Ave, Oakland. A French boulangerie on the upper end of College that locals line up at for the morning bun, a caramel-crackled spiral worth beating the crowd for. Get there early; the good pastries go by mid-morning. @lafarinebakery

Eight stops, one walkable stretch of Oakland's Rockridge: A Cote, Pegasus Books, Belly, Rockridge Market Hall, Zachary's, Ramen Shop, Cole Coffee, La Farine. Coffee to deep dish to a bag of books, all without moving your car. Which corner do you start on?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.
